a168f06b-94e4-40b4-a431-a1b39d0ca5b2: One purpose of art is to support and communicate political messages. Using color, letters, and shapes, Patricia Guthrie’s abstract quilts deliver political messages relating to the government, international relationships, and global warming. She creates artwork using cotton fabric, wool batting, dyes, and machine stitching. Bio: After retiring as a professor and department chair of Human Development and Women’s Studies at California State University East Bay, Patricia Guthrie decided to actively engage in the visual arts. She began taking community-based art classes: drawing, photography, quilt making, and printing on fabric. Quilt making and all its aspects has become her passion. Guthrie hopes her quilts encourage viewers to move beyond art that is merely pleasing to the eye to seek a deeper meaning. Her work has been shown nationally and internationally including Schweinfurth Memorial, Art Center, Auburn, New York; International Quilt Museum, Lincoln, Nebraska; Philadelphia Museum of Art, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Tuch + Technik Museum, Neumunster, Germany. This is Guthrie’s second solo show at Mercury 20 Gallery. 19496588-a6e3-57d9-b614-48b86f5b301d: 250 Years, Indigenous Futures Presented By Haines Gallery As the U.S. marks its 250th anniversary, Haines Gallery presents 250 Years, Indigenous Futures , a group exhibition centering the work of leading Native American artists. While occasioned by this anniversary, 250 Years, Indigenous Futures does not commemorate it. ABOVE: Haines Gallery is in Building C (far right). TOP OF PAGE: Bra d Kahlhamer , “ Pima Air + Space , ” 2025 (detail). Acrylic, ink, pencil on bedsheet, 69.25 x 53.5 inches, framed. Courtesy of the artist and Haines Gallery, San Francisco. Photo: Shaun Roberts EVENT DETAILS 250 Years, Indigenous Futures takes its title from the writings of Standing Rock Sioux historian Philip J. Deloria and his colleagues, who argue that Native peoples should be understood not primarily through the past, but “through the lens of futurity.” Indigenous knowledge, they write, is not peripheral to contemporary life but generative of new ways of understanding it. In this spirit, the exhibition considers Native presence and creativity as powerful forces shaping our collective future. The artists in the exhibition are: Victoria Grace Canby (Diné [Navaho]); Jordan Ann Craig (Northern Cheyenne); Sky Hopinka (Ho-Chunk Nation / Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians); Brad Kahlhamer (Indigenous ancestry); Terran Last Gun (Piikani / Blackfoot); Jamie Okuma (Luiseño, Shoshone-Bannock, Wailaki, Okinawan, and La Jolla); Wendy Red Star (Apsáalooke [Crow]); and Keith Secola (Northern Ute / Anishinaabe). Working across painting, drawing, sculpture, film, and photography, these artists engage contemporary culture, Nation-specific visual traditions, and personal histories in distinct and expansive ways. Rather than commemorating the 250th U.S. anniversary, the exhibition recognizes 1776 as only one moment within much longer histories of Indigenous presence, adaptation, and sovereignty. Creating space for artists to define their own terms of engagement, the exhibition aims to bring forward concerns central to their practices. The works on view draw inspiration from a vivid range of sources: boldly painted Piikani lodges; the precise geometry of Northern Cheyenne beadwork; the Indians of All Tribes’ occupation of Alcatraz; cars adorned with blankets and regalia for the annual Crow Fair; blood-soaked horror films; and archival photographs whose subjects meet the visitor’s gaze. The exhibition is informed by Apsáalooke artist Wendy Red Star’s caution against a “foe-based” framing of Native art – one that risks tethering meaning to resistance alone and obscuring the specificity of Nations, histories, and individual practices. Here, each artist’s work emerges from particular relationships to language, land, and material culture. No single framework can contain these worlds. About the Artists Victoria Grace Canby (Diné, b. 1978, Albuquerque, NM). Marin-based artist Victoria Grace Canby’s new works on paper, created for the exhibition, depict the Three Sisters – corn, beans, and squash – as a living model of resilience, healing, and collective care that connects Indigenous Peoples throughout the Americas. “Through fostering our connection to these plants’ powers,” Canby notes, “we can overcome the impacts of colonization.” Jordan Ann Craig (Northern Cheyenne, b. 1992, San Jose, CA). Jordan Ann Craig’s paintings draw from references ranging from Northern Cheyenne beadwork and quillwork to the postwar abstraction of Agnes Martin, all of which she translates into exacting, poetic fields of color and form. In works such as “ Miss Your Musk ” (2024), Craig foregrounds Indigenous abstraction as a living and evolving practice – one capable of holding personal narrative, formal experimentation, and cultural continuity without being reduced to any single source or meaning. Sky Hopinka (Ho-Chunk Nation/Pechanga Band of Luiseño Indians; b. 1984, Ferndale, WA). Sky Hopinka’s film Sunflower Siege Engine (2022) brings together distinct Indigenous sites and histories, connecting the Indians of All Tribes’ occupation of nearby Alcatraz Island (1969–1971) with Illinois’ Cahokia Mounds , one of the largest pre-contact urban centers in North America and a site from which ancestral remains continue to be repatriated. Brad Kahlhamer (Native American ancestry; b. 1956, Tucson, AZ). Painted in acrylic, ink, and pencil on a bedsheet, “ Pima Air + Space ” (2025) belongs to Kahlhamer’s recent “dream sheet” paintings. Its title recalls Arizona’s Pima Air & Space Museum, while birds, horses, masked figures, and a spectral presence drift through an aurora borealis of saturated color. Terran Last Gun , Saakwaynaamah’kaa (Last Gun) (Piikani / Blackfoot; b. 1989, Browning, MT on the Blackfeet Nation Reservation). Inspired by the bold geometric designs of Piikani painted lodges, Terran Last Gun has created a suite of works for the exhibition: precise compositions on vintage ledger paper that bring ancestral forms, colonial records, and the ongoing vitality of Indigenous abstraction into charged relation. Jamie Okuma (Luiseño, Shoshone-Bannock, Wailaki, Okinawan, and La Jolla; b. 1977, Glendale, CA). In “Of Love and Sacrifice: Motherhood” (2026), Jamie Okuma deploys her signature single-stitch beadwork to transform a brain-tanned deerskin handbag into a dazzling portrayal of two figures from Luca Guadagnino’s horror film Suspiria (2018). Drawing bracing cinematic imagery into dialogue with exacting Payómkawichum (Luiseño) beadwork techniques, Okuma conjures the selfless and steadfast power of maternal love. Wendy Red Star (Apsáalooke; b. 1981, Billings, MT). Wendy Red Star’s works from “ The (HUD) ” series focus on the colorful facades of houses built through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development on Montana’s Apsáalooke (Crow) reservation, where the artist was raised. Though their hues were chosen not by residents but by a government agency, Red Star’s images reveal signs of domestic beauty that exceed the mandates of bureaucracy. Keith Secola (Northern Ute / Anishinaabe; b. 1988, Randlett, UT on the Uintah and Ouray Reservation) Keith Secola screen-prints archival portraits of Native Americans onto the covers of vintage books, placing Indigenous presence in direct tension with exclusionary narratives of America’s past. Secola’s images depict subjects who often look directly back at the camera, meeting its gaze with a quiet intensity that transcends time and negates erasure. 298500a8-b54c-5d87-863c-e580a268bce6: Soulful flow is a robust vinyasa yoga class that brings balance to the body, mind and spirit. Anne-René has always been drawn to the spiritual side of life and yoga. This influences her movement meditations that are physically challenging and inspiring to the heart. Her class intertwines asana, breath, awareness, attention to transition and experiencing a personal connection to the movement that opens the door for a meditative flow to wake you up. Hand mudras, chanting, inspired readings, and music are incorporated into the class. About the teacher: Anne-René is a dance artist, Alexander Technique teacher and the artistic director of Sculpted Motion. She began her yoga studies back in New York City in the 1990's. In 2008 she received her Vinyasa yoga teaching certification from the White Lotus Foundation. She is inspired and influenced by her many teachers and studios: Ty Landrum, Sara Baird, Erin Dudley, Keith Borden, Cindi Lee's Om Yoga Center, Laughing Lotus Yoga, and the anatomical teachings of Irene Dowd and Leslie Kaminoff. Other influences are Krishnamurti, Ram Das, Kundalini yoga, Gaga, and Gyrotonic. "I have always expressed myself through movement. I find inspiration in watching the sky, feeling the sun on my skin and the wonderment of the night sky. Trees are amazing, animals are graceful, poetry can bring me to my knees. I find comfort in the resiliency of the human spirit and kind words from my friends. There is a fullness and flow to life that I know exist and I find comfort in knowing that I am a work in progress flowing toward it."

Scott Traffas has spent decades exploring the various exoteric and esoteric traditions of the East and West. What will be discussed at this session...? 0f16c633-93c1-4fbc-add9-b1b51b94a519: An intimate examination of Oscar Award-winning film and stage actress Geraldine Page, written with compassion and honesty by her only daughter, Angelica Page. Bountiful: Growing up with Geraldine Page is the first book about legendary screen and stage actress Geraldine Page, presenting a one-of-a-kind look at her body of work and private life. Includes insider stories of her stage and film career (nominated for four Tony Awards and eight Academy Awards, Oscar winner for The Trip to Bountiful ), her relationships with other renowned actors including her husband and Angelica’s father Rip Torn, Actors Studio founder Lee Strasberg, and her interactions with other legends including James Dean, John Wayne, Jackie Kennedy, and many more. Angelica Page, daughter of Geraldine and Rip Torn, skillfully weaves in stories of her own coming of age: being mesmerized by her mother’s stage performances as a child and a rebellious young adult; learning to swim in Grace Slick’s guitar-shaped pool; enduring a chaotic home life, immersing herself in the 1970s and 80s NYC underground of CBGBs, Max’s Kansas City, and the Mudd Club. This is as much a theatrical history lesson as a first-person survival guide to life in the fast lane. A love song sung by the daughter of a remarkable artist who should not be forgotten any time soon. Includes more than 40 rare photos from family archives. “A definitive memoir by a brilliant actress about a truly beloved American actress, mother and hero.” —Elizabeth Ashley, actor “Supercharged with boundless talent, emotion and at times unrequited love, Angelica Page’s portrait of the great Geraldine is one for the ages.” —Sandra Bernhard, actress “Be warned, this book is dangerous; it can make you regret never having lived through the thrilling, dangerous times Geraldine Page lived in and partly created. In these trying times, she is an important reminder of the potential of the individual, in art and in life.” —F. Murray Abraham, actor Angelica Page is an American actress, director, producer, and writer and the only daughter of legendary actors Rip Torn and Geraldine Page. She has appeared frequently onstage on- and off-Broadway, earning an Outer Critic’s Circle nomination for best Solo Performance, the Helen Hayes Award for Best Actress, and the New York People’s Choice Award for Best Supporting Actress. She is the creator of the critically acclaimed one-woman show Turning Page on which Bountiful is based. When not touring the US, she lives in Mexico. The Flour Craft Bakery & Cafe Cookbook empowers readers with simple and approachable recipes for mouthwatering cakes and cookies, pastry and savory bakes, everyday treats and holiday centerpieces, plus fresh salads and soups--all naturally gluten free. 75+ recipes cover breakfast, brunch, lunch, teatime, and dessert, from coffee cakes to focaccia, scones to tartines. bb8d1547-a600-4be5-852a-d1256b9359ef: Inspired by Where We Made Room , this workshop sends you out into the Castro for a walking and blind contour drawing session, capturing the buildings and streets that have held queer life for generations. Back at the museum, we'll trace those sketches onto transparency paper to create negatives, then head outside again to turn them into cyanotype prints using sun print paper—letting the sun fix your drawings into deep Prussian blue. Just as Landeta's silks layer archival exteriors with imagined interiors to blur document and dream, your prints will hold both what's actually there on the block and the loose, intuitive line your hand found along the way. No drawing experience necessary, all materials provided. Wear shoes ready for a walk. *Due to the materials cost for this event, GLBT Historical Society Members are limited for one (1) free ticket to this program. INSTRUCTOR Photo: Jasmine Singh Rosado Aleo Landeta (they/them) is is a trans and Latine visual artist and educator based in Oakland whose practice spans drawing, painting, installation, and public programming. 91823464-fd34-5285-8849-df369498c610: Whether or not you like monsters, one has to admit, most of us like a good scare now and then. The word Monster derives from the Latin monstrum, itself derived ultimately from the verb moneo (“to remind, warn, instruct, or foretell”). From this vantage point, monsters take on a new inspiring role, not to just scare us, but to inform us. So what can monsters teach us about our fears, our society and beyond? The Tiny Monster Show explores our fears so we can take a deeper look at what we’ve been suppressing and what we need to confront. From classical to political, The Tiny Monster Show gives space to capture, reveal, and maybe conquer those elements that keep us frozen in fear and hopefully shine a light on what it means to be human. Hopefully, you’ll experience a moment of laughter in recognition that you are more powerful than the monster wants you to think.

6f0fb18e-a112-4a38-9235-619c51f01a6c: “My purpose in writing this book is not only to teach you what high sensitivity is—because it’s so much more than what people assume—but also to show you that, contrary to what you may have thought, this trait can be an immense gift. Highly sensitive people are the emotional leaders, healers, problem solvers, and changemakers of the world.” — Excerpted from BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY by April Snow, LMFT In BIG FEELINGS, BIG JOY: The Essential Practices to Reclaim Your Strengths as a Highly Sensitive Person , licensed psychotherapist and sensitivity expert April Snow delivers a practical and empowering toolkit for Highly Sensitive People (HSPs) to embrace their sensitivity and chart their own path to joy. Drawing from her clinical experience with thousands of HSPs and her own life as a highly sensitive person, Snow makes it clear that sensitivity is a core part of who you are—something to value and nurture, not change. Tend to your nervous system: Practice easy strategies to manage overstimulation, navigate emotional lows, and regain a sense of calm and clarity. Set boundaries with compassion: Gain tools for advocating for your needs in relationships, work, and daily interactions—so you can protect your energy without guilt. Embrace sensitivity as your strength: Experience how sensitivity can fuel creativity, intuition, deep empathy, and meaningful connections. With this book, April Snow encourages readers to confidently honor their needs, celebrate their sensitivity, and build a life that reflects their true selves—full of joy, balance, and deeper connection. Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! is a journey into the complicated, surprising, and often intimate connections between humans and wild animals. From close encounters in the field to quieter moments of recognition, these essays explore what draws us to the wild—and what happens when habitat recedes. Hunt for renegade she-lizards in the Chiricahua Wilderness Learn about the “Dogs Saving Cats” program to help save cheetahs Track Namibia’s rare black rhino—and learn why “dehorning” backfired By turns curious, funny, and deeply felt, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You! explores connection, responsibility, and the enduring allure of the wild. She is your pal, your sister, your shadow-person who does the adventure with you and then says just the thing you wish you'd said." -Allen Fish, Director, Golden Gate Raptor Obvservatory "King's powerful piece on saving wild elephants is a moment you should not miss-even if it hurts." -Natalie Lefevre, Editor, Ethical Traveler Laurie McAndish King is an award-winning writer whose subjects include a one-legged toucan, an elephant orphanage, the alleged medicinal qualities of rhino horn, and the basics of eagle sex. King’s essays and photography have appeared in Smithsonian magazine, the Washington Post , the San Francisco Chronicle Magazine , Travelers’ Tales’ The Best Women’s Travel Writing , Lonely Planet’s The Kindness of Strangers , and other magazines and literary anthologies. King’s three books of travel stories—insightful, poignant and often quite funny—are celebrated for the way they inspire and entertain readers. Her latest book, Wild Thing, I Think I Love You: Curious Encounters with Wildlife around the World , is due out in September, 2026. 53c96efa-c0e1-4d6c-ac02-b80c7c155130: Laura Malone, Carnivale, Oil on Linen, 60” x 48”, 2021, Photo courtesy of the artist Present Figures brings together five California painters whose works exist within the figurative language of portraiture, simultaneously expanding and disrupting it. Centered around themes of intimacy, boundaries, and embodied emotion, each artist takes an individual approach to media, scale, and the capacity of the human form to be both a site of identity and a vessel of metaphor. Engaging in profound considerations of what it is to be human—our physicality, sense of self, relationships, consciousness, and creativity, these artists invite us to engage with these shifting, eternal questions and reflect on our own experiences—be they practical, peaceful, disturbing, humorous, fragmented, spiritual, or otherworldly. As individuals, choices that begin with who and what to portray later manifest in stylistic and material communiquès that boldly and poetically reveal themselves to the world. Collectively, the psychologically charged spectrum of the group reminds us of the myriad ways our sentience can be narrated. Like Anais Nin said, “We don’t see things as they are, we see them as we are.” Bio: With Present Figures, Laura Malone expands her practice to curation. Malone invited four artists to show alongside her, chosen for their unique and diverse approaches to representing the figure: two Southern California artists — Cindy Craig and Shannon Rae Fincke — and two from the Bay Area — Nina Katz and Heidi Brueckner. Collectively their work has been shown across the globe in Europe, Asia, and the United States. Malone’s artwork was featured in The Crocker Kingsley National Art Competition and included in “Disrupted Realism,” juried by John Seed, who wrote the book of the same name. Malone currently resides in Oakland, CA and has been a member of Mercury 20 since 2023. 954025f2-829c-44e1-adc6-121d90f35f4a: Tara Esperanza, Guardians, 2026, acrylic-on-panel, 20” x 16”, Photo courtesy of the artist Whether painted in California or Oaxaca, the works in Close to Home begin with the same impulse: to slow down and look closely. Working on a more intimate scale than in her previous work, Tara Esperanza found herself drawn to quiet moments of observation, where familiar plants reveal unexpected beauty through color, form, and light. Created between two places that have become part of her life, these paintings are less about geography than about attention. Though rooted in different landscapes, each painting is shaped by the same curiosity and sense of wonder inspired by the resilience and sculptural elegance of plants. For many years, succulents have been Esperanza’s way of exploring themes of adaptation, diversity, and endurance. Through this body of work, the smaller scale invites viewers to slow down, look closely, and discover that what is closest to us often has the most to reveal. Bio: Tara Esperanza resides in Oakland, California, where succulents thrive year-round. When she is not painting, she enjoys running and capturing images that later inspire her work. Esperanza earned a BFA in Painting, graduating cum laude from the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, and studied plein air painting in Brittany, France. A representational painter inspired by nature, she has dedicated years to portraying the remarkable beauty and diversity of succulents. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery in Oakland, CA, since 2020. Her work has been shown at the Women’s United Art Movement Virtual Gallery, as well as numerous group exhibitions. In 2025, Esperanza received Best of Show at the Annual National Juried Painting Exhibition at Emerald Springs Art Center in Oregon. Her paintings have been featured in Create! Magazine, New Visionary Magazine, and other publications, and are held in private collections throughout the United States. It’s an all-out Emergency!!! THIS TIME IS DIFFERENT! This isn’t just a blurb – ask around. It’s time to get out of denial, stare down the grim reality, and… party ? There’s nothing like an encounter with a mysterious stranger at a party: take a risk, lay yourself bare, and – just maybe – find a tiny bit of hope and laughter amidst the chaos. And so many questions along the way! Starting with something safe… “Can we just not… like… talk about Fascism?” “Is the right to eat beef really in the 2nd Amendment? “ If you make it past the chit chat, the questions go deeper: “Maybe it’s time to drop the whole notion of Reality?” “Is it already too late?” And eventually… “Why the two of us, right here, right now?” “What’s next?” Paul Sussman’s latest creation tosses us into the center of the swirl, and offers us lifelines to laugh, to cry, to hope, and to act. “One of the most authentic presentations of humanity I’ve ever seen” “Paul has entered some other zone… of deep thoughtfulness and connection.” ” I laughed, I cried, and I left carrying so much to think about. The way you wove together themes of grief, anger, and how we’re all navigating this moment in time was powerful and deeply resonant.” “You have outdone yourself in this medium –your depth and candor, scope from the personal to the epochal, agile shifting from gentle or scathing satire to the existentially terrifying. I am stunned into silence pondering the implications you invite audiences to consider for this moment.” “You avoid easy answers and platitudes. The threats and the stakes in play have an urgency and brutality that you confront head on, with humility and honesty.” “I loved, loved, loved, your show. Such courageous saying out loud all the things we think, and in such a funny way. Thank you” “This show was so great — so of the moment, so hilarious and at moments horrific at once. Sussman has worked for over 40 years to champion affordable housing development in San Francisco and received the Catherine A. Baur Lifetime Achievement Award from the Non-Profit Housing Association of Northern California in 2017. Consumed by excruciating pain, she finds it impossible to imagine any future worth living. Until, on an ordinary trip to the grocery store, she hears The Voice. The trouble is, Susan doesn’t believe in Voices. And yet, when The Voice tells her to walk the Camino de Santiago in Spain, she obeys despite knowing nothing about this ancient pilgrimage. With only her pack and her pain, Susan begins a journey through unrelenting rain and temperatures that rarely get above 50 degrees. With the help of some improbable Spiritual Guides, a little bit of magic, and the Camino itself, Susan must face her past to have any hope of creating her future. Alone on stage, she becomes 23 characters to take the audience on her solitary walk through 540 miles of rain, resentment, and redemption. Buen Camino is a moving story about grief leading to surrender, and ultimately to freedom. A published writer, performer, and career consultant, Susan Edsall grew up in Montana and now lives in Kailua Kona, Hawaii. Author of the forthcoming novel Bitterroot , she has also written two memoirs, Into the Blue: A Father’s Flight and a Daughter’s Return and Saved . She premiered Buen Camino at the SOLO STARS Series in Los Angeles in December 2024, winning their Encore Award. Susan brought the show to United Solo on 42nd Street in New York City in March 2025 and the Hollywood Fringe Festival in June 2025. d43c0b61-90b3-413f-8261-6b5737072aa1: PALACE ARE BACK WITH “KID” AND MASSIVE TOUR OF USA + CANADA Palace have been making music together for over a decade. What started out as carefree jam sessions between Leo Wyndham, Rupert Turner and Matt Hodges in an airless studio in North London has burgeoned into a project that has amassed a global audience more akin to a community than a fanbase. Their early EPs - Lost In The Night (2014) and Chase The Light (2015) - were recorded in the band’s beloved aforementioned studio, The Arch, and established a DIY ethos that remains intrinsic to the spirit of the band to this day. Four albums followed; So Long Forever (2016), Life After (2019), Shoals (2022) and Ultrasound (2024): each one a musical exploration of a particular feeling in a particular place during a particular time; ranging from grief and the loss of a relationship to the emergence of new love and light. Consequently, it's not easy to sonically classify Palace. Their sound varies from the atmospheric and ethereal to the more grounded notes of Blues and Americana, yet in every song there is still something remarkably identifiable as Palace: an ineffability to the feelings conjured up by the music. In a word, transcendent. Perhaps it is this feeling of transcendence which resonates so deeply with their supporters; loyal fans who, by the time Palace had made their Coachella debut in 2024, welcomed them home to a sold-out show at London’s Hammersmith Apollo. In early 2025, Palace took a career leap that harkens back to their DIY origin. They released the Greyhound EP on their own label, Palace Presents - a collective they'd started in 2016 as a monthly night at The George Tavern in East London, which had quietly grown into something more intentional. A positive and protected space as Leo described it, away from the usual constraints of the music industry. The EP followed a sold-out run across the USA and Canada to growing crowds of dedicated fans. Kid was released in April 2026, together with the announcement of a 30 date tour of the USA and Canada in the Fall of 2026, culminating in a show at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. “Kid is about longing for a child an ocean away. It’s the ache we feel for our people when we’re separated from them. It doesn’t feel like a sadness or heaviness, but more an affirmation of that love, a primal release sung into the sunset as the road flies by." The journey from an airless studio in North London to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles is a long one, and by doing things their way, Palace have managed to arrive still recognisably, unmistakably themselves

62ef4371-b94b-4f6d-9761-ff23093a9752: To celebrate Thelonious Monk’s birthday — an SFJAZZ tradition — Marcus Shelby and his New Orchestra honor the large ensemble work of the iconoclasic jazz legend with special guests including pianist Cyrus Chestnut, saxophonist Sarah Hanahan, and vibraphonist Warren Wolf. Bassist, composer, arranger, educator and bandleader Marcus Shelby is a figure synonymous with Bay Area jazz and the spirit of collaboration. A recipient of the Charles Mingus Scholarship, Shelby attended Cal Arts and studied with Charlie Haden and James Newton while working simultaneously with the all-star jazz ensemble Black/Note, who released a series of highly regarded albums in the 1990s. Since moving to the Bay Area, he has led a highly regarded jazz orchestra and numerous small groups, with large-scale commissions focused on the history, present, and future of the African-American experience. On what would have been Monk’s 109th birthday, Shelby and his band evoke the spirit of the pianist’s 1959 classic The Thelonious Monk Orchestra at Town Hall and 1964’s Big Band and Quartet in Concert. Piano great and Monk disciple Cyrus Chestnut sits center stage, joined by Sarah Hanahan — a major new voice on saxophone — along with the SFJAZZ Collective’s Warren Wolf, who has a deep connection to Monk’s singular songbook. Personnel: Marcus Shelby (bass); Cyrus Chestnut (piano); Sarah Hanahan (tenor saxophone); Warren Wolf (vibraphone); Others TBA

5aaed545-d7ed-5251-8b03-4383ff894020: Emotional Surfing is a micro-meditation technique for working with emotional activation. When things get charged, when you're shutting down, reacting, or about to say something you'll regret, it gives you a way to stay grounded. You learn to bring presence and compassion into the moments that usually throw you off. You’ll get personalized guidance for where you uniquely get stuck, like personal training for your emotions. Relational Surfing is relational practice for pairs or groups that uses the present moment as its only material: what's happening inside you, right now, and what's happening between us. We're real with each other. Whatever patterns run your life, the places you go quiet, the ways you perform, the things you avoid, they'll show up in the room. It Is has its roots in Circling, Relatefulness and other authentic relating practices. What makes Relational Surfing distinct is its incorporation of Emotional Surfing micro-meditation and its inclusion of healing our wounding as an explicit goal of the practice. Developmental Friendship (or spiritual friendship) is a kind of friendship that supports our growth in multiple dimensions -- waking up to our essential nature, cleaning up our developmental wounding, growing up into mature human beings, and showing up in our communities. We've found that these two practices together form the cornerstone for strong developmental friendships that can massively accelerate our growth and support us through life's inevitable twists and turns. All levels welcome. No meditation or authentic relating experience required.

It is an ideal read for anyone interested in creating sacred spaces, garden sanctuaries, and connecting more deeply with nature. Create a garden that becomes a sanctuary for peace, reflection, and spiritual growth with this meditative guide to mindful gardening and sacred spaces. In Soulful Sanctuaries, Janaki Sandy Gaal—known as “The Rose Lady”—invites readers to reimagine gardens of any size as places of renewal, healing, and connection to the natural world. Blending practical gardening wisdom, meditative practices, and heartfelt storytelling, this richly photographed book offers a meaningful approach to cultivating an outdoor space that feels personal, restorative, and spiritually alive. Drawing on decades of experience as an organic gardener, garden designer, and consulting rosarian, Janaki shares guidance on organic gardening, year-round cultivation, and creating garden altars that reflect each reader’s own intentions and beliefs. Featuring photography by her daughter, Rebecca Gaal, Soulful Sanctuaries is both an inspiring guide and a keepsake gift book rooted in family, beauty, and spiritual practice. Here’s what makes Soulful Sanctuaries meaningful: • Mindful Gardening for Every Space: Helps readers turn gardens of any size into places to slow down, reconnect, and cultivate meaning. • Practical Organic Gardening Wisdom: Includes sustainable practices, year-round cultivation, and insights from Janaki’s experience as a consulting rosarian. • Spiritual Practices Made Personal: Offers meditative practices, intention-setting, and guidance for creating garden altars. • A Beautiful Keepsake Gift Book: Rebecca Gaal’s photography creates an immersive experience for gardeners, spiritual seekers, and anyone seeking a more restorative living space. Soulful Sanctuaries is a mindful gardening book and spiritual gardening guide for readers interested in sacred spaces, organic gardening, garden sanctuaries, meditation, and connecting more deeply with nature. Janaki Sandy Gaal is an author, educator, gardener, and longtime student of Ram Dass. Her reflections explore the connection between spirituality, nature, and everyday living. She knew from a young age that she wanted to relieve suffering, first as an ICU nurse and later by opening her garden to the public. She is an Organic gardener, Garden Designer, and Consulting Rosarian. She learned that helping others connect with the beauty of nature inspired an irreplaceable kind of joy. Through her writing and teaching, Janaki encourages readers to cultivate reflection, presence, and healing through simple daily practices, including gardening, cooking, and connecting with the natural world. She lives on the island of Maui in Hawaii surrounded by Ohana. Janaki Sandy Gaal - photo courtesy of the publicist Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage at our Corte Madera store. Immediately, her mental health improved, her attention span increased, and her curiosity returned. Since then, she has made it her mission to help others do the same. Every year, 10-year-old Meridian spends her summer with Grandpa Frank on Wide Eye Lake, where she helps out at his quirky museum dedicated to the mysterious Wide Eye monster. Hidden among the clutter are some old mementos that unlock a long-buried family secret—one that turns her entire world upside down. Not only does Meridian have a family mystery to solve, but this summer she has to avoid 2 prankster classmates who just so happen to be vacationing nearby. Summer at Wide Eye Lake really isn't turning out to be the magical escape it used to be. 59f4c774-a243-5209-887b-50e698d36ce7: Don't miss this extraordinary conversation with Academy Award-winning actor and producer Michael Douglas celebrating the release of his new memoir, One Helluva Ride . A signed bookplate edition of the book is included with each ticket. Beginning with his fractured childhood and a complex relationship with his superstar father, Kirk Douglas, Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of a remarkable life. One Helluva Ride reveals incredible behind-the-scenes stories featuring a Who’s Who of Hollywood, many of them never revealed before and some outrageously funny, with an unflinching honesty about his sometimes bad-boy life. Michael will be joined in conversation by Lance Gardner the executive artistic director at Marin Theatre Company in Mill Valley. More About One Helluva Ride Beginning with his fractured childhood and a complex relationship with his superstar father, Kirk Douglas, Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of a remarkable life. One Helluva Ride reveals incredible behind-the-scenes stories featuring a Who’s Who of Hollywood, many of them never revealed before and some outrageously funny, with an unflinching honesty about his sometimes bad-boy life. Initially dismissed as just the handsome son of a legendary movie star, at age thirty-one he shook up Hollywood when he won his first Oscar for producing the five-time Academy Award-winning classic film One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest. Told he would never be more than a “TV actor,” he quit the hit series The Streets of San Francisco to become an international movie star, with a list of classic films that have grossed billions of dollars, winning a second Oscar for his riveting performance as Gordon Gekko in Wall Street. “I can’t think about my life without thinking of my movies,” Douglas says, and he recounts his career through twelve of his most iconic films, including One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, The China Syndrome, Romancing the Stone, Jewel of the Nile, Fatal Attraction, Wall Street, War of the Roses, Basic Instinct, Falling Down, The American President, Traffic and Behind the Candelabra. These movies not only captured the cultural zeitgeist but often defined it. Yet as Douglas’s fame grew, so did his personal struggles. He recounts the full, unfiltered story of his turbulent first marriage; infidelity and affairs with some of the most beautiful actresses in Hollywood; his own serious struggle with alcohol, drugs and rehab; the heartbreaking fight to save his son from an addiction that sent him to prison; and his against-all-odds battle with stage IV cancer. He saw Catherine Zeta Jones on a movie screen and instantly fell for her. Their incredible love story transformed his life and proved all the tabloids wrong, enduring after twenty-five years of marriage. Father, son, husband, actor, producer, brother and friend. This is the real, raw, deeply honest and vulnerable Michael Douglas you didn’t know—until now. --- --- --- Michael Douglas is a legendary actor and producer. Throughout his career, he has received two Academy Awards, a BAFTA Award, five Golden Globe Awards, a Primetime Emmy Award, and two Screen Actors Guild Awards. He was honored with the AFI Lifetime Achievement Award in 2009, two Honorary Cesars in 1998 and 2016, a Film Society at Lincoln Center Gala Tribute in 2010, a Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award in 2004, and a Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018. Douglas has also served for twenty-seven years as a United Nations Messenger of Peace. LANCE GARDNER (Marin Theatre Company Executive Artistic Director) A familiar face in the San Francisco Bay Area theatre scene, Lance Gardner is an actor and producer born and raised in the Bay Area. He has earned dozens of theatre credits over the last 20 years, including six mainstage shows and a school tour at Marin Theatre. He has also performed in multiple shows at Berkeley Repertory Theatre, California Shakespeare Theater, Magic Theatre, TheatreWorks, and more recently served as the President of the Board of Aurora Theatre. He comes to Marin from KQED, where, as a live event producer, he helped launch KQED Live, a year-round, in-person and virtual events program where he crafted unique experiences marrying journalism, arts, and entertainment. Harnessing the power of public media, he created bespoke concerts, game shows, performances, food and dining events, interviews and more. His work has been featured on KQED TV and on the radio at KQED and KALW. Event details: This event will be hosted by Book Passage & Calvary Presbyterian at Calvary Presbyterian, SF. All tickets include a signed bookplate copy of One Helluva Ride . Lobby doors open at 3:00 pm / Open Seating Additional copies of One Helluva Ride will be available for purchase at the event.
6cd4056c-5662-485c-9e75-03aed860ef0e: A story of recovery, love, and loss—a memoir of healing ourselves and the natural world. Moving through the intensely personal and kindred terrain of love, recovery, and loss, An Armsfull of Birds is a climate memoir that tells the story of developing deeply held commitments to ourselves, to those we love, and ultimately to the ailing natural world. Cara will be joined in conversation by Neal Allen, a coach and co-author of the recent New York Times Bestseller Good Writing. Cara Benson did not come to love easy. As a low bottom addict, she crawled through subway tunnels and partnered with an abusive man. When she came face to face with her own death, she chose life. Her journey of survival led her into recovery, to climbing mountains, and ultimately to Jon, the man with whom she cultivated a relationship that began as “second chance lovers” and slowly developed into one as lifetime partners. Years later, Benson unexpectedly found herself in devastation as she came to terms with losing Jon to suicide. As she retreated into her grief, she also retreated into the woods of upstate New York, exploring the forests not as the avid hiker she’d become in recovery, but as a meanderer who had lost her way. Here she found more grief in her observation of the effects of climate change. In confronting her loss, Benson came to realize that the lessons she learned from loving Jon in sickness, health, and death could be applied to her relationship with the non-human world. From squirreling away oak acorns for reforestation of a logged property to maintaining feeders for the birds Jon adored, Benson’s daily life became a sort of field guide for how to live with a deep and abiding commitment to the future of the planet despite challenging odds. Moving through the intensely personal and kindred terrain of love, recovery, and loss, An Armsfull of Birds is a climate memoir that tells the story of developing deeply held commitments to ourselves, to those we love, and ultimately to the ailing natural world. “I opened it up to read the first few pages and then spent five hours reading the rest. Beautifully done. Poignant, human, authentic.” —Jenny Lawson, The Bloggess and #1 New York Times bestselling author of How To Be Okay When Nothing Is Okay "This is a book about many profound things, but one of them is healing, and in particular the healing possibilities of the physical world around us. Of course, as Benson recognizes, healing needs to—and can—go both ways. A valuable book!" —Bill McKibben, author of Here Comes the Sun “Cara Benson feels everything so deeply and tells her stories so honestly. Part recovery story, part eco-travelogue, part grief memoir, An Armsfull of Birds is a nuanced, thoughtful book about what it means to live fully, even when that means surviving your most beloved people. A memoir that will break your heart and put it back together again.” —Amy Shearn, award-winning author of Animal Instinct and Unseen City Cara Benson has been published in The New York Times, Boston Review, Orion, Sierra Magazine, The Brooklyn Rail, Los Angeles Review of Books , and selected for Best American Poetry . Her first book, a collection of prose poems called (made) , was well reviewed in The Huffington Post and The Brooklyn Rail , among other publications. She has received a New York Foundation for the Arts Fellowship and the bpNichol Award. Benson lives in a former church on the ancestral homelands of the Stockbridge-Munsee Band of Mohican Indians in upstate NY. An Armsfull of Birds: A Personal Field Guide to Love, Loss, and Commitment is her first memoir. Neal Allen is a coach and writer. He co-authored the recent New York Times Bestseller Good Writing: 36 Ways to Improve Your Sentences (Penguin Avery 2026) with his wife, Anne Lamott. In his private practice Neal draws from historical, psychological, and spiritual perspectives to design practical tools that aim toward freedom. A former journalist and corporate executive, he has written for newspapers, general interest magazines, and literary journals. Other books are Better Days: Tame Your Inner Critic (Namaste Books, 2023) and Shapes of Truth: Discover God Inside You (2021). Neal holds master’s degrees in Political Science and Eastern Classics. Anne and Neal live in Marin County. da8db867-f7db-495d-9ef2-1ea2198f870c: Join us at the Ferry Building for a meet-and-greet celebration of award-winning chef, author, television personality, and activist Melissa King to mark the release of her new memoir, The Girl Who Became King . This intimate, captivating, and heartfelt memoir explores family, food, and Melissa's journey to finding her voice as a queer Chinese American chef. Embracing my love of food has empowered me to embrace every layer of who I am: my Chinese heritage, my American upbringing, and all the parts of me that felt too much and not enough. When I chose myself, I set her free. Just me. The girl who became king. As a kid, Melissa King lived for the moment she would come from elementary school, grab her prized Chinese meat cleaver, and prepare dinner for her family. She already knew cooking was her future, but she didn’t know how hard she’d have to fight to make that dream a reality. Growing up, King felt like she was stuck in a box that was only getting smaller. Her Shanghainese and Cantonese immigrant parents had certain expectations—none of which included going to culinary school or falling in love with women. American culture also dictated that kitchens were a man’s world. But trying to live by these rules felt like no life at all. Determined to forge her own path, she fought her way into the demanding world of Michelin- starred kitchens, while discovering a home in the queer community. When she entered Top Chef as a reluctant contestant, inspired by her grandmother’s advice to follow her heart, she began embracing the flavors, culture, and parts of herself she had once forgotten. This journey of self- discovery through food leads her back to her parents, where love creates room for their strengths and imperfections. In this heartfelt memoir, Melissa King shows that empowerment comes from embracing all the different ingredients that make up who you are, and models the hard-won courage it takes to believe in yourself against the odds. “This book is not only a chronicle of humble beginnings and big dreams. It’s an immigrant story, a story of finding your particular identity as a queer woman and insisting on who you are while still holding grace for the imperfect people who love you. One can’t help but root and cheer for our Chef King.” —Padma Lakshmi, New York Times bestselling author of Love, Loss, and What We Ate “We have known and loved Melissa King, the chef, for years, but in this no-holds-barred memoir, we finally meet Melissa King, the person, with layers of heartbreak, fears, joys and triumphs that make her the singular force of nature that she is today. Essential reading for any modern-day foodie.” —Edward Lee, chef, finalist on Culinary Class Wars , and author of Bourbon Land “Melissa King had the courage to ignore just about everyone’s expectations for her—and thank goodness she did. This memoir is funny, honest, and full of heart, reminding us that belonging isn’t something you wait to be given.” —Atsuko Okatsuka “Melissa’s story is a powerful reminder that success comes not from fitting into someone else’s expectations, but from embracing your whole self.” —Chef Kwame Onwuachi “Melissa King may not be the tallest chef in the kitchen but her ambition, talents, and drive make her tower over her contemporaries.” —Chef Martin Yan, host of Yan Can Cook , bestselling author, and restaurateur “Melissa King’s memoir made me laugh with its familiarity. What impressed me most was how brave and not very Chinese she was in sharing her story with such truth and transparency. Her honesty and struggles touched my heart, as she will touch yours. I see you, Melissa.” —Ming-Na Wen, actress and author of Have You Eaten Yet? “As the daughter of immigrants, I recognized so much in her journey—the sacrifices of family, the ties that bind generations, the pull of two cultures, the pressure to succeed, and the challenge of finding your own voice. . . . Full of honesty, humor, and heart.” —Michelle Kwan “Written with the same confidence and precision that made Melissa King such a force in the kitchen . . . sharp, satisfying, and impossible to put down.” —Tegan Quin “What stayed with me is how honestly King traces her journey: the pressure, the contradictions, the quiet negotiations between who you’re expected to be and who you know you are. She’s telling the story of becoming. This book is a reminder that there’s no single way to do that.” —Jon M. Chu, director of Crazy Rich Asians and author of Viewfinder **** Melissa King is a James Beard Award-winning chef, author, and television personality. She is the author of the cookbook Cook Like a King: Recipes from My California Chinese Kitchen , which won the 2026 James Beard Award. She is the winner and fan favorite of Bravo’s Top Chef: All Stars L.A. and holds the record for the most challenge wins in the show’s history. Known for her modern California Chinese cuisine, she is a leading voice shaping conversations through food, cultural storytelling, and advocacy. A queer Shanghainese Cantonese American, she grew up in Los Angeles’s San Gabriel Valley. Her work has since taken her beyond the kitchen into television, fashion, and culture, including hosting Tasting Wild for National Geographic, curating the 2022 Met Gala menu, and being featured in global campaigns for Levi’s and GAP. 28ef01f3-fc82-4a68-92f8-a0f336302c5b: Elephant Gym successfully completed a world tour spanning 60 cities across 23 countries. However, behind this achievement lay an unseen crisis of disbandment, along with hidden conflicts and struggles. What does it truly mean to be a band? The film was first screened in October 2025 at the Kaohsiung Film Festival, one of Taiwan’s leading film festivals, and will also be shown in theaters in both Japan and Taiwan. While their world tour across 23 countries and 60 cities was a major success, the film reveals the untold story behind it—including a looming breakup crisis during its preparation, as well as the band’s internal conflicts and struggles. “If your dreams were to become reality, what price would you be willing to pay?“ Elephant Gym, an instrumental band from Kaohsiung, Taiwan, has been creating indie music since its formation in 2012. Their sound blends complex rhythms with irregular time signatures and sophisticated melodies. In Taiwan, their avant-garde musical style often raised the question: who would even listen to this? However, in 2024, they embarked on a world tour covering 23 countries and 60 shows, including three performances in the Philippines. They captivated audiences worldwide and firmly established their presence. Yet behind the glamorous stage, there were deep struggles. Between guitarist Tell Chang and bassist KT Chang—who are siblings—there were conflicts between family ties and band dynamics. Drummer Chia-Chin Tu had to make the difficult decision to leave another band. And just before the world tour, the band faced a crisis that nearly led to their breakup—filled with unseen pain and clashes. Still, they chose to believe in their music and in their bond, and continued moving forward. From a niche genre to the global stage, Elephant Gym asks through their musical journey: What is a band made of people with different backgrounds? What does it mean for people to connect? Between dreams and reality, they found their own “truth.” Come witness that answer in theaters. Band member Q&A (over Zoom) to follow the screening! 3f6e747c-a018-44fc-a26c-51ae30cb9a18: Please join us for a discussion with the author of No to Nuclear: Why Nuclear Power Destroys Lives, Derails Climate Progress and Provokes War . Linda Pentz Gunter and Eric Wolfe speak in conversation on Sunday, October 11th at 7 pm. Trump is pushing for nuclear power expansion, to enrich himself and his billionaire tech friends. But does anyone else really benefit? In No To Nuclea r, Pentz Gunter moves beyond the science and statistics, centering the stories of the Nuclear Age around the inherent colonialism and corruption of the nuclear industry and the Indigenous communities who have been preyed upon for profit and left to pay a terrible price. She takes us to Native American and First Nations communities, to the nomadic Tuareg of Niger and Aboriginal lands in Australia, where Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, far from the countries who profit, have been forced to mine the uranium that fuels the nuclear industry. She finds similar stories where atomic bombs have been tested, in the Marshall Islands and French Polynesia. And she reminds us that animals, who we disregard so cruelly, are harmed, too. Finally, the book urges us to rediscover the beauty and the miracle that is Planet Earth and to embrace justice first, if we are to have a chance to prevent the worst of the climate crisis and avoid nuclear war. Linda Pentz Gunter is the founder and executive director of the US-based non-profit Beyond Nuclear. She also created and writes for her organization's news platform, Beyond Nuclear International. A former full-time journalist, she continues to contribute feature stories to the Morning Star (UK) and Ralph Nader's Capitol Hill Citizen . Eric Wolfe has been active in peace, environment, and labor issues for 60 years. He helped organize the Clamshell Alliance in 1976 to oppose construction of the Seabrook reactors. Through his puppet show, Burnt Toast: Trouble in the Nation’s Breadbasket , he advocated for non-violent direct action against nuclear power in 20 states, including California. Acres of Clams , his feature-length documentary about the Clamshell Alliance, was released in 2024. Eric has lived in San Francisco since 1988 with his wife, science writer Susan Freinkel.
4b63d810-bc6a-5066-963d-86428283d352: In this immersive workshop, we explore the deeper esoteric meanings within the poetry of Indian mystic saints such as Kabir and Guru Nanak through the indigenous folk songs of the Malwa region of Central India. Priyal will guide us through this journey by singing and interpreting these songs while accompanying himself on traditional instruments like the Tambura and Kartaal. Printed translations will be provided, allowing participants to follow along and join in the singing if they wish. After each song, we will pause for reflection, creating space for participants to share whatever arises within them. We will also spend time in shared silence, gently turning inward to experience the stillness pointed to in the songs. Priyal will also share stories from the life of Kabir, insights into India’s oral traditions, and reflections on his own journey — how he encountered his Guru and how these teachings have shaped his life. Through song, storytelling, collective reflection, and silence, this workshop invites us to touch something deeper within ourselves — a space where boundaries soften, and a sense of oneness with each other and the world begins to emerge. About Priyal Maheshwari: Priyal Maheshwari is a musician and yoga teacher whose journey bridges the worlds of science, spirituality, and the arts. After graduating from Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur and spending six years in the IT industry, he felt an inner calling to step away from the corporate path and dedicate his life to the transformative power of music and wellness practices. His approach helps people reconnect with the deeper aspects of their being and cultivate a more balanced, integrated way of living. Alongside extensive training in classical music, Priyal has immersed himself in the oral traditions of saint poets such as Kabir, Nanak, and Meera. These teachings have deeply shaped Priyal’s own musical journey, grounding it in devotion, simplicity, and the timeless wisdom of the saints. Priyal regularly shares his music in concerts, satsangs, and community gatherings. He also organizes retreats and collaborative events with Prahlad ji and his ensemble, creating spaces where participants can experience the confluence of music, spirituality, and collective harmony.

This is essential reading for these times!” —Colette Baron-Reid, bestselling oracle expert, author, and artist "In a sea of books on astrology, Debra’s stands out." —Gabby Bernstein, #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Universe Has Your Back Debra Silverman is an astrologer, psychotherapist-trained educator, and author who has spent nearly five decades building a disciplined, system-based approach to astrology rooted in temperament, pattern recognition, and human behavior. At a moment when astrology is both ubiquitous and flattened into algorithmic shorthand, Silverman has become one of the field’s most consequential institutional voices, known for codifying chart literacy into frameworks that can be taught, applied, and carried forward across relationships, work, and personal change. Silverman’s work is anchored in clinical training and long practice. She earned a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology and Dance from York University and a Master’s degree in Clinical Psychology from Antioch University, then built a career working with individuals, couples, and families while developing a methodology that treats the birth chart as a structured vocabulary rather than entertainment. Her signature emphasis on the Four Elements gives audiences a clear entry point into temperament, conflict style, and stress response, translating complex archetypal material into language that holds up in conversation and decision-making. In 2016, she founded Debra Silverman Astrology, formalizing her methodology into a global education platform spanning multi-level curriculum, mentorship, retreats and intensives, and advanced practitioner training. At the center is Applied Astrology School, a structured program that has trained thousands of students worldwide, supported by trained mentors and advanced cohorts. Silverman also developed the 4E process, an elements-based methodology practiced through individualized sessions and certification retreats by trained facilitators, extending her work beyond instruction into a defined practice model. Within contemporary astrology, Silverman is widely regarded as a trusted authority for method and rigor. Her work has trained thousands of students and practitioners in a shared vocabulary and practical tools, while also serving as an on-ramp for a growing mainstream audience looking to engage astrology as a framework for self-understanding. Over decades, she has built a curriculum-driven ecosystem rooted in accountability, and her teaching has become a primary source of institutional knowledge in a field often dominated by shorthand. Silverman has also made her mark as a published author. Her first book, The Missing Element: Inspiring Compassion for the Human Condition (Findhorn Press), introduced her Four Elements framework to readers looking for language around temperament, patterns, and the parts of themselves they tend to judge, and it was later selected for Aaron Rodgers’ book club in 2022. Her second book, I Don’t Believe in Astrology: A Therapist’s Guide to the Life-Changing Wisdom of the Stars (St. Martin’s Essentials, April 2025), begins with a skeptic’s premise and builds a therapist’s argument, treating the chart as a practical framework for self-observation and accountability rather than a matter of belief. Debra’s influence extends well beyond her school. Across platforms, she has built a large, highly engaged audience of adult learners, particularly women, who return to her work for language around temperament, relationships, and the patterns that repeat until someone finally names them. She also hosts The I Don’t Believe in Astrology Podcast , a natural extension of her teaching, where she breaks down her framework in real time, defines terms with precision, and translates the chart into behavior you can recognize in yourself and in the people closest to you. That combination of institutional teaching and public-facing explanation has placed Silverman in a rare position: both a leading trainer within the field and a trusted interpreter for the broader culture. She has been sought out by public figures and creatives across industries; notable supporters and collaborators include Zach Bush, Gino Wickman, Aaron Rodgers, Sting, Tommy Chong, Jennifer Aniston, Julianne Hough, and India Arie. Taken together, her books, education platform, trainings, retreats, and media work operate as a cohesive body of instruction, with a shared vocabulary that students return to and practitioners carry forward. ee6dd2f0-7fde-4dbd-b3c6-23da56a2cb27: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. 86d3bcdd-41de-54da-939c-4f8aed8b81f1: What would you give for a chance to be the most omnipotent version of yourself? To finally be rid of the petty human desires that keep you from achieving greatness? To finally have it all, everything you’ve ever wanted? What would you trade? What are you willing to lose? What would you do for power? These questions are at the core of KiNG MALA’s debut album, And You Who Drowned In The Grief Of A Golden Thing . Across its wide-ranging 12 tracks – which seesaw between invigorating industrial pop and delicately refined R&B balladry – the singer-songwriter spins a tale as equally rooted in a sci-fi nightmare as it is in reality. The album follows the classic storyline of a hero’s journey to redemption, focusing on two non-descript, fictionalized characters: a human and an all-mighty entity. The front half is packed with the wonder of “what if.” What would an exchange for power look like? And more importantly, what would it sound like? (Think the experimental, living aesthetic of Bon Iver’s 22, A Million or Dijon's Absolutely , she offers – but with more bite.) The back half of the project provides answers – and it’s not pretty. By the story’s end, the human not only lacks power, but everything that made then human as well. “It's what we become, because the real dark shit that happens to women, you are never the same,” KiNG Mala shares. And at a time when the world is embracing such left-of-center storytelling, KiNG MALA is primed to emerge at the forefront of dark-pop’s new wave. “Everyone's being weird as fuck right now,” she says, citing world-building artists like Charli xcx and Chappell Roan and movies like The Substance . “We're moving into this space where we can be fucking freaks and finally be angry and disgusting – it's all manifesting.”

ff0d85a5-191a-4173-bf90-e44a666b31c9: Featuring Nate’ THESOULSANGER & Mirraje · Two powerful women. Two distinctive voices. One soulful night of music. NATE’ THESOULSANGER Some artists find their voice. Nate’ THESOULSANGER inherited hers. Born and raised in Oakland, Nate’ comes from a rich musical heritage as a descendant of the Grammy-winning Gospel Hummingbirds . Raised in a legacy of faith, storytelling, and soul, music was never simply something she discovered it was part of her foundation. An award-winning vocalist, international recording artist, songwriter, producer, actress, event host, and co-founder of SoulGlo Productions, LLC , THESOULSANGER has built a career that refuses to be confined to one genre. Her sound moves through soul, gospel, R&B, hip hop, theater, and beyond , bringing authenticity, power, and unmistakable Oakland soul to every performance. Throughout her career, she has shared stages and studios with artists including Patti LaBelle, Kelly Price, Carlos Santana, MC Hammer, LaRussell , and Grammy-winning producer Narada Michael Walden , with whom she has developed a longstanding creative relationship. Her voice is also woven into Bay Area music history. Nate’ created and recorded the memorable hook for Mac Dre’s “Make You Mine,” a song that became part of his enduring musical legacy. Her credits span radio, film, theater, live production, and recording. A Bay Area Rising Star and Best Vocalist award recipient , she has received KMEL airplay, contributed vocals to the Warner Bros. film The Invasion , and established herself as a trusted creative force both onstage and behind the scenes. At Yoshi’s Oakland , Nate’ has become such a familiar presence as a headliner, host, featured vocalist, producer, and collaborator that she earned the affectionate nickname “Ms. Yoshi’s.” Whether singing, producing, acting, hosting, mentoring, or creating opportunities for others, Nate’ brings the same qualities to every room: authenticity, excellence, soul, and connection. Singer. Songwriter. Producer. Actress. Host. Mentor. Community Builder. Oakland soul in every room she enters. Nate’ THESOULSANGER. The THE is intentional. CHRISTIE “MIRRAJE” MALONE Christie “Mirraje” Malone was born to sing. The daughter of blues musician George “Bluestone” Malone , Mirraje began singing at the age of three and writing songs and poetry by age nine. A gifted singer, songwriter, and natural stage performer, music has been woven into her life from the very beginning. Growing up in Los Angeles, Mirraje’s journey has been shaped by love, loss, perseverance, and an unwavering desire to create. After caring for her mother and experiencing her passing, Mirraje stepped away from singing and writing for four years. The memory of her mother—her greatest inspiration, biggest fan, and loudest cheerleader—eventually reignited her passion and gave her the courage to dream and create again. As she embarked upon her solo career, Mirraje recognized the extraordinary musical journey that had already taken shape. She has shared the stage with celebrated artists including Stevie Wonder, Evelyn “Champagne” King, Morris Day, Zapp, Club Nouveau, Cameo, Sugar Hill Gang, and Klymaxx . Mirraje’s musical influences span genres and generations, with Anita Baker holding a special place among her favorites. Her eclectic love of music allows her to find inspiration in the experiences, thoughts, emotions, and sounds that surround her. Rather than allowing her artistry to be defined by a particular genre or category, Mirraje creates from a place of freedom and authenticity. In her own words: “Life is unpredictable and unique. It should never be defined by genres or categories; nor should our music be. I just do what feels good.” SANG SIS! Together, Nate’ THESOULSANGER and Christie “Mirraje” Malone bring two extraordinary musical journeys to one stage for SANG SIS! —a celebration of powerful women, authentic voices, soulful storytelling, and music that refuses to be put in a box. Rooted in different musical legacies but connected by soul, these two women bring experience, grit, passion, and undeniable vocals to Yoshi’s Oakland for a night designed to make you feel something.

This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10.
