e104c744-6e45-4eb2-b9d5-78d9763f332d: Uncovered after 50 years, an absorbing and illuminating photographic archive of Black West Oakland in the 1970s. In 1974 Ken Light, a young underground press photographer recently arrived in California, was encouraged by residents of West Oakland to document daily life in the neighborhood. A white activist building relationships in an eminent Black community, Light was invited into homes and churches, flagged down on the street for impromptu portraits. The resulting images, taken over two years, ended up unpublished and nearly forgotten for half a century. Now made public for the first time in Soul City: Oakland, U.S.A. , they form a stunning and historically important archive of Black urban life in a major American city in the 1970s. These photographs reveal the deep pride running through West Oakland, despite the formidable attempts of local governments and agencies to tear the neighborhood apart. Soul City presents the everyday experiences and emotions of West Oaklanders: hard work, love, determination, resistance, humor, delight. Ken Light is the Reva and David Logan Professor in Photojournalism at the UC Berkeley School of Journalism and he will be in conversation this evening with Noni Session of The East Bay Permanent Real Estate Cooperative and Andrea Steves of the 7th Street Museum . They will be in conversation about Light's book, his career as a journalist in Oakland and the East Bay, West Oakland - its history and transformations - and the importance of documenting everyday life in our communities. Following the conversation will be audience Q&A and a book signing. Mrs. Dalloway's will be on site selling copies of the book. Please register to receive updates and reminders. Registration assists with planning; however, it does not guarantee a seat. Additionally, masks are encouraged and will be provided. Get accessibility information .

1bfe2385-b917-4525-8772-d267c9799543: Books Inc Palo Alto welcomes author Jim Emison November 19 at 7pm, for a discussion of his new narrative nonfiction Murder on the Hatchie. He will be joined in conversation by Matt Gonzalez, Chief Attorney San Francisco Public Defender's Office. About Murder on the Hatchie: Nearly forgotten voting rights history is resurrected. A narrative nonfiction account of the NAACP's 1940 attempt, the first in the 20th Century, to register black voters in majority black western Tennessee's Haywood County; the white terror campaign that followed culminating in the murder of Elbert Williams, the NAACP's first voting rights martyr; the FBI's faux investigation; sabotage by the US Attorney and the FBI; and the DOJ shameful reversal of its decision to prosecute Williams's killers. Murder on the Hatchie resets the timeline and the geography of the beginnings of the Civil Rights Movement and raises the question whether some of the bloodshed in the 1950s and '60s could have been deterred by a vigorous prosecution. Praise for Murder on the Hatchie "At a time of accelerated pushback to hard-won gains of the modern American civil rights movement, this book illuminates the human cost paid to secure voting rights for Black Americans. Expertly researched, it invites us to better comprehend the raw courage of individuals determined to exercise full American citizenship rights in the face of violent white supremacy." --Lecia J. Brooks, Southern Poverty Law Center "A powerful and necessary reminder of the courage and sacrifice that shaped the NAACP's earliest fight for justice. Jim Emison brings to light a painful but pivotal chapter in our history with clarity and care." --Derrick Johnson, president and CEO, National Association for the Advancement of Colored People "Jim Emison brings to light the largely forgotten killing of NAACP organizer Elbert Williams. Through years of research, he reconstructs the violence that followed Black citizens' attempts to register to vote. Murder on the Hatchie restores this story to the history of the civil rights movement." --Gilbert King, Pulitzer Prize-winning author of Devil in the Grove "In a day when just being a member of the NAACP could get you killed in the South, Elbert Williams and five other members stood up against the Jim Crow system and attempted to register to vote. Jim Emison captures the courage of Williams and the others in his insightful book, which reminds us why the right to vote remains critical to the survival of our American democracy." --Jerry Mitchell, investigative reporter "A searing excavation of terror and truth, a thunderous reminder that the right to vote has always been paid for in blood. This is not just buried history; it is a reckoning blazing into the light." --Keith A. Beauchamp, filmmaker, The Untold Story of Emmett Louis Till and Till "This powerful book is no mere cold investigative report of the past, but a warmly inspiring story of a lawyer and a community seeking to find answers for the present and our future. Painstaking research and a poignant story make this book a must-read--and a must-heed." --Rev. Cornell William Brooks, Esq., 18th president and CEO, NAACP, and professor, Harvard Kennedy School "Murder on the Hatchie exposes how racism, fear, and abuse of power shaped both the crime and the community's response to it. More than a true-crime narrative, it serves as a moral reckoning while challenging readers to confront the enduring legacy of racial terror, systemic discrimination, and the importance of historical memory." --India A. Artis, archivist for NAACP, and former business manager of The Crisis magazine "With Murder on the Hatchie, we have it--the right man writing the right book at the right time.... In this invigorating, groundbreaking narrative, Jim Emison recounts the history as can only one who has lived close to it." --Margaret A. Burnham, director, Northeastern University Civil Rights and Restorative Justice Center, and author of By Hands Now Known: Jim Crow's Legal Executioners "Emison importantly confers on Elbert Williams the greater notoriety he deserves for his heroic efforts as an early civil rights pioneer and member of the NAACP. Williams can now take his place in the pantheon of civil rights martyrs." --Matt Gonzalez, chief attorney of the San Francisco Public Defender's Office "This book is a magnificent legacy that shows how a mighty few can expose our worst behaviors of the past, then come together decades later to win redress." --Hank Klibanoff, director of the Georgia Civil Rights Cold Cases Project at Emory University and coauthor of the Pulitzer Prize-winning The Race Beat: The Press, The Civil Rights Struggle, and the Awakening of a Nation BIOS Jim Emison , noted Tennessee courtroom lawyer of 43 years, lives in the adjoining county, only 20 miles from the events he brings to life. He knew many of the actors but the horrific events were a taboo topic he only learned of in retirement in 2012. He has been working and speaking about the murder ever since. Currently he is working to establish an Elbert Williams Interpretive Center in Brownsville Tennessee modelled on the Emmett Till Center in Sumner Mississippi. Matt Gonzalez , Chief Attorney in the San Francisco Public Defender's Office, is a Stanford Law grad, a former President of the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, and was in 2000 the Green Party's candidate for Vice President of the United States.
31ff457c-7427-414a-bb60-f11a734ccbb7: Agriculture, Adaptation, and the Politics of Belonging · An evening with author Margiana Petersen-Rockney in conversation with journalist Anna Sale What happens when the climate is changing faster than the stories we tell about ourselves? Farmers and ranchers are experiencing climate change directly. Drought, wildfire, extreme heat, shifting seasons, water scarcity ~ these are not abstract predictions but realities shaping land, livelihoods, families, and futures. Yet the politics of climate change can make responding to them extraordinarily complicated. In Farmers and Climate Change: Agricultural Adaptation in an Age of Rural Polarization , Margiana Petersen-Rockney takes us beyond the divide between those who “believe” in climate change and those who don't. Drawing on seven years of research in Northern California, she explores how farmers actually adapt ~ and the social, political, economic, and deeply personal forces shaping their choices. Because changing how we farm can mean changing a relationship to land. To family. To neighbors. To identity. To generations of knowledge about what it means to be a farmer. Petersen-Rockney joins award-winning journalist Anna Sale , host of Slate's Death, Sex & Money and People Trying , for a conversation about what happens when climate science meets lived experience, and what becomes possible when we listen to the complicated realities beneath polarization. The evening will begin with a short introduction from anthropologist Cari Borja , whose work sits at the intersection of food, agriculture and education ~ placing the conversation within a larger question: How do we ask people to change without first understanding what we are asking them to risk? Perhaps meaningful climate action begins not only with changing practices ~ but with understanding people, the places they belong to, and what change is asking of them. Margiana Petersen-Rockney is a political ecologist who studies climate change and rural livelihoods. Margiana grew up farming and worked in food justice non-profits before receiving her PhD from University of California, Berkeley where she was a National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellow in the Environmental Science, Policy and Management Department. She’s now an Assistant Professor of Environmental studies in the Franke College of Forestry and Conservation at the University of Montana. Anna Sale is a journalist who hosts the award-winning interview podcast Death, Sex & Money from Slate and the new multimedia interview series People Trying , featuring people who work close to land, water, and nature as we're all adapting to change. She’s also been a contributor to This American Life, Fresh Air, The New York Times, and The Atlantic, and the author of Let’s Talk About Hard Things. She splits time between Berkeley and Cody, Wyoming.

d88b9d36-84f4-4b5e-81b7-07ef9b0c1805: Funk. Jazz. Fusion. Culbertson. · Over the course of crafting a 29-album catalog and architecting 40 Billboard #1 singles as a keyboardist, songwriter, and producer, Brian Culbertson has charted his own unique course in music. Label him jazz, and he makes a funk record. Call him an R&B artist, and he drops an acoustic jazz trio collection. Brand him pop, and he creates a 32-minute New Age opus. And you’d be hard pressed to name another instrumentalist of his ilk who can mount an elaborately designed concert production that will keep him on the road for three consecutive months. Culbertson burst onto the scene in 1994 with a chart-topping album that he recorded in his college apartment, featuring keyboard-led contemporary jazz tracks. “Long Night Out” landed him a lengthy record deal and signaled that a star was born. Flash forward to the present day, Culbertson has been going back and listening more and more to music that inspired him as a young musician, such as David Sanborn, The Brecker Bros, Chick Corea, Al Jarreau, Pat Metheny, and others in the jazz fusion world. "It instantly brought me back to the days of ‘no rules’ and the pure joy of music, something that I think a lot of albums today are lacking. With that said, I set out to write and produce a new album that would try to capture a little bit of that late 70’s and early 80’s spirit of music exploration, along with using only live musicians and real instruments. Similar in style to “Another Long Night Out”, “Day Trip” is the daytime version!” said Culbertson. Possessing style, panache, and a savvy business mind capable of moving the needle in music and beyond, Culbertson founded and curates the annual Napa Valley, New Orleans, Hawaii, and Chicago Jazz Getaways, which have attracted guests from all over the globe to experience his premier events. Whether you’re listening to music from “Day Trip” on record or live in concert, you’re hearing an eclectic, entertaining and engaging set from an artist at the peak of his power.
16a9770a-5fac-50f1-a1a9-49b621513778: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Computerwife New York City-based Addie Warncke began Computerwife in 2018 at the beginning of her college career, using SoundCloud as a diary to chronicle her emotions. When the pandemic hit, Warncke released the five songs she was proudest of as her self-titled debut EP, and the strength of those tracks led to a signing with Danger Collective Records. Now, she’s poised to release her debut self-titled full-length: a raw and intimate portrait of her experiences processing the small but poignant moments that shape a life. Computerwife’s sound is captivating and nuanced, pushing the boundaries between analog and digital. “The main theme that ties this album together is an interest in the deep web and an attempt to combine existing media to make something new,” she explains. With her seamless blend of shoegaze, emo, and lo-fi noise pop, Computerwife speaks directly to the disquiet experienced by every 21st century digital girl with a tenuous grip on life and identity. Without any prior production knowledge or a band to work with, expanding her songs beyond the writing stage was a challenge Warncke sought to overcome. A Song Exploder episode about Grimes inspired her to download a free trial of Ableton so she could flesh out tracks and learn more about electronic production. On her dorm room bed, she began to record with her dad’s guitar and bass, a Fender deluxe amp, and a focusrite to Ableton. Her first EP and forthcoming debut LP are pulled from these 3 years of exploring music production on her computer, made with limited, portable equipment. Computerwife ultimately reflects Warncke’s very core; it was inspired by internet rabbit holes, books, films, albums, and bands that have shaped her: from Coney Island to My Bloody Valentine, Alex G, The Flaming Lips and Texas Chainsaw Massacre . Lyrically, Computerwife grapples with the psychological state Warncke was in when she, in her own words, “went crazy, deleted all my music, and ran back home.” Created out of rediscovered mp3 files, scraps of almost-forgotten melodies and re-recorded instrumentals, the album is a hard-hitting digital collage that mirrors her disparate influences and a tangle of raw emotions. Lead single “Lexapro” teeters between pop and shoegaze and finds Warncke drawing inspiration from Sonic Youth as she grapples with feelings of failure and stasis. Driving standout “I Get Better Everyday,” influenced by Alex G’s production, sees her turn a corner: “When I made it, I thought I was gaining control of my life and building self-confidence. I wanted to write about a friend I had grown up with who kept telling me she hated how I changed, because to me I felt like I was finally doing what I wanted to do instead of living for other people,” Warncke explains. “This song is one of the first songs that taught me how to write lyrics. I was reading Annihilation (by Jeff VanderMeer) and wrote down interesting words and then found ways to use those words to express my own thoughts.” The breezy and heavenly highlight “Vacation” came about after Warncke read How to Do Nothing (by Jenny Odell) and visited Coney Island for the first time: “I thought the ecosystem was really beautiful and people seemed really relaxed together. I really needed that kind of environment to clear my head for a while and it was very inspiring.” On the tense and explosive “You Make It Look So Easy,” Warncke explores the relatable experience of admiring someone so much that your fondness turns to jealousy. “Texas Chainsaw Dilemma” uses Sally’s screams from the movie Texas Chainsaw Massacre in place of spoken vocal samples over a pulsing and shimmering electronic beat. While the first few sets Warncke played as Computerwife consisted of her alone on stage with her laptop, sampler, and bass, she’s since expanded her live show into a full band for a bigger and heavier sound, including drummer John Supnik and guitarist Dalton Salisbury. After polishing their performance and playing several hometown shows around New York City, the band opened for the Southeastern tour leg of British lo-fi legends Panchiko and have also played shows supporting Been Stellar, Hello Mary, and They Are Gutting a Body of Water, among others. Computerwife is dialectical music at its finest, managing to be simultaneously painful and celebratory, noisy and dancey, detached and heartfelt. “This album is alot about finding my values, figuring out what I want my life to be like, and committing to it” says Warncke. a1a3f0da-af83-5a0f-8c9d-b73131c47abf: Artist and producer duo RØZ, comprised of Manolo Cabrera and Hugo Lara, has rapidly emerged as one of the most innovative forces in Mexico’s electronic music renaissance. In less than three years, the project has evolved from digital experimentation to selling out major venues, redefining the expectations of Latin electronic music with a fluid, boundary-breaking sonic identity. Manolo Cabrera began his artistic journey inspired by the cinematic world of large-scale electronic festivals – specifically, the Tomorrowland films that first awakened his fascination with dance music. Early explorations led him through trap, Tropical House, and Future Bass, releasing early work on SoundCloud as he developed his voice. Hugo Lara’s path started in classical music. At just four years old, he played violin to the works of Italian composer Antonio Vivaldi. In his adolescence, artists like Skrillex pulled him toward EDM, prompting him to experiment with production through GarageBand – an entry point that eventually enabled his first collaborations with Manolo. The two met in high school, each maintaining their solo projects while constantly exchanging ideas and feedback. “He created sounds with synths that I didn’t know how to make,” Manolo recalls, while Hugo admired the originality in Manolo’s compositions. Their chemistry crystallized after a joint track with Tom & Collins, and the two officially united under the name RØZ, marking the beginning of the duo. Their evolution has been intentional and uncompromising. After an early phase shaped by imitation and experimentation, they found their voice when they decided to reject the “rules” of genre altogether. “When our sound truly changed, that’s when we realized there were no rules,” explains Hugo. This breakthrough sparked a distinctive aesthetic that merges drum and bass, trap, reggaeton, UKG, and electronic textures into a singular style. Their transition to Spanish lyrics in mid-2022 became a key turning point, cementing the identity that would propel them into global recognition. Unlike many Mexican electronic projects that focus on recreating global trends, RØZ is committed to building an identity that is deeply personal – and deeply connected to its audience. “Instead of seeing the people who follow us as fans, we see them as friends,” says Manolo. In the past year, RØZ’s rise has accelerated to unprecedented heights, marked by major festival debuts at EDC Mexico, Bandidos Festival, Baja Beach Fest, and many more, where their high-energy performances have become a calling card. Demand reached historic levels in late 2025: their first-ever U.S. tour, “Oye, Estados Unidos,” sold out within minutes in every major market, solidifying RØZ as one of the most sought-after live acts of the year. Just before the tour launch, they delivered their biggest solo concert yet – “Se está haciendo tarde CDMX”– packing Pabellón Oeste del Palacio de los Deportes in Mexico City. This runaway live momentum paralleled their chart breakthrough, as RØZ secured three entries on the Billboard Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart with “flashes” featuring Yng Lvcas, their viral anthem “CORA DE HIELO,” and their powerhouse collaboration “Apaga la luz” with Peso Pluma. Combined with the viral acclaim of their groundbreaking Spotify Sessions, and surpassing 410 million career streams, RØZ’s 2025 run established them as one of the most inventive, globally resonant acts rewriting the future of Latin music. In December 2025, RØZ released their anticipated debut EP, mañana, temprano– a masterclass in genre fluidity that moves seamlessly through reggaeton, electronic, house, bachata, and techno with cinematic flair. The EP reflects the duo’s boundary-breaking ethos and global reach, featuring collaborations with creative trailblazers Nsqk, DannyLux, El Bogueto, and UK hitmaker Cloonee. 2026 has already been full of milestones for RØZ. They've been on their sold-out tour with stops all over the US and at festivals like Coachella (leaving people out of the tent since it was over capacity both weekends!), EDC Las Vegas, and Sueños Fest. Plus, the guys also joined Peso Pluma on stage at his show in NYC, made it onto Rolling Stone en Español’s Future 25 list, and hit 300M+ all-time global streams. Showing no signs of slowing down, RØZ recently announced their upcoming debut album SE ESTÁ HACIENDO TARDE, set to release on August 7th with 19 new songs. Their recent single, “HBU” featuring Artemas, offers a glimpse into the duo’s new era as they continue to push their evolving sound to the next level. The duo is building on a remarkable trajectory, establishing themselves as one of the most visionary and influential forces in contemporary Mexican electronic music

This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts. While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga. After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today. Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

b6054daa-5108-5047-a1a3-93068b81b2d0: When we gather with others, conversation almost automatically drifts toward what has already happened or what might happen next. Stories, plans, reactions, hopes—these patterns are so ingrained that we barely notice how completely we relate to one another through the lens of the past and future. But when we pause those habits, something surprising occurs. The room changes. Attention sharpens. A different kind of connection begins to emerge. A small clearing inside awareness opens—a place where no future is rehearsing itself, and no echoes of the past are allowed to enter. We can touch this space alone in contemplative practices, but it's rare to enter it with others. The Present Moment Game is a simple social meditation designed to explore that possibility. Participants speak only from what is happening in the moment, and gently bring each other back when attention drifts. What unfolds is often unexpected, and never the same twice. Curious? Come play! ____________________________________________ IMPORTANT ARRIVAL INFO: Please arrive anytime between 6:30 and 7:00. You’re welcome to a cup of complimentary tea as you settle in—just note that drinks won’t be brought into the circle, so do come early if you’d like to enjoy an unrushed cup. Also, please note that this is a “sealed-container” experience, so late entry isn’t possible. After a brief 5-minute grace period for unforeseen delays, doors will close and we’ll begin promptly at 7:05. Thank you for planning accordingly! ____________________________________________ Is This Event for You? A few things to consider before you decide: * Phones and watches off As an invitation to loosen your grip on time, you’ll be asked to remove your watch and fully power down your phone for the duration of the experience. * This is not an Authentic Relating practice T-Group, Circling, and other AR forms use present-moment awareness as a vehicle for relational exploration. That’s not what we’re doing here. Our subject isn’t each other, but the moment itself. * Kindness is essential Please come willing to encounter everyone in the room with openness and warmth. This is a gentle space for contemplation and focused attention, not edge-pushing or confrontation. ____________________________________________ One participant’s experience: "As a person who loves, thinks, and talks about language for a living, I am wide-eyed at how rich, alive and vital it feels to speak solely in the present tense. It’s the best of meditation and conversation distilled into a social elixir. I feel hooked, thirsty for more. Alli creates a magical container. You won’t regret it." — Sophia ____________________________________________ Want more info about the game? * WEBSITE: https://www.thepresentmomentgame.com/ * INSTAGRAM: https://www.instagram.com/thepresentmomentgame/ * WHATSAPP GROUP: https://chat.whatsapp.com/IPCe9wNzLqc8yFvB5n7THb (Announcing upcoming games. It's a notification-only group that publishes 1-3 messages per month)

71989a84-1403-405e-9ecd-f9234efbf18a: (Please do not bring infants to the show) Born into a radical theater company, Joyful Raven was tasked from the tender age of 5 with the daunting mission to save the world from impending doom… using theater. Forced into animal-print unitards and political positions long before she was a consenting adult, she never had a fighting chance at anything resembling a normal life. You think your parents were embarrassing? Did you have to sing about salmon sex on stage, in a unitard, at 12 years old… WITH your parents? I didn’t think so. In an attempt to heal her hippie trauma, she runs away from home to seek solace in the arms of a spiritual teacher… and accidentally finds herself in the yoga-to-fascism pipeline. Can she save herself? Can she save the world… using theater?! Blending standup, drag, storytelling, & clown, Raven takes audiences on a dystopian and hilarious romp through the looking glass. ACTOR : Joyful Raven is an award-winning actor, director, and “story midwife” known for her powerful and thought-provoking solo shows, where she tackles thorny social issues with humor, heart, and nuance. Born into an iconic political theater family, she has been devising original work for over 20 years. Her first solo comedy, Tales of a Sexual Tomboy , was dubbed “…one of the funniest shows now on display on Bay Area stages” by the SF Chronicle, won Best of the Fringe at the 2016 San Francisco International Fringe Festival, and enjoyed an Off-Broadway run in 2017. Her latest solo show, Breed or Bust , was nominated for Best Comedy at the 2022 Hollywood Fringe Festival, critically acclaimed at the 2023 Edinburgh Fringe, where it won an Offie (OffWestEnd Award), and went on to have an extended run at The Marsh, where it received a Critics’ Pick in the SF Chronicle. She co-founded the award-winning theater company Rococo Risqué and co-authored four plays for the Prize of Hope-winning company Human Nature. As an actor, she has appeared in numerous stage and film projects, including Odyssey Works, the film The Pursuit of Happyness alongside Will Smith, and Spring Awakening, directed by Stafford Arima. Joyful holds an MFA in Dramatic Art from the University of California, Davis, and teaches solo performance and storytelling at Berkeley Rep School of Theatre, The Marsh, and her own studio in Berkeley. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joyfulraven/ Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/joyful.raven DIRECTOR : Jael Weisman , a founding member of the Dell’Arte Players Co. and a multi-Obie-winning director, is a trailblazer in actor-based theater, directing acclaimed productions like “Whiteman Meets Bigfoot,” “Performance Anxiety,” and “Mad Love.” With Dell’Arte, his works have toured extensively in South America and Europe, earning him numerous Dramalogue Awards for Directing. Noteworthy projects include “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which traveled to New York and was awarded an Obie, the American premiere of “Red Noses” at the San Diego Repertory Co., “Uncle Gunjiro’s Girlfriend” at the Adelaide Festival, and “Mermaid Meat” for the Berkeley Symphony Orchestra. He has collaborated with luminaries like Carlo Mazzone-Clementi and Joe Chaikin and worked with renowned Bay Area performance artists including Jeff Raz and Brenda Wong Aoki. In his early career, he worked with The San Francisco Mime Troupe, directing among other things “The Dragon Lady’s Revenge,” which was awarded an Obie. Weisman holds a BA from Reed College and an MFA from Carnegie Tech Lighting Design : Kiara Valderrama Show Photos : Cynthia Smalley It is with great love and a deep bow of gratitude that I roast by inimitable parents, Jane Lapiner and David Simpson and their theater company Human Nature. bfa6a7e3-2cf2-40c5-bc64-65e6f0f31769: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”
0fbd1152-0c23-4ef3-9724-6ec4064f69ec: In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process. In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.
3926c95f-fee7-40c7-8d63-ca93ebca9eb2: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.
55a8643b-b3bc-4e1a-a76c-1b76c4e03dec: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Babehoven Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive. "Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead. 9cb3464d-1db1-4cbb-a167-725533c431ff: Spencer Day Feinstein's at the Nikko November 20 & 21 Previewing his new Project: La Frontera Spencer Day comes home to San Francisco for the first live preview of La Frontera , his exciting new collection of original music inspired by his life in Mexico. Blending jazz, pop, the Great American Songbook and Latin influences, Spencer explores the cultural connections between Mexico and the U.S.—and the unexpected ways music can bring us together. This special evening will feature brand-new songs and arrangements from La Frontera alongside favorites from Spencer’s celebrated catalog, plus a very special guest musician from Mexico. With his signature mix of sophisticated musicianship, storytelling and humor, Spencer invites audiences to be among the first to experience where his music is headed next. A new chapter. A special homecoming. A first listen. Don’t miss Spencer Day at Feinstein’s at the Nikko. From the Artist “I’ve spent the last few years falling ever deeper in love with Mexico—not just with the music, but with the people, the culture and the way so many of our traditions coexist,” says Day. “ La Frontera grew out of that experience. It’s about more than just the border—it’s about what happens when cultures meet, influence one another and create something new. It’s a meditation on the many things that connect us and divide us. I’m incredibly excited to share it for the first time with the city that gave me my start. San Francisco has always felt like coming home. ”

4f433308-7173-49f5-a771-5ec5d975d037: A powerhouse performer blessed with a voice made of pure soul, Seattle-based singer, composer, and keyboardist Brittany Davis brings their deeply felt songs blending jazz, R&B, and hard-grooving funk. Raised in Kansas City, Davis developed into a commanding vocalist, pianist, producer, and songwriter whose work is rooted in vulnerability, social consciousness, and deep musical intuition. Her breakthrough debut album, Image Issues, earned widespread acclaim from NPR, KEXP, SPIN, and Good Morning America, establishing her as an artist capable of transforming personal struggle into cathartic, transcendent art. Davis has collaborated closely with Stone Gossard through the project Painted Shield and released music on his Loosegroove Records label, while also working with acclaimed Seattle musicians including Evan Flory-Barnes and D'Vonne Lewis. Her music draws comparisons to Nina Simone, Roberta Flack, and Rahsaan Roland Kirk for its emotional intensity and spiritual depth. Her latest album, Black Thunder, is a bold, largely improvised work of spiritual jazz recorded live over two days. Featuring hypnotic grooves, explosive improvisation, and deeply personal storytelling, the album showcases Davis at her most raw and visionary, confirming her status as a transformative force in modern music. Personnel: Brittany Davis (keyboards, vocals); Others TBA

ce170670-2ccb-48a0-bd3d-d9c64d16b07d: Pioneering Romani jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt lamented that he might be neglected by history, but today the ebulliently swinging “jazz manouche” sound he created with French violinist Stéphane Grappelli is more pervasive than ever. For this very special night, the leading purveyors of the style, the Django Festival Allstars, return to the Miner stage for a magical evening of hot jazz. Featuring the guitar mastery of Samson Schmitt of the Schmitt clan, the first family of jazz manouche, the Django Festival All-Stars also includes accordionist and keyboardist Ludovic Beier, violinist Pierre Blanchard, and rhythm guitarist Francko Mehrstein — all of whom gained fame as part of the original band led by family patriarch Dorado Schmitt — joined by bassist Antonio Licusati. This assemblage of masters in the Roma jazz style are regular performers at the annual Django Reinhart Festival in Samois-sur-Seine, France and New York’s celebration at Birdland, which celebrates over a quarter century of music. The group performs in support of their new Motéma Music release, Evolution, a hard-swinging collection of original compositions written and arranged by the members of the band. DownBeat magazine hailed the release as “(jazz manouche) for the 21st Century!” Personnel: Samson Schmitt (guitar); Francko Mehrstein (guitar); Pierre Blanchard (violin); Ludovic Beier (accordion, keyboards); Antonio Licusati (bass)

472c6a50-6960-4971-ac44-ce4a801af28f: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet-and-greet signing event with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan, following their Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan's beautiful new work, Market Memories Cookbook , celebrates 50 years of the Davis Farmers Market with 92 all-new seasonal recipes illustrated by the authors. Guest essays about the market’s origins, the battle for farmers market certification and the sense of optimism and change of the 1970s add yet another dimension to this celebratory book. Throughout the pages, heartfelt anecdotes from the farmers, vendors and shoppers illuminate the poignant role the market continues to play in our daily lives. The Davis Farmers Market was voted USA Today’s 10 Best Farmers Market (2015) and America’s Favorite Farmers Market (2009). For more information on awards and the market, go to www.davisfarmersmarket.org . “When the Davis Farmers Market opened, it was extraordinary, and it is astonishing that it is still here fifty years later. It stands as a testament to the simple, radical idea of connecting people directly with local organic farmers and ranchers. I am so impressed.” ALICE WATERS, Chez Panisse Restaurant and Edible Schoolyard Project, Berkeley For more than fifty years, Ann M. Evans , former mayor and Citizen of the Year of Davis, California, has helped to bring healthful eating to an ever-growing audience through both her work with government and non-profit organizations and her writing. Among her many accomplishments is the co-founding of three regional food-system mainstays: Davis Farm to School, one of the first farm-to-school programs in the country; the 51-year-old Davis Food Co-op; and the award-winning Davis Farmers Market. She was also at the table for the creation of the Certified Farmers Market regulations, representing the Department of Consumer Affairs. Ann is the author of several cookbooks and texts to improve school lunch, as well as a botanical artist drawing inspiration from her garden, the creeks and wildlands of Yolo County, and the market. Her food influences stem from a lifetime of international travel, childhood summers in Chapel Hill and Durham, North Carolina, summers in Provence, France, her northern England family heritage, and a lifetime amidst the agricultural landscape of Northern California. She lives in Davis with her husband, surrounded by a small edible garden where she keeps bees and chickens. At age eight, Georgeanne Brennan wrote her first cookbook. The recipes were written on lined foolscap paper stapled together with a bright yellow cover, titled My Recipes. Since then, she's written more than thirty cookbooks, won a Julia Child award for one and a James Beard award for another. She has lived in Provence, where she raised goats and made and sold cheese, taught high school in Arctic Alaska, and cooking classes across the nation. For six years, she hosted her own Culinary Vacation program, bringing people to share a week for shopping, cooking, and foraging in the interior Provence, where she has had a home for more than forty years. In the early 1980s, Georgeanne co-founded Le Marche' Seeds and was instrumental in importing European heirloom seeds and selling them to farmers across the United States, earning her place in the pantheon of the California Food Revolution. She lives in Winters with her husband, where she gardens, cooks, writes, and paints between welcoming her extended family, including eight grandchildren and their dogs. Ann M. 968f5ae3-0cb3-5e5b-81be-a6e385faa0ce: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please pay at the door. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

c3cd6487-2918-4907-97d0-ceeb786985f5: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

Lynne Kaufman ( Playwright ) is the author of 20 full-length plays that have been produced in San Francisco, Los Angeles, Washington D.C., and Louisville at such theatres as Magic Theatre, Actors Theatre of Louisville, TheatreWorks Silicon Valley, and many more –with Shameless Hussy being her most recent work which premiered at The Marsh San Francisco spring 2025. Four of Kaufman’s plays, Extreme Acts, Acid Test, Two Minds , Who Killed Sylvia Plath , and Poetic Justice, have premiered on stage at The Marsh, while two others, Exposing Margaret Mead and The Smartest Woman in America, have appeared on The Marsh’s digital platform MarshStream. Who Killed Sylvia Plath went on to win Best Play in The Marsh’s 2020 MarshStream International Solo Festival. Kaufman’s plays have won many awards including the Glickman Award for Best New Play ( The Couch ), the Kennedy Center’s Fund for New American Plays Award ( Speaking in Tongues ), and the Neil Simon Festival New Play Award ( William Blake in Hollywood ). Kaufman has published four novels, and her short stories have appeared in Cosmopolitan , Redbook , and McCall’s . She was also the recipient of the Otis Guernsey Outstanding New Voice in American Theatre Award from the William Inge Theatre Festival. Warren David Keith ( Director ) is delighted to be reunited with Playwright Lynne Kaufman. His work with her began in 2012 with the Marsh Berkeley premier of Acid Test: The Many Incarnations of Ram Dass , a solo piece in which he played the title role. The play was extended twice in Berkeley then transferred for one performance to a massive tent on Maui, Hawaii where it was seen and enjoyed by Ram Dass and about 300 devoted followers. Subsequently, Acid Test opened at the Marsh San Francisco in 2013 where it also had several runs. As a director he mounted more than 15 productions for American Conservatory Theater’s Young Conservatory Program. beb7c4c8-06e7-4b0c-b763-a0f3b3932a26: Grammy-nominated saxophonist and multi-instrumentalist · Born and raised in Los Angeles, Albright was already an accomplished saxophonist by the time he enrolled at the University of Redlands, but he switched to bass after he saw Louis Johnson in concert. A few months after graduating from college, he joined jazz pianist/R&B singer Patrice Rushen, who was in the process of forming her own band. Later, when the bassist left in the middle of a tour, Albright replaced him and finished the tour on bass guitar. Playing both sax and bass, he became the consummate session and touring musician in the 80s, working with everyone from Anita Baker, Ray Parker, Jr., Atlantic Starr, The Temptations, and Maurice White to Les McCann, Teena Marie, the Winans, and Whitney Houston. He launched his solo career in the infancy of what became the smooth jazz format, with Just Between Us in 1987, and has been a core part of the genre with chart-topping albums, countless radio hits, and as a member of many all-star tours, including Guitars & Saxes and Groovin’ For Grover. In the late 90s, he fronted a big band and toured with pop star Phil Collins and did a dual recording with vocal great Will Downing called Pleasures of the Night . Between his last two Grammy-nominated solo albums, Pushing The Envelope (2010) and Slam Dunk (2014), he enjoyed hit collaborations with two huge hits – 24/7 with guitarist Norman Brown and Summer Horns by Dave Koz and Friends (including Mindi Abair and Richard Elliot), which were also Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Instrumental Albums. He toured with Brown and Summer Horns, and most recently has been on the road with South African gospel/jazz singer and guitarist Jonathan Butler. Albright’s other albums, whose titles perfectly reflect their flow, include Smooth (1994), Groovology (2002), Kickin’ It Up (2004), and Sax for Stax (2008). Because Albright’s musical muse has taken him to so many fascinating locales along the contemporary R&B/urban jazz spectrum, he’s joyfully defied easy categorizations. “Top to bottom,” Albright says, “Whether in concert, listening to my music over the radio or CD player, I always want my listeners to be taken on a musical journey with different textures, rhythms, chord progressions, and moods. I want people to know where I’ve been and where I’m going, and to let them hear that I’m in a really good place in my life.”

9162841a-47e3-43dc-bed9-a1eae2320e29: Orchestra Liberation : A Symphonic experience featuring music of The Black Diaspora led by Kev Choice, 60-piece orchestra, choir, and special guest. Orchestra Liberation is a fresh, new, Black-led and musician centered , Oakland-based orchestra bringing the power of the symphonic tradition together with the sounds, rhythms, and creative spirit of the Black Diaspora. Intergenerational and multi-genre, the ensemble reimagines what an orchestra can sound like, look like, and represent, rooted in a simple principle: our music, played by our people, in community with one another. The repertoire will move fearlessly across generations and genres, featuring original works by Kev Choice, a composition by Cava Menzies, and dynamic orchestral arrangements spanning Stevie Wonder, Bay Area Hyphy, Hip-Hop classics, R&B staples, and works by African American classical composers. More than a concert, it is designed to be a living, communal experience, with audiences singing, dancing, and vibing along to a rich, soulful sonic palette that moves seamlessly from the symphony hall to the block. Led by Artistic Director Kev Choice—an Oakland pianist, composer, producer, and MC, classically and jazz-trained yet deeply rooted in Hip-Hop, Soul, and R&B—the orchestra unites strings, winds, brass, percussion, rhythm section, choir, vocalists, MCs, DJs, spoken word, and more for a powerful, interactive, and dynamic musical experience. The choir is directed by acclaimed Oakland composer and educator Cava Menzies, founder/director of CO-LLAB Choir. This intergenerational collective features Bay Area luminaries including harpist Destiny Muhammad, rising jazz artist Ayo Brame, veteran R&B and Hip-Hop musicians, and accomplished symphony players—coming together to celebrate Black musical legacy, community, and a bold new vision for the orchestra. **VIP ticket includes Priority Seating, Meet & Greet with Kev Choice, Orchestra Members, and a Special Guest after the show**

cea0e849-2687-4d1a-b1d6-e03605af2d72: A short list of the most exciting young alto saxophonists to emerge in the last five years would have to include Sarah Hanahan. Her incendiary performances were already turning heads via far-flung touring with the Mingus Big Band, drummer Ulysses Owens Jr. and Generation Y, Sherrie Miracle and the Diva Orchestra, and drummer Joe Farnsworth. But the release of her 2024 debut album Among Giants catapulted her into a whole new realm, earning a rare five-star review from DownBeat. She brings the magic of that album to the Joe Henderson Lab with her powerful quintet. More than holding her own with veteran masters Marc Cary (piano), Nat Reeves (bass) and Jeff “Tain” Watts (drums), Hanahan completed the journey from apprentice to leader, playing with the intensity, self-possession and audacious creativity of a major-league talent. She’d studied with Reeves at the Jackie McLean Institute of Jazz at the Hartt School of Music as an undergrad and with Cary at Juilliard, where she earned a Master’s in 2022. That same year Hanahan was tapped for the first-ever class of NPR Jazz Night in America’s Youngbloods and featured as one of five “up-and-coming jazz geniuses who are revolutionizing their genre” in their 20s. She’s been ascending steadily ever since. Personnel: Sarah Hanahan (alto saxophone); Others TBA
e0b488a7-6c13-4338-8fba-50b2135c0792: GRAMMY-winning drummer and composer Brian Blade brings back The Fellowship Band to perform music from across their seven studio releases. Easily one of the most versatile and soulful musicians in jazz, Blade grew up as the son of a Baptist pastor in Shreveport, Louisiana and was immersed in gospel music from his birth. He formed the Fellowship in 1997 with pianist and fellow Loyola student Jon Cowherd, releasing a series of increasingly accomplished sessions culminating in his 2023 session on his own Stoner Hill imprint, Kings Highway. Featuring Blade, Cowherd, saxophonists Melvin Butler and Myron Walden, and bassist Christopher Thomas, The Fellowship is recognized for a “sound that echoes grace and unity” (The New York Times). As Blade was developing his own musical identity as a bandleader, he became an increasingly in-demand sideman and band member, cultivating long-term associations with Joshua Redman, Joni Mitchell, Kenny Garrett, Daniel Lanois, Bill Frisell, and Chick Corea, with whom he earned a GRAMMY. In 2000, Blade began his most visible and fruitful partnership as a member of jazz legend Wayne Shorter’s all-star quartet, touring the world and recording four albums with the saxophonist, including the GRAMMY-winning 2013 release, Without a Net. The Fellowship band returns to SFJAZZ for their first performance since 2018. Personnel: Brian Blade (drums); Melvin Butler (soprano & tenor saxophones); Myron Walden (alto saxophone, bass clarinet); Jon Cowherd (piano); Christopher Thomas (bass)

b490959d-ae58-5367-af09-ce39132aafa7: In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic. Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves.. Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition. Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. eb5adff1-e954-5b11-a6b6-83085f780c0c: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

About the book: For fans of Katherine Arden and Kell Woods, an enchanting, feminist fantasy retelling of the Brothers Grimm tale “The Wild Swans”: a young woman’s handiwork and determination is tested to the limits to save her six brothers, cursed to become swans. “Know this; no word of yours shall ever break my spell.” As the only daughter in her noble family, Elisa von Ahlefeldt has always been the untamed outlier. Unlike her six brothers who follow the protocols and duty of the court, she is ellevilde —elf-wild—a child of nature. She spends her days in the woods where she has befriended Nuve, an ash-tree maid who teaches her the ways of forest magic. Elisa finds she has a gift for magic that matches the needlecraft talent she learned from her mother—whose tragic death has torn the family apart. Following the funeral, Elisa’s father reveals he has been spellbound by a Hexe into marriage and sends his young children into hiding. Years pass before stepmother Belinde locates them, transforms the boys into swans, and alters her husband’s perception of his daughter, casting her out of their lives. To break her brothers’ curse, Elisa is guided by Nuve to use her needlecraft to create magical garments from stinging nettles for each of them under a vow of silence. A silence she must keep while impersonating a missing noblewoman. A secret she must hold dear even as she is betrothed to a handsome stranger. A power she must wield to defy the evil Belinde and rescue her family before their bird nature steals their human lives away forever. For Elisa, despite the perils of the Hexen and her own fears, knows deep in her heart that: “Silence has its power, and not all that is wild can be tamed.” A coming-of-age fantasy adventure, Curse of Feathers , is a tale of inner strength at the crossroads of faith and mysticism, rich with historical details in this retelling of the classic Brothers Grimm fairy tale. Kimberly Bea is the author of mythology and fable-inspired fiction, including The Changeling Queen and The Curse of Feathers. A member of the Society for the Promotion of Speculative Fiction, her shorter work has been published in the anthologies Den of Thieves and Spring: Dreams and Nightmares and poetry in the anthology Nothing But Red . She is a social historian and lifelong feminist with undergraduate and graduate degrees in Ancient History with comparative fields in medieval history and the ancient Near East. A native of California, she lived in Minneapolis for 25 years before moving back to her home state. Visit her online at KimberlyBea.com .

98c73945-7329-58fd-a3e6-830ff408713f: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

1106d1ef-46e4-5491-8e6d-a894a7d910bf: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. About Suzanne (Zan): With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

33f9ded4-e7cd-5448-b6df-212b96935762: Experience the deep benefits of Zhineng (Wisdom Healing) Qigong. This practice strengthens the immune system, supports the body’s natural capacity to heal, and cultivates mental clarity and emotional steadiness. Through simple, time-honored movements, the nervous system unwinds, the mind becomes more spacious, and the heart opens. Over time, practitioners often feel more resilient, centered, and connected — both inwardly and outwardly. Tickets are sliding scale $10-$25 - Please arrive at least 5-10 minutes early. Hiromi will be in Japan February 1-21 but will resume classes when she gets back Hiromi Vardy is a certified Zen Shiatsu, Yang style Tai Chi, and Zhineng Qigong healer and practitioner. She first encountered Tai Chi in 1973 while studying theater design and performance art in London. Initially drawn to the beauty of the movements, she soon discovered that the practice had a profound effect on her consciousness, awakening a deep interest in the healing arts. While collaborating on stage with dancers in London, Hiromi began treating injuries in overworked bodies. In 1976, after a serious accident that resulted in loss of circulation in her leg and concern about possible amputation, she turned to daily Tai Chi practice, self-massage, and treatment from a Japanese acupuncturist. This experience became a turning point in her healing journey and led her back to Japan, where she studied Shiatsu at the Namikoshi School and trained at the Zen Shiatsu Center under Shizuto Masunaga. After moving to the United States with her family in 1987, Hiromi continued deepening her practice and teaching. During a period of significant stress later in her life, she encountered Master Ming Tong Gu and began studying Zhineng (wisdom healing) Qigong under his guidance, eventually becoming licensed to teach. The healing shift she experienced through this practice was profound and continues to inform her teaching today. Since 2013, Hiromi has been dedicated to teaching Zhineng Qigong, expanding her offerings to include online classes in 2020. Her work invites students to explore the foundations of Qigong and Tai Chi as embodied, healing practices that cultivate awareness, vitality, and resilience.

841a1770-d48d-43e4-ac23-20c2221b0a02: Queen of Percussion · One of life’s constants for Sheila E. comes down to a simple phrase: follow the beat. And her impeccable inner rhythm is the pulse behind a trailblazing career that still knows no bounds. Family, faith and music were guiding forces for Sheila E. growing up in the Bay Area. In addition to percussionist dad Pete, the Oakland, CA native counts former Santana member/Azteca founder Coke Escovedo and The Dragons front man Mario Escovedo as uncles. Fellow Latin star Tito Puente was her godfather. In addition to being weaned on Latin jazz and Motown, Sheila E. was exposed to a diverse array of Bay Area acts. Those influences ranged from the rock of Jefferson Airplane and the Grateful Dead to the R&B/pop of the Pointer Sisters and the funk of Sly & the Family Stone. “I used to sit on the corner outside of the local community center with Twinkies and 7-Up listening to Sly and Larry Graham rehearse,” remembers Sheila E. “The sounds of the Bay Area molded me.” So it’s no surprise that after such a music-immersive childhood, the gifted, world-class drummer and percussionist began amassing an impressive string of credits playing not only with her dad but also with pioneering talents like George Duke, Herbie Hancock, Marvin Gaye, Diana Ross, Lionel Richie, Prince, Ringo Starr, Gloria Estefan, Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez. Grammy Award-nominated singer/songwriter behind the seminal hits “The Glamorous Life” and “A Love Bizarre.” A fearless multi-instrumentalist, equally proficient on guitar and bass, actress, mentor and philanthropist. Following a Bay Area gig in the late ‘70s, Sheila E. met Prince backstage. Their Purple Rain recording sessions—including her vocals on the 1984 classic “Erotic City”—morphed into launching her solo career that same year. Debut album The Glamorous Life spun off the Grammy Award-nominated top 10 hit of the same name plus a second top 40 single “The Belle of St. Mark.” Between her ‘80s tenure as drummer, songwriter, and musical director for Prince’s backup band, Sheila E. released two more solo albums ( Romance 1600 and Shelia E.) and scored another classic hit with “A Love Bizarre.” Sheila E.’s fierce, dynamic verve onstage has made her a major concert draw since the ‘90s. Along the way, she has acted in the films “Krush Groove”, “The Adventures of Ford Fairlane”, “Chasing Papi” and launched various music projects (E-Train, C.O.E.D., E Family Band). She added to her arsenal of credits performing on the 2012 Academy Awards with pop hitmaker Pharrell Williams and composer Hans Zimmer. Sheila E. was also among the roster of stars chosen to perform at the 2013 Kennedy Center Honors, whose honorees included artists Herbie Hancock, Billy Joel, and Carlos Santana. Sheila E.'s producing, arranging, and performance talents have been showcased throughout the music and film industry with appearances on The Academy Awards, The Latin Grammy Awards, BET Awards, The American Music Awards, The Kennedy Center Honors, The Summer Olympics, WOW Awards, ALMA's, and The Image Awards, just to name a few. In 2010, Sheila was nominated for an Emmy Award for “Outstanding Music Direction” in recognition of her leadership as musical director for President Obama’s Performance at The White House: Fiesta Latina and again more recently in 2020 for “Let’s Go Crazy” Grammy Salute to Prince. Other projects include The E Family
