59d25ad2-4c75-569a-963d-0d86663527b3: A joyful, mischievous, heartfelt book for children and the grown-ups who love them. Recommended for ages 6–10, parents, grandparents, teachers, and anyone who wants to remember what it feels like to live with curiosity, courage, humor, and heart. The Braunicles invite readers into the wonderfully imperfect world of a spirited little boy named Braun. A world filled with adventure, mischief, big feelings, unexpected lessons, and an irresistible enthusiasm for life. Written by Jennifer Levi, the stories are warm, funny, honest, and deeply human. Jennifer gives a distinctive voice and captures childhood in a way that feels both whimsical and completely real: the bold ideas, the questionable decisions, the enormous emotions, the funny family dynamics, and the little moments that often become the memories we treasure most. At its heart, The Braunicles is about living fully. Braun approaches the world with curiosity. He takes chances. He includes people. He makes mistakes. He loves fiercely. He finds fun where others might not see it. And through each story, young readers discover that some of the qualities that make a child challenging, surprising, loud, adventurous, or different can also become their greatest strengths. For parents and grandparents, there is another layer. These stories are a gentle reminder not to rush through childhood trying to make everything perfect. Sometimes the mess is the memory. Sometimes the mischievous child becomes the unforgettable adult. Sometimes the moments that make us shake our heads today are exactly the stories we will tell for the rest of our lives. Jennifer’s voice brings humor and perspective to parenting without preaching. That makes The Braunicles more than a children’s book. -It is a book children can enjoy for adventure. -It is a book parents can recognize themselves in. -It is a book grandparents can give with meaning. -And it is a book families can read together and talk about long after the final page. Jennifer Levi is the founder of The Live Like Braun Foundation and the force behind The Live Like Braun movement. Since the death of her son in May 2025, Jennifer has become a powerful advocate for DUI awareness and meaningful legislative change, passing a new Bill in CA, testifying at the CA State Capitol and on Capitol Hill. She regularly speaks to audiences at DUI workshops and schools all over Southern CA. She serves on MADD's CA State Legislative Board. Jennifer’s advocacy has been featured across multiple media outlets and television networks including NBC, ABC, Fox, and CBS, along with well-known podcasts hosted by Dr. Phil, Kennedy, Jason Kennedy, Amanda Kloots, Kelly Gores, Meghan Judge, and Kate Casey. Jennifer has spoken openly about the profound transformation of her life following the death of her son. She has become a featured contributor to Maria Shriver’s Sunday Paper, writing about the ways grief has reshaped her life with raw honesty, deep emotion, and a touch of irreverence. She hopes The Braunicles inspires children to embrace exactly who they are and encourages grown-ups to give young people the freedom to let their brightest, silliest, most authentic selves shine. Jennifer is a mother, wife, advocate, writer, and former TV executive. Although she has worn many hats, she has always said she is most proud of her role as mom to her two children, Adelle and Braun. She lives in Pacific Palisades, California, with her family and two very naughty dogs. dea54605-5970-5067-b005-8fa31c312cc8: Many of us work with psychedelics without a guide or with limited support to integrate these experiences. That can feel painful or lonely when we’ve had meaningful journeys (and also when we’ve had disappointing journeys!). Healing – especially from interpersonal injuries – deepens when done in community. The same is true of personal and spiritual growth. Even the most joyful experiences are best metabolized when witnessed. Together, we become a mosaic – a colorful and varied community, greater together than the sum of our parts. Mosaic is a psychedelic integration circle for self-identified women. Here, you’ll find a supportive space to integrate the lessons, challenges, and wisdom from psychedelic journeys so that you can apply those learnings to everyday life. Together, we’ll seek to understand our psychedelic experiences and make profound insights accessible and actionable. This is a drop-in, monthly supported peer group rather than a psychotherapy group. We create space for sharing stories and experiences, receiving support, and forging genuine connections. Meditation, mindful movement, somatic practices, Internal Family Systems parts work, and creative tools are all part of the fun. Whether you’re new to integration or looking to deepen your practice, you’ll find a supportive community here. Note: You’re invited to bring an object for our community altar that represents some aspect of your journey. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please pay at the door. This event is a closed container. There will be no further entry after 2:15. Dr. Lyssa Menard is a psychologist, psychedelic therapist, and professor (Northwestern University Medical School) with specialties in Integrative Medicine, trauma treatment, and health psychology. She is the founder of Strategies for Change, a coaching and consulting firm promoting personal, organizational, and leadership change and has been a consultant to a wide range of media outlets, including CNN, New York Times, and WebMD. She brings this varied background to her integration groups, facilitating growth and change through a multi-media concoction of integrative therapeutic approaches (mindful movement, creative arts, somatic healing and embodiment, social connection, and spiritual ritual). Dr. Menard’s book, "Results May Vary: Hope & Healing through Psychedelic-assisted Psychotherapy" is scheduled for release in 2026. As a beneficiary of excellent (and also, sadly, lackluster) psychedelic treatment, she is a skeptic of the field, a critic when necessary, and a true believer in the healing possibilities offered by these medicines. She serves as an advocate for community and patient education and fights for legal access to psychedelics for health and healing. As a recent transplant to California's Bay Area, Dr. Menard spends a ridiculous amount of time at The Berkeley Alembic, cavorting in nature, worshipping the sun, and developing community. 2c5ebbc8-b832-44d7-b506-ed7d6bfef162: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

94f55b3a-2524-449f-993c-302b3a0edcfa: This Christmas season, experience an unforgettable evening of jazz with Bay Area legend Tammy L. Hall as she celebrates one of the most distinctive voices in jazz history: Shirley Horn . With her unmistakably rich voice, elegant piano playing and extraordinary sense of timing, Shirley Horn had a rare ability to make every song feel intimate and deeply personal. She didn't simply sing a song—she lived inside it, finding emotion in the spaces between the notes. Her legendary recordings, including Here’s to Life , have made her an enduring favorite among jazz lovers and musicians alike. Now, acclaimed San Francisco pianist and vocalist Tammy L. Hall brings Horn’s music to life in the intimate setting of Feinstein’s at the Nikko. Joined by Kevin Goldberg on bass and Jason Lewis on drums , Hall will explore the songs, sounds and spirit that made Shirley Horn such a singular artist. And this is exactly the kind of music that belongs in a room like Feinstein’s. With only 125 seats, every seat puts you close to the performance. You’ll hear the subtleties—the beautiful piano voicings, the warmth of the bass, the conversation between the drums and piano, and Hall’s expressive interpretation of Horn’s extraordinary repertoire. Whether you are already a Shirley Horn devotee or are discovering her music for the first time, Here’s To Shirley! promises an evening of sophisticated, soulful jazz performed by musicians who understand that sometimes the most powerful moments happen when the music simply has room to breathe. Make it part of your holiday tradition. Gather your friends, bring someone special, enjoy a cocktail and settle in for a beautiful night of live jazz with one of San Francisco’s own musical treasures. The Tammy L. Hall Trio Presents: Here’s To Shirley! A Tribute to Shirley Horn Sunday, December 6 • 7:00 PM Feinstein’s at the Nikko Tammy L. Hall — Piano & Vocals Kevin Goldberg — Bass Jason Lewis — Drums One legendary voice. One extraordinary Bay Area artist. One intimate night of jazz. Here’s to Shirley.

ba35853d-42c3-5e46-b7ca-fa900fe2117c: In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic. Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves.. Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition. Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.
c963e37a-a92a-5732-b8ad-661ec0e71326: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.
1a182e64-fbd7-43ef-a8c0-d9875c5626ed: What is Bookagami? Book Folding is a global art genre. No glue, no scissors, no stress! Learn how to repurpose discarded (or favorite) books into beautiful, sculptural art with the award-winning Marin artist Adrienne Biggs, the originator behind Bookagami. This hands-on Bookagami workshop guides participants through the meditative and mindful practice of folding books into unique, creative, and sustainable art. Adrienne Biggs’ Bookagami art has captivated Marin . A 30-year Marin resident and former book publishing professional, Adrienne will introduce her unique approach—combining origami, altered books, and circular economy principles—to help every attendee fold up to three books into works of art. Workshop Highlights: Learn Bookagami techniques: Start with simple folds and progress to more complex forms, suitable for all skill levels. Embrace sustainability: Discover how book folding diverts unwanted books from the landfill and gives them renewed purpose. Connect and create: Enjoy a community atmosphere where creativity sparks joy and every fold is intentional yet also spontaneous. Take home your art: Finish the session with your handmade Bookagami sculptures to display at home or give as gifts, and the skills to keep folding. What to bring to the workshop: Newer paperbacks or hardcovers with minimum 1” spine (around 300 pages) work best. Books with words and books with images produce different results/color patterns, so you are encouraged to bring and try both at the workshop (see images below for examples). Book Passage can also supply you with books if needed. Meet Your Instructor Adrienne Biggs is an accomplished artist known for fostering creative inclinations within this community, while rescuing books from landfill (or a dusty bookshelf) by repurposing these common two-dimensional objects into three-dimensional works of art that people of all ages can enjoy, create, and share. Since 2024, she has created more than 600 unique “Bookagami” (as she calls them). Her Atlas, 1963: You Are Here won First Place Blue Ribbon at the 2024 Marin County Fair, and her Bug-a-Gami totem and her Stars, Stripes & Stories piece each won ribbons in 2025 and 2026. Past public art exhibits include two-month shows at Town Books in San Anselmo and at Marelli’s in downtown San Rafael; three month shows at the downtown San Rafael Public Library and at the Friends School in San Francisco; one-month show at ACCI Gallery in Berkeley; and various exhibits at ArtWorks Downtown in San Rafael. Her current solo show, Black White & Read All Over, is at Falkirk Cultural Center in San Rafael November 6 - December 15, 2026. Learn more at @IntoTheFoldBookagami on Instagram. What students are saying about Adrienne "Adrienne was so much fun, and I took home 3 lovely art projects and will make more on my own." Susan F. "Loved it! Adrienne was an excellent teacher. She told fun stories and was very motivating. I had three great examples I created and brought home...I am not crafty and Bookagami was easy to do and fun to learn." Diana S.

2b36ecac-e60c-5f64-b39d-0312f233453a: Who Gets to Tell the Story? · Every book on a shelf is the result of a series of choices. Which ideas are considered urgent? Which voices are given space? Who decides what gets published, how a book is positioned, who is imagined as its reader, and, ultimately, which books find their way into our hands? From the outside, publishing can look like a relatively straightforward journey: an idea becomes a manuscript, a manuscript becomes a book, a book arrives on a shelf. But behind that journey is an ecosystem of editors, publishers, marketers, distributors, booksellers, institutions, economics, relationships, taste, timing, and power. At every stage, someone is deciding what is worth paying attention to. Join us at Clio’s for a conversation about the politics of publishing with Tim McKee , Publisher of North Atlantic Books; Michelle Phan , Marketing Manager at University of California Press; author and advocate Kelechi Ubozoh ; and cultural anthropologist and Clio’s founding member Cari Borja , whose programming explores what can happen when different voices, disciplines, and ways of knowing are deliberately juxtaposed, creating the possibility for unlikely conversations. Together, we’ll follow a book from idea to bookshelf while asking the harder questions beneath that journey: Who gets through the door? What kinds of knowledge are valued? Which stories enter the cultural conversation, and which don’t? What gets changed, or lost along the way? And what roles do authors, publishers, marketers, booksellers, programmers, and readers play in determining which ideas circulate through our culture? Kelechi Ubozoh’s We’ve Been Too Patient: Voices from Radical Mental Health gives us a particularly powerful book through which to examine these questions. Bringing together voices challenging conventional understandings of mental health and healing, the anthology asks what happens when lived experience itself becomes a form of knowledge, and what it takes for voices outside dominant systems to make their way into print and into public conversation. A bookstore is never simply a place where books are sold. It is a place where voices are chosen, ideas are juxtaposed, unlikely conversations begin, and culture is made. Tim McKee, Publisher, North Atlantic Books Tim came to NAB in 2013 and is honored to serve as publisher. Born in New York City, McKee grew up in Los Angeles and received a BA from Princeton University and an MA in journalism from the University of Missouri. He has worked in the nonprofit sector for his entire career, including serving as the long-time managing editor of The Sun magazine, the grants director for a social-justice foundation in San Francisco, and as a writer for several community-based organizations in California. He has also taught college-level writing and journalism. His book No More Strangers Now: Young Voices from a New South Africa (Dorling Kindersley) was an Honor Book for the Jane Addams Book Award and a Los Angeles Times bestseller. He is happiest when bringing necessary stories to the page. Michelle Phan , Marketing Manager, UC Press Michelle launched her publishing career at North Atlantic Books as a publicist before transitioning to marketing at UC Press. With 7+ years of experience in book promotion, she is passionate about uplifting authors and books that share the knowledge necessary for our times. As Vice President of Bay Area Women in Publishing and Co-Chair of the Robin Seaman Award Committee, she also cares deeply about fostering meaningful relationships and building inclusive community within the industry. Kelechi Ubozoh, Author and advocate For over a decade, Kelechi has worked in the California mental health system in the areas of research and advocacy, community engagement, stigma reduction, youth development and peer support. Kelechi has spoken publicly about her experiences on multiple platforms, including CBS This Morning with Gayle King, O The Oprah Magazine, and The S Word documentary. Kelechi began her career as an investigative reporter in New York City, and was the first student-reporter ever published in The New York Times . In 2019, Kelechi published her anthology with L.D. Green, We’ve Been Too Patien t, which features diverse voices who all share their stories of radical healing and consider the recent movement towards reform in the mental health field, including the mad pride/consumer movement, theater as therapy, peer support, combating stigma, and trauma-informed care. Most recently, she co-authored What I Wish My People Had Known: The Psychiatric Green Book: A Guide for Black Folks with Yolo Akili Robinson, a strategic guide helping Black communities protect against racialized violence and institutional harm.

Berkeley. In The Flying Death: Poison, Plunder, and the Quest for a Miracle Medicine in the Amazon (FSG; November 10, 2026), historian Matt O’Hara tells the story of a young, frail American explorer named Richard Gill, who traveled to the Amazon in the 1930s to open a tourist ranch. Instead, he stirred up an international hunt to harvest a local vine known as curare. As Gill and his rivals quickly realized, curare was both a dangerous poison used by local tribes in blow darts and a potential cure for numerous ailments, including multiple sclerosis and other motor diseases. Seeking to treat his own degenerative illness and make a fortune, Gill established connections with tribal leaders and pharmaceutical companies back home—even as his Russian-born rival, Boris Krukoff, sought to do the same. Navigating treacherous terrain and politics, Gill and Krukoff successfully created a veritable curare industrial complex. The plant became a key element in shock therapy treatments and, eventually, in anesthesia back in the United States. Gill and Krukoff’s rivalry and ethical compromises offer a timeless reflection on how personal ambition, competition, and obsession can shape—and sometimes distort—scientific and cultural progress. In this ethnobotanical adventure story, O’Hara deftly explores the intersections of indigenous knowledge, scientific exploration, and exploitation, and poses searching moral ​conundrums about the price of progress. And who pays it. “The Flying Death is as gripping as the exotic poison at its heart. This is historical narrative nonfiction at its best.” —Mitchell Zuckoff, author of Lost in Shangri-La “Matt O’Hara has uncovered the thrilling true story of Richard Gill, a sickly American explorer who ventured into the Amazon in 1938—and ended up transforming medicine. The story will surprise you, infuriate you—and it will definitely make you smarter.” —Deborah Blum, author of The Poisoner’s Handbook “An unforgettable tale of medicine, ambition, greed, and the natural world, The Flying Death is a true page-turner. Matt O’Hara is a tenacious historian who writes with great skill and with a keen eye for human drama and injustice.”—Hector Tobar, author of Deep Down Dark Matt O’Hara is a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Cruz. He is the award-winning author of many journal articles and two books, The History of the Future in Colonial Mexico and A Flock Divided: Race, Religion, and Politics in Mexico, 1749–1857. Rebecca Herman is Associate Professor of History at UC Berkeley, where she teaches about environmental politics, US-Latin American relations, and modern Latin America. She is the author of Cooperating with the Colossus: A Social and Political History of US Military Bases in World War II Latin America and is currently at work on a book about anti-extractivism in Antarctica. 7fc1f9d7-71d9-5132-a3c9-e31f6ead1bc5: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

393bcee2-d3a0-4d39-994e-fda39c648035: Rebuilding Our Cities — And Our Democracy · Cities like New York, Los Angeles, and San Francisco are in crisis. Chronic housing shortages are driving countless middle-class and working-class households out of high-opportunity areas. Homelessness is skyrocketing. Cars continue to rule city streets, poisoning the climate and putting everyone’s health and safety at risk. And city governments, instead of rising to meet the challenge, are increasingly dysfunctional and unaccountable. Build or Die: How America Is Suffocating Its Cities and What to Do About It traces the history of a disaster a century in the making, detailing how shortsighted and reactionary policy decisions led to the interlocking crisis that threatens America’s great cities.Join Build or Die author Ned Resnikoff, California Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, and Economic Security Project co-founder Natalie Foster for a conversation about what ails America's great cities—and how we can revitalize both urban America and American democracy. Ned Resnikoff is an independent writer and urban policy analyst. His work has appeared in The New York Times , San Francisco Chronicle , The New Republic , The Nation , Dissent , and The Atlantic , among other publications. He writes Public Comment , an online newsletter about cities and democracy. Natalie Foster is author of The Guarantee: Inside the Fight For America’s Next Economy and co-founder and former President of Economic Security Project, an organization dedicated to building economic power for everyday Americans. She's a Senior Fellow at the Aspen Institute Future of Work Initiative. Assemblymember Buffy Wicks represents the East Bay in the California State Assembly, with a district spanning the communities of Oakland to Richmond, and includes the Cities of Berkeley, El Cerrito, and others. Asm. Wicks is Chair of the Appropriations Committee, after serving as Chair of the Assembly Housing Committee for two years prior. She has a track record of taking on the toughest fights to solve our state’s housing crisis. In addition to this work, she focuses heavily on protecting our social safety net, keeping kids safe in the digital world, and championing the rights of women and working families. A lifelong organizer, Asm. Wicks previously served for President Barack Obama for six years. She lives in Oakland with her husband, Peter, and daughters, Jojo and Elly.

745c0337-933d-4cf7-b9cc-c39b376661c3: Three time GRAMMY® winning ensemble · Spanish Harlem Orchestra, the three-time GRAMMY® winning Salsa and Latin Jazz band, sets the gold standard for excellence in authentic, New York-style, hardcore salsa. Whether in a concert hall or at an outdoor jazz festival, there is no easing you in as they come at you full force, from start to finish. Their energy on stage and their rich sound and musical precision leave audiences mesmerized until the last note is played. With an unwavering respect for the music’s storied history, the ensemble’s thirteen world-class musicians and vocalists come together to create an unparalleled musical experience. For over 20 years, SHO has been dedicated to the sounds of the barrio (Spanish Harlem, NYC). Their music is characterized by the raw, organic, and vintage sound defined by the genre. They are on a mission to keep the musical legacy of salsa dura (hard salsa) alive and expand its audience to those who love great music, not just Latin music. Grounded in the past, while focused on the future, they strive to keep the music relevant, creating a unique and fresh approach. “As a leader and producer, my mission and vision are to represent the great history and legacy of this music that I’ve been blessed to be a part of my entire life,” reflects Hernández. “Our passion and commitment to this music is never-ending.” With this unyielding motivation, SHO’s GRAMMY® nominated 2022 release Imágenes Latinas saw the band exploring new dimensions but never deviating from its core belief. “As with all the new SHO recordings, the concept and sound are the same, but the playing of new songs, arrangements, and performances always aim to create a new magic for the listeners,” Hernández adds. SHO released their 9th studio album, Swing Forever , in 2024, further solidifying the group as “the leading light of the salsa reconstruction movement” ( Newsday ). With eight albums and six GRAMMY® nominations, this powerhouse orchestra is aware that it is crucial to continually push itself and raise the bar. Their sixth album, entitled Anniversary, won the 2019 GRAMMY® Award for Best Tropical Album.

dd3cc0ba-fdd6-5284-862d-ad83ebbad822: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. About Suzanne (Zan): With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

952ca31b-c87f-5293-a510-726387b6b5a7: From a stunning new voice in popular science, Bogland is a beguiling debut that invites us to discover the hidden power of Earth’s mysterious landscapes while calling for their defense before it’s too late. Not quite land and not quite water, boglands have long been dismissed as wastelands—too sodden to farm, too perilous to cross, too unruly to be considered beautiful. Come closer, however, and a strange truth emerges: These wild, eerie landscapes stretch our minds, hold the history of humanity, and will shape the future of our planet. In Bogland , acclaimed ecologist Merritt R. Turetsky invites readers to discover the elusive magic and surprising power of these misunderstood places, where the boundaries blur between life and death, past and present, refuge and peril. Venturing from the boreal forests of Canada to the jungles of Borneo, and from the planet’s oldest bog in Greece to some of its newest in Greenland, Turetsky unveils bogs as marvelous paradoxes that defy categorization and their own systemic undervaluation. Here, radical life forms—acid-flinging mosses, amphibian-eating plants—spring from layers upon layers of dead matter. The past and present commingle with uncanny intimacy as peat safeguards artifacts for centuries, along with ancient lives unearthed later as “bog bodies” so remarkably preserved they are sometimes mistaken for the recently missing. Proverbially dangerous, bogs have offered shelter throughout history to the marginalized and resistance movements from Virginia to Vietnam. Crucially, they also regulate the planet’s climate, sequestering nearly one-third of Earth’s soil carbon while covering just 3 percent of its surface—even as accelerating exploitation risks transforming them from climate allies to climate foes, and erasing these ecosystems just as we’re learning to appreciate them. The debut of an extraordinary nature writer, Bogland is an ode and a call to action: to defend bogs’ strangeness and stillness from rising destruction, to value them precisely for their refusal to conform, and to learn from them new ways to adapt, endure, and belong on our changing planet—before it’s too late. Merritt R. Turetsky is a university professor and ecologist. She has served as a science adviser for Eos Magazine and has been featured in Time Magazine and on CNN, PBS NewsHour, and the BBC. She lives in Boulder, Colorado. Ed Yong is the author of two prize-winning New York Times bestsellers, An Immense World and I Contain Multitudes . He won a Pulitzer Prize and a George Polk Award in 2021 for his coverage of the COVID-19 pandemic, and was awarded a Guggenheim Fellowship in 2024. His work has appeared in many publications including The Atlantic , The New York Times , National Geographic , Wired , and The New Yorker ; he was also featured in three editions of the Best American Science and Nature Writing anthology, which he then guest-edited in 2021. He regularly does talks and interviews, and his TED talk on mind-controlling parasites has been watched by over 1.9 million people. He lives in Oakland, California, with his wife Liz Neeley, founder of Liminal Creations, and his corgi, Typo. He is almost certainly looking at birds right now. Merritt R. 9b773990-998e-5976-92c7-a9b743eb0249: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Storefront Church Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. 156754fa-aad1-5405-9093-7fbd3ae44d88: When we gather with others, conversation almost automatically drifts toward what has already happened or what might happen next. Stories, plans, reactions, hopes—these patterns are so ingrained that we barely notice how completely we relate to one another through the lens of the past and future. But when we pause those habits, something surprising occurs. The room changes. Attention sharpens. A different kind of connection begins to emerge. A small clearing inside awareness opens—a place where no future is rehearsing itself, and no echoes of the past are allowed to enter. We can touch this space alone in contemplative practices, but it's rare to enter it with others. The Present Moment Game is a simple social meditation designed to explore that possibility. Participants speak only from what is happening in the moment, and gently bring each other back when attention drifts. What unfolds is often unexpected, and never the same twice. Curious? Come play! ____________________________________________ IMPORTANT ARRIVAL INFO: Please arrive anytime between 6:30 and 7:00. You’re welcome to a cup of complimentary tea as you settle in—just note that drinks won’t be brought into the circle, so do come early if you’d like to enjoy an unrushed cup. Also, please note that this is a “sealed-container” experience, so late entry isn’t possible. After a brief 5-minute grace period for unforeseen delays, doors will close and we’ll begin promptly at 7:05. Thank you for planning accordingly! ____________________________________________ Is This Event for You? A few things to consider before you decide: * Phones and watches off As an invitation to loosen your grip on time, you’ll be asked to remove your watch and fully power down your phone for the duration of the experience. * This is not an Authentic Relating practice T-Group, Circling, and other AR forms use present-moment awareness as a vehicle for relational exploration. That’s not what we’re doing here. Our subject isn’t each other, but the moment itself. * Kindness is essential Please come willing to encounter everyone in the room with openness and warmth. This is a gentle space for contemplation and focused attention, not edge-pushing or confrontation. ____________________________________________ One participant’s experience: "As a person who loves, thinks, and talks about language for a living, I am wide-eyed at how rich, alive and vital it feels to speak solely in the present tense. It’s the best of meditation and conversation distilled into a social elixir. I feel hooked, thirsty for more. Alli creates a magical container. You won’t regret it." — Sophia ____________________________________________ Want more info about the game? * WEBSITE: https://www.thepresentmomentgame.com/ * INSTAGRAM: https://www.instagram.com/thepresentmomentgame/ * WHATSAPP GROUP: https://chat.whatsapp.com/IPCe9wNzLqc8yFvB5n7THb (Announcing upcoming games. It's a notification-only group that publishes 1-3 messages per month)

CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

8c25f0ec-d1bd-4db8-8425-96b0510c7b4a: Coming up as a teen through the Duke Ellington Orchestra and serving a memorable five-year stint with the iconic Miles Davis, saxophone virtuoso and 2023 NEA Jazz Master Kenny Garrett is “one of the most admired alto saxophonists in jazz after Charlie Parker” (The New York Times). He returns to SFJAZZ with his latest ensemble. A Detroit native, Garrett came of age in the 1980s and was grouped in with the so-called neo-traditionalist “Young Lions” of the era, but it was clear from the start that his adventurous spirit defied easy categorization. Beyond his work with Davis and the Ellington band, Garrett performed with trumpeters Woody Shaw and Freddie Hubbard before releasing his 1984 debut, Introducing Kenny Garrett, and joining one of the last iterations of Art Blakey’s vaunted Jazz Messengers. Garrett’s extensive output as a leader established the saxophonist as a masterful composer and conceptualist, with standout sessions including 1990’s African Exchange Student, 1997’s Songbook, 2003’s Standard of Language, and the expansive, GRAMMY-nominated 2006 release Beyond the Wall. Garrett received a GRAMMY nod for the 2009 all-star Five Peace Band Live with McBride, Chick Corea, and John McLaughlin, and his latest is the 2024 Mack Avenue release Who Killed AI?, an innovative electro-acoustic collaboration with keyboardist and producer Svoy. 42f4d319-b904-4b2b-afb9-e025db7dd5d1: Jenny Andrus Children's Book Author and Librarian Elsa's Chessboard Elsa carries her chessboard everywhere, always ready for a game. When World War II forces her from Europe, can chess help make America home? Growing up in 1900s Vienna, Elsa watches her brothers play chess. “No girls!” they tell her when she first asks to learn; but she’s determined, and soon she’s such a pro that they give Elsa her very own special chessboard. From then on, Elsa plays chess whenever she can. When she grows up, she even meets her husband over games in the park. But when World War II grips Europe, the young Jewish family flees to America, where they find themselves surrounded by unfamiliar languages. Luckily, Elsa knows one language that can always bring people together: chess! Based on the life of author Jenny Andrus’s grandmother, with illustrations by award-winning artist Julie Downing, Elsa’s Chessboard is an inspiring and exciting tale, perfect for any reader who's ever found meaning in a special object. Lady Georgiana Rannoch never expected to be more than a guest at the coronation of King George VI, but murder and some international intrigue make for a change of plans… One of the most daunting things about being related to the royal family but not being royalty myself is finding just the right ensemble for incredibly important events like the coronation. The process has become especially difficult as my maid has fallen ill and I am now relying on Queenie for everything—well almost everything. We do have a lovely new nanny with whom my son James is quite smitten. My concerns about gowns and Queenie-related disasters are put aside when I receive a worrisome letter from my mother. She seems anxious to see me and is missing her grandson-not at all like her! Darcy and I read between the lines only to discover a coded plea for help. We decide the best way to get Mummy away from Hitler and his cronies is to secure her an invitation to the coronation and have her stay at Eynsleigh along with our other guests for the big event. Two complications quickly arise. A stern member of the German government has arrived with Mummy who seems to be watching her-and our-every move. And then I unexpectedly find myself involved in the coronation ceremony at Westminster Abbey. Well, that solves my worry about what I should wear as I will be outfitted by Buckingham Palace for the festivities. But with a house full of visitors for the big event, Darcy receives word that the ceremony itself, and all of the royal attendees are under threat. And to make matters immeasurably worse, one of my esteemed house guests is found quite dead in their bed. Darcy and I must find a killer and prevent a terrible tragedy all while I do my best to avoid any embarrassing mishaps at the coronation, as quite literally, the world will be watching. Rhys Bowen , a New York Times bestselling author, has been nominated for every major award in mystery writing, including the Edgar®, and has won many, including both the Agatha and Anthony awards. She is also the author of the Molly Murphy Mysteries, set in turn-of-the-century New York, and the Constable Evans Mysteries, set in Wales, as well as two international bestselling stand-alone novels. She was born in England and now divides her time between Northern California and Arizona. CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985

14bff46d-bcf5-4441-b493-8060d4cb084f: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: June McDoom There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition. She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for. Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive. Mento is the root of all of it: ska, rock steady, reggae, dub and everything after. He is the one who put a guitar in her hands. An inheritance, a gift and a map. Even her name is part of it, though she will tell you she landed on it more by feel than reason. She records as June McDoom, born Alyssa, June being a nickname one of her grandmothers, Joan, went by, a name she thought was cool to carry and simply liked the sound of. An etheric channel that reverberates all the same. A dub all its own. Made slowly and by hand with her longtime partner Evan Wright, Follow the Light lays the harmony of folk over the rhythm of dub, with Dionne Warwick, Minnie Riperton, Pentangle and the washed guitars of Cocteau Twins haunting its outer edges. Voice and guitar seeking each other out first, then everything else stacked across long days in the studio they keep at home, restraint kept on purpose. The lead single "Without You" is the whole method surfacing, split open and sparkling like a geode in a creek bed. Angelic heroics, and nothing less. At the heart is family. Her grandmother Aggie, the light behind "Memory," guiding still. And underneath, the quieter truth the record keeps: none of us are only one person, but a continuum of selves, the ones who shaped us and the ones we have yet to meet. Future you is an ancestor your current self gets to greet. Press play and the same invitation is yours: A few minutes out of time, a place that turns familiar the longer you stay until you surface somewhere new and find it was yours all along. Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

6d6a456e-41a1-44f1-94af-45d0a3a594cb: (Please do not bring infants to the show) A hippie, activist, lesbian, feminist, lawyer, judge’s search for identity & justice. The at times humorous and at times deadly serious show begins when Amy moves to Berkeley in the early 1970’s during second wave feminism. Amy finds her identity as a lesbian feminist, goes to law school to fight for women’s rights, represents coal miners and battered women in Appalachia and returns to California to open a lesbian feminist law practice. She is representing women who had been sexually harassed – pre-Anita Hill – but keeps seeing all sides of things, becomes an administrative judge and starts a law firm to do mediation and impartial investigations of harassment and discrimination. She adopts two children – both biracial – and experiences racism up close and personal. In the meantime, she can’t stop revisiting her first experience with the criminal justice system in 1970 when she accompanied a friend to a rape trial. Her (white) friend had been raped by a (Black) boyfriend. The friend wanted him to get help, rather than serve a decade in prison. This restorative justice solution was not an option. Amy wonders about her role in the verdict and if real justice is possible in an unjust world. Content Advisories: The content of this production includes topics and events that may be triggering to some people including sexual violence/rape, sexual harassment, racism and familial violence.

b0e14365-c5a0-465d-8ae0-07ce9a8cf404: Brown Sturgis & Brown Mark Brown, Patrick Sturgis and Nona Brown. The music of Mark Brown crosses all musical genres – his impressive vocal range and extraordinary counter tenor voice continues to cross boundaries and reach new heights. He is an extension of a musical legacy left by his father, Charles Brown, well known on the New Orleans R&B music scene as part of ‘Sultans of Soul’ vocal duo, which gained much popularity in the 1950’s. A native of New Orleans, Mark has done background vocals for such notables as Bebe Winans, Patti LaBelle, Carlos Santana, Wyclef Jean, and Oleta Adams, to name a few. Vocalist, keyboardist, songwriter, producer, Patrick Sturgis was just 8 years old when he was featured on the front page of a newspaper holding the caption “8- Year-Old Soloist Sparkles Among Stars. Now, some 42 years later, he breaks new ground by satisfying his latent affinity for jazz, particularly American jazz standards reminiscent of the legendary Nat Cole and Ella Fitzgerald. His love affair with music has spanned over three decades and continues to evolve through new collaborations and mediums. Nona Brown - Nona recorded her first CD in 1997 entitled, I’ll Sing My Song. In 2019, after writing music for years, she emerged with her sophomore release, Songs from my Journal Volume 1, ranking #14 and #21 on Billboard Gospel chart in weeks one and two! With the success of Songs from my Journal Volume 1, Nona is excited to share Songs from my Journal Volume 2, scheduled for release on August 22nd. The project features some of the Bay Area’s finest vocalists and musicians performing songs written by Nona. Nona’s music career includes some amazing accomplishments – arranger and background vocalist on the 2022 GRAMMY Award winning Best Children’s Album by Falu A Colorful World and 2022 Telly Award Winner for her “Black Lives Matter” music video co-written with Tony Saunders. As an active member of the music community, Nona previously served as San Francisco Chapter Board Governor, Vice President, and Black Music Collective (BMC) Ambassador before becoming the first black woman to be elected President of the San Francisco Chapter of the Recording Academy. Put it all together and you have one of the most dynamic jazz trios!

CONFUNKSHUN The R&B funk icon, Confunkshun, who has been pleasing fans for over 50 years, is at it again! After the success of Love’s Train being rerecorded by Silk Sonic (Bruno Mars and Anderson Paak) and reaching #1 on the charts, the band’s locomotive has once again rolled out with recent singles Text Me Tomorrow and Smooth from their highly anticipated 2024 spring album release, Smooth Jukebox. Initially known as Project Soul, the R&B funk icon group we now know as Confunkshun has been pleasing fans for over 50 years. Originating in Vallejo, CA, founding member Michael Cooper, along with high school classmates Louis McCall, Karl Fuller, Cedric Martin, Danny Thomas, Paul “Zebulan” Harrell, and newfound talent Felton Pilate, started this unprecedented music journey. Eventually, the group found a home in Memphis in the mid-'70s when they booked a performance backing Stax Recording Artist the Soul Children. Soon, they were recruited as the background band for Rufus Thomas for the Golden Globe-nominated Wattstax Benefit Concert/ Documentary. While in pursuit of a recording contract, the group adopted a new name inspired by the group NiteLiters’ song, Confunkshun. The newly renamed act attracted the attention of Mercury Records, and soon set funkateers around the world on fire with their debut album featuring their first single “Sho'Feels Good To Me.” Confunkshun went on to release a total of 11 albums and eight top ten Billboard hits, including the No. 1 hit single “Ffun”, “Chase Me”, “Shake & Dance”, “Baby I’m Hooked”, and more. Ironically, their biggest hit was an album cut that was never released as a single. The fan favorite, Love’s Train, propelled Confunkshun’s “To the Max” album to Gold Status. But it was 40 years later that supergroup Silk Sonic’s remake of the single took it to #1 on the charts, helping the duo (Bruno Mars & Anderson Paak) win a BET Album of the Year Award. In 2022, Michael Cooper and Felton Pilate were presented with Honorary Doctorates of Humane Letters from the Christian Bible Institute, with Confunkshun member Dr. Ron Moton earning his Ph.D. In 2018, Confunkshun can proudly claim to be one of the only R&B Funk bands with three doctoral members! Dr. Cooper and Dr. Pilate were also honored to receive the Presidential Lifetime Achievement Awards for their lifetime of service through music and more. This prestigious award has been awarded to a select few Americans to recognize over 4,000 hours of extraordinary service. Confunkshun’s current lineup includes three original members, Michael Cooper, Felton Pilate, and Karl Fuller, as well as the talents of Kurt “KC” Clayton, Ron Moton, Aaron Green, Rene Escovedo, and Brian LaTour. Additional support includes the service of long-time road manager and travel agent Steve Sullivan & Master of Ceremonies (Conductor), Clarence Isadore. They continue to mesmerize audiences with magnetic performances on their worldwide 2023 Smooth Jukebox Tour. The group is also a frequent favorite on the Soul Train Cruise and Tom Joyner Cruise, and will soon be on the upcoming Keith Sweat’s Sweatfest in the Dominican Republic. Their contribution to R&B music was recognized in 2014 with the National R&B Music Society Lifetime Achievement Award. Confunkshun’s catalog of hits remains on worldwide radio playlists and in the hearts of their dedicated fans. Con Funk Shun has produced several hits throughout their career. Some of their most popular songs include: 1. Ffun: This song topped the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 2. Shake and Dance with Me: This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1978. 3. Chase Me: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1979. 4. Got to Be Enough: This song reached No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1980. 5. Too Tight: This song peaked at No. 8 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1981. 6. Baby, I’m Hooked (Right into Your Love): This song reached No. 5 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1983. 7. Electric Lady: This song peaked at No. 4 on the U.S. Billboard black singles chart in 1985
f426858f-cd7b-5a09-a0a5-1e674ba18e62: Ella Dair is a NYC-based jazz vocalist. Originally from San Francisco, she started singing at a young age, performing with many Bay Area legends in her aunt’s swing band “Lavay Smith & Her Red Hot Skillet Lickers.” Ella continued her education in music and performance with SFArtsEd, falling in love with the songs of Harold Arlen and Kander & Ebb, among other classics of the Great American Songbook. As a teenager she was a vocal soloist with the youth choir at Glide Memorial, the renowned non-denominational church presided over by civil rights leader Cecil Williams. Ella earned her bachelor’s degree from Bard College, studying anthropology and Latin American studies with a particular interest in ethnomusicology. Her studies broadened her musical tastes and sent her to Mexico City, where she lived post-grad. Ella then moved to New York City, joining the staff at Dizzy’s Club at Jazz At Lincoln Center, where she has been exposed to many of the greatest jazz musicians in the world. On her regular trips to the West Coast Ella performs at The Royal Cuckoo Organ Lounge in San Francisco, an iconic institution that has received rave reviews from the New York Times and the San Francisco Chronicle. At the Royal Cuckoo, Ella has sung with Etta James’ trumpet player Mike Olmos, Lyle Lovett’s alto player Brad Leali, and tenor saxophonist Howard Wiley, a resident Artistic Director at the SFJAZZ Center. Ella covers a range of material, including jazz standards, soul, country and folk tunes. She has a keen eye for unique and beautiful songs, and she continues to work tirelessly on expanding her repertoire, always on the lookout for obscure gems in addition to timeless classics.

0fafea4e-8218-49d1-80ec-1a65619c2cf7: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. With Echoes and Other Songs, Stern brings together an all-star group of musicians, including Christian McBride, Chris Potter, Antonio Sanchez, Richard Bona & Dennis Chambers, for 11 brand-new originals that will captivate and unite guitar and jazz fans of all generations. This is Stern’s first release since the loss of longtime producer and keyboardist Jim Beard (who played on and produced the album), the closure of Stern’s beloved 55 Bar, and his 2016 injury, from which he continues to face physical hurdles. Echoes and Other Songs is a powerhouse document from one of the finest guitarists in jazz history, at a time in his career when he overcame immense physical struggles and experienced profound loss. In the sheer might of these performances, Echoes is a defiant record — not so much a victory lap as a call to arms. Echoes and Other Songs could be considered a loving farewell to Jim Beard, who passed away in March 2024. Beard acted as Stern’s go-to producer for over three decades, and as a favorite keyboardist for even longer. “I’m not exaggerating when I call Jim Beard a genius,” Stern says. “People would say, ‘You should change up your producer — you know, just mix it up.’ And I would say, ‘Why?’ Everybody loved Jim. He was just great at what he did — how he used technology, how he produced, how he mixed.” Stern goes on to describe Beard’s touch as a player. “Incredible.” He pauses. “Ridiculous… Everything he did was perfect. The records he came out with were amazing, but I think he could have done even more as a piano player.” In the end, though, Stern was most affected by Beard’s devotion as a friend. “When I had the blues,” he recalls, “when I felt low and wanted to talk to somebody, he’s one of the people I would reach out to. It would be short, but he would know exactly what I was talking about. It’s a heartbreaker.” Echoes also marks the first album Stern has released as a leader since the West Village jazz haunt 55 Bar closed its doors in 2022, a casualty of the pandemic. Stern’s regular gig there was legendary, enduring and advantageous; it was at 55 where Michael Brecker became interested in hiring the guitarist. His 55 residency also provided a physical-therapy regimen of sorts after Stern broke both of his humerus bones in 2016. He stumbled over construction materials on the street in New York and fell, and the aftermath included potentially career-ending nerve damage that threatened his picking hand. The road to recovery has been long, hard, and ongoing. Stern has had the abiding support of his wife, Leni, to help him, as well as godsends like Dr. Alton Barron, an orthopedic hand specialist recommended by a friend, fellow guitar master Wayne Krantz. Advised by another pal, the drummer Ray Levier, Stern came up with an efficient system for holding his pick, using wig glue and tape. “It was a challenge and a half,” Stern says, “and it still is, sometimes, just to accept it. It gets me really upset and frustrated because I used to play stuff with my fingers. I had to change certain things about my technique.” But Stern pushes on and rises above, as he has throughout his career — like when he rejoined Miles Davis’ band in 1985, having found sobriety. Throughout Echoes, you’d be hard-pressed to find a second in which Stern’s chops are less than sublime. In terms of expressivity, his flatpicking has no limitations. “I’m gonna keep trying with whatever I got,” Stern says. “You know I got to. Because I love it, and love means that some days you hate it; those two sides are on the same coin. But the love is definitely winning out.” Consider Mike Stern’s Echoes and Other Songs his love letter to jazz, to the guitar, to bandstand camaraderie, and to his own undefeated will.
