bd76953f-04f8-4dff-b562-e981701ada7e: UC Berkeley School of Law Professor, Saira Mohamed will discuss her book, WHAT A COUNTRY OWES ITS SOLDIERS . A clarion call to recognize soldiers’ rights, arguing that volunteering to fight and die for one’s country does not mean consenting to exploitation in the process. American leaders endlessly profess their admiration for military service members. But these effusive declarations hardly comport with reality. Soldiers receive shoddy equipment and inadequate medical care; they are ordered to commit crimes and deployed to illegal wars. Such treatment is rarely recognized for what it is: a violation of the duty owed to soldiers by their government. When American service members are injured or killed during training, for example, they and their families are barred from suing the military for negligence or malfeasance. And when the torture of detainees at Abu Ghraib came to light, the subsequent proceedings focused just on low-ranking perpetrators. The psychological harm done to the soldiers themselves by commanders who ordered them to commit torture in the first place went unacknowledged. Copies of the book will be available for purchase from Tally Ho! Books . Doors open at 6:00. Come early to enjoy a cup of tea provided by Peet's. f86dcbff-9e14-45c1-b2f7-a046ed2c6431: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

7c3fb2cd-2fc0-4481-891e-423ec2ac3242: To celebrate the legacy of the late pianist and composer Eddie Palmieri during the week that would have marked his 90th birthday, pianist and SFJAZZ Director of Education Rebeca Mauleón leads a truly all-star Latin jazz orchestra with special guest saxophonist David Sánchez as well as members of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music Latin Jazz Ensemble. A Nuyorican innovator of salsa, Palmieri and his band La Perfecta brought the boogaloo to the Latin jazz sound in the 1960s and infused the modern jazz approach into the music over the course of his monumental career. Mauleón considers Palmieri her “gateway” to serious Latin music and the Cuban icons that guided her own stellar trajectory. For this night, she honors his pioneering body of work and the major developments of the prime eras of his creative life with an ensemble of the greatest names on the local scene including flutist Chloe Scott Jones, saxophonist Melecio Magdaluyo, and Santana percussionist Karl Perazzo along with SFJAZZ Collective saxophonist Sánchez. An artist discovered by Palmieri while still living in Puerto Rico, Sánchez contributed to the maestro’s GRAMMY-winning 2005 Concord Picante release Listen Here! And his KUVO radio series Calienté! with Eddie Palmieri. Personnel: Rebeca Mauleón (piano, vocals, music director); Chloe Scott Jones (flute); Melecio Magdaluyo (baritone sax); Mike Olmos (trumpet); Jeff Cressman (trombone); Obrayan Calderón (trombone); Ernesto Mazar-Kindelán (bass); Karl Perazzo (percussion & vocals); Jesús Diaz (percussion & vocals); Christian Pepín (percussion & vocals); Christelle Durandy (vocals); SPECIAL GUESTS; David Sánchez (tenor saxophone); Members of the San Francisco Conservatory of Music Latin Jazz Ensemble

b13ce3f3-a49f-4bb3-9288-513a9992ce64: “The best pianist of his generation” (Time Magazine), Cyrus Chestnut has established a career as a peerless soloist and torchbearer of the classic piano trio setting. He brings back a favorite of the holiday season, performing Bay Area jazz luminary Vince Guaraldi’s music from the beloved 1965 Charles Schultz animated classic A Charlie Brown Christmas. A standout since his student days at Berklee, Chestnut spent formative years accompanying vocalese legend Jon Hendricks, anchoring the quintessential young lion quintet of Terence Blanchard and Donald Harrison, and touring with Wynton Marsalis. But he credits his early 1990s stint in vocal explorer Betty Carter’s band with radically expanding creative vision, appearing on her landmark 1992 late career Verve release It’s Not About the Melody. Since then, the pianist has racked up dozens of recording credits with jazz’s greatest names and 35 albums as a leader. Chestnut’s performances of Guaraldi’s timeless score to the holiday classic appeared on his all-star 2000 Atlantic Records album Charlie Brown Christmas with the Boys Choir of Harlem and guests including the late Michael Brecker. For this date, Chestnut is joined by a terrific ensemble to help make your spirits bright. Personnel: Cyrus Chestnut (piano); Others TBA

6e8bfe4d-add8-52d1-96b6-925fddea70f8: Meet & Greet Book Signing Only • SF Ferry Plaza Market 11:00 AM PT Food Demo // 11:30 AM PT Book Signing Please join us for a special meet and greet signing event with Florencia Ramirez, following her Foodwise demo at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market. The Kitchen Activist empowers readers to transform everyday meals into joyful, practical actions that reduce waste, restore the planet, and, with a 30-day meal planner and 17 approachable recipes, make the home kitchen a catalyst for meaningful environmental change. The Kitchen Activist is a spirited guide to transforming daily food choices into meaningful environmental action. With warmth, humor, and grounded research, Florencia Ramirez invites readers to reimagine the kitchen as a catalyst for change--after all, the global food system accounts for over 30% of greenhouse gas emissions, and the home kitchen is responsible for 42% of all food waste. From smart meal planning to low-waste shopping and regenerative food sourcing, this book offers practical strategies rooted in environmental science, cultural wisdom, and personal storytelling. Whether you're a seasoned cook or just starting out, The Kitchen Activist meets you where you are, with no judgment, only encouragement to begin making a difference. A follow-up to her award-winning Eat Less Water , this book serves as both a toolkit and a manifesto for anyone ready to connect their plate to the planet. "With its accessible action plans, this will encourage readers to build purposeful action into their everyday routines." —Publisher's Weekly " The Kitchen Activist shows us that food is about more than what’s on your plate. It tells the story of why what we eat matters—and, most of all, how it connects us to nature. Ramirez reminds us that farmers and everyone who works with food are part of that story. Eating, after all, is an act of nature." —Mas Masumoto, third-generation organic farmer and Julia Child Cookbook Award–Winning Author "Like music, food and the art of cooking cross political, environmental, artistic, and cultural barriers. The Kitchen Activist shows how we can be catalysts for positive environmental and social change, beginning right in our own kitchens." —Joan Baez Florencia Ramirez is the author of Eat Less Water: The Solution to Water Shortages Is in the Kitchen. A storyteller at heart and researcher by training, she holds a masters degree in public policy from the University of Chicago. Through writing, research, and lived experience, she explores how the everyday choices we make in our kitchens can become acts of environmental and social change. Her work has been featured on NPR, PBS, KTLA, CBS, KCRW's Good Food, and in the Los Angeles Times.She is the founder and Executive Director of the Pesticide Free Soil Project and the recipient of the Environmental Hero Award and the Gift of Freedom Award in Creative Nonfiction. Married and the mother of three Kitchen Activists, she splits her time between Oxnard, California, and Santa Fe, New Mexico. This event will be hosted by Foodwise with Book Passage at the Ferry Plaza Farmers Market (Foodwise Classroom tent) at the SF Ferry Building. f959278e-c45b-5822-b2e6-effbdf5a6fbd: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

ddfdbd11-5275-4f2b-ae79-4746b453a75b: From beloved Zen teacher and poet Norman Fischer, a new collection of wise and surprising essays that explores what it means to dive fully into spiritual practice and to embody our deepest aspirations in every waking moment. In The Great Road , acclaimed Zen teacher and writer Norman Fischer explores what it means to make everyday life itself a spiritual practice. Inspired by the teachings of legendary Japanese Zen master Eihei Dogen, this wide-ranging collection of essays examines the philosophy of “continuous practice”—the idea that awakening is not separate from ordinary living, but discovered within it. Weaving Buddhist thought with literature, Western philosophy, and deeply personal reflection, Fischer brings Dogen’s teachings into conversation with figures such as Simone Weil and William Wordsworth, while drawing on his own decades among America’s most influential Zen practitioners. The result is a work that moves fluidly between the spiritual, philosophical, and literary, inviting readers into a richer understanding of attention, compassion, and human experience. At once intellectually expansive and deeply intimate, The Great Road offers a timely meditation on how to live with greater presence and meaning in a distracted world— revealing the extraordinary possibilities contained within ordinary life. “A true delight! Norman Fischer has long been one of the best interpreters of Zen Buddhism for the modern world. By illuminating the everyday relevance of Zen's most far-reaching teachings, Fischer gives us a book that is simultaneously thought-provoking, inspiring, and deeply hopeful.” —Adam Frank, author of Light of the Stars: Aliens Worlds and the Fate of the Earth “Repetition is central in Zen practice, offering us an opportunity to see with fresh eyes. That’s the relationship you will want with this book, returning to it again and again for new insights. Norman has given us a deep and accessible book. He invites us into continuous practice and the miracle of presence in everyday life.” —Frank Ostaseski, author of The Five Invitations: Discovering What Death Can Teach Us About Living Fully “The Great Road winds around a single question: what is our human life, really, and what are we supposed to do about it? ... Continuous practice is not particular to Dogen or to Zen. It is the form of any serious human life. As Fischer teaches us, continuous practice means closing the gap between one's deepest aspirations and one's ordinary speaking, thinking, and acting.” —Bonnie Nadzam, author of The Magpie Spoke to Me: How the Stories We Tell Shape Our World NORMAN FISCHER is a Zen teacher, poet, translator, and director of the Everyday Zen Foundation. A beloved figure in the Buddhist world, he is also well-known for his efforts at interreligious dialogue. His numerous books include The World Could Be Otherwise: Imagination and the Bodhisattva Path, What Is Zen?: Plain Talk for a Beginner’s Mind, and Training in Compassion: Zen Teachings on the Practice of Lojong. a8342722-dad8-474d-a72c-59909b0ee066: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

35eb1152-4964-4cbe-bf4f-f1b37e33311b: Every performance by the Count Basie Orchestra is a jazz holiday celebrating a 90-year legacy so bountiful that a month-long residency could only scratch the surface. But a Christmas concert with the Basie Band takes the party to another level, delivering a Santa’s sled full of swing with a program of seasonal standards over an evening show and Sunday matinee. Under the direction of trumpeter Scotty Barnhart since 2013, the orchestra staked a claim to the North Pole with 2015’s chart-topping A Very Swingin’ Basie Christmas!, the first Xmas album ever recorded by the Basie organization. The project featured special guests Ledisi, Johnny Mathis, Ellis Marsalis, and Carmen Bradford, the ebullient jazz and blues singer who continues to tour with the band. The orchestra followed up that celebratory project with a series of excellent albums, scoring GRAMMY Award nominations for 2018’s All About That Basie (with special guests Stevie Wonder, Jon Faddis, and Take 6) and 2022’s Live At Birdland, while winning a GRAMMY with 2023’s Basie Swings the Blues. For swing-loving jazz fans, there’s no better gift than a night with the Basie Orchestra.

3b5b1b22-d73b-5778-aba0-e59923b34d6b: The Bay Area Evolving Ground local group meets regularly at The Alembic to meditate together and explore contemporary Vajrayana. We meet and greet, then start with a short introduction to opening awareness meditation. We sit for 20 minutes, take a break, practice some slow standing meditations together, take a break, and then sit for another 20 minutes. We end with questions and discussion. Opening awareness is a seated meditation leading to vividness and spacious clarity. It is Evolving Ground’s foundational meditation and is a contemporary version of the Dzogchen practice of shi-ne (shamatha in Sanskrit). The movements come from the Sky Realm Series (Nam'khor in Tibetan). These are Dzogchen long-de practices unique to Evolving Ground. They look and feel quite similar to Qi Gong, though they operate on a different principle: discovery of the nonduality of clarity and bliss, through the experience of “tsal”—embodied awareness as non-ordinary sensation. Attendees need no prior experience. There will be plenty of space for questions, reflections, and group exploration of the practices. This meetup is free to attend. Evolving Ground is a global community exploring a transformational path of passionate involvement with the world. Our life-affirming approach empowers creative, effective individuals: people who live with courage, kindness, and grace.
d6359b26-72b1-4168-86c8-0392e4ba25d1: Every performance by the Count Basie Orchestra is a jazz holiday celebrating a 90-year legacy so bountiful that a month-long residency could only scratch the surface. But a Christmas concert with the Basie Band takes the party to another level, delivering a Santa’s sled full of swing with a program of seasonal standards over an evening show and Sunday matinee. Under the direction of trumpeter Scotty Barnhart since 2013, the orchestra staked a claim to the North Pole with 2015’s chart-topping A Very Swingin’ Basie Christmas!, the first Xmas album ever recorded by the Basie organization. The project featured special guests Ledisi, Johnny Mathis, Ellis Marsalis, and Carmen Bradford, the ebullient jazz and blues singer who continues to tour with the band. The orchestra followed up that celebratory project with a series of excellent albums, scoring GRAMMY Award nominations for 2018’s All About That Basie (with special guests Stevie Wonder, Jon Faddis, and Take 6) and 2022’s Live At Birdland, while winning a GRAMMY with 2023’s Basie Swings the Blues. For swing-loving jazz fans, there’s no better gift than a night with the Basie Orchestra.
5f81c681-9467-5cbc-a222-2d5ae0334df2: Butoh is a slow, surreal movement practice rooted in deep listening, imagination, and transformation. In these guided movement meditations, we explore the body as landscape, myth, and memory, softening habitual patterns and awakening new ways of being. No dance experience is needed, only a curiosity and openness to move, feel, and enter the unknown. Each class begins with a gentle opening circle to arrive, ground, and set intention together. We move into a somatic warm-up, awakening sensation, breath, and subtle awareness in the body. From there, you’ll be guided through a butoh-fu score; poetic, image and/or narrative based originally written long-form prompts that invite transformation from the inside out, allowing the body to become something other than itself. We’ll also explore simple butoh exercises that deepen presence, perception, connection, and imaginative embodiment. We close with a soft landing: time to integrate, reflect, and share (if desired), leaving you resourced, expanded, and a little more in touch with the mysterious wisdom built of your body. Arrive however you are, and leave having touched something vast, intimate, and unknowably alive within you.

99bdb572-ae1e-4b1e-bb16-92e5110cb4dc: Jazz pianist bridging musical and artistic genres · Robert Glasper is the leader of a new sonic paradigm with a career that bridges musical and artistic genres. To date, he boasts 5 Grammy wins and 15 nominations across 9 categories, an Emmy Award for his song for Ava Duvernay’s critically hailed documentary “13th” with Common and Karriem Riggins, and a Peabody Award for his Composition of “Mr. Soul!”. His work and accolades bridge all aspects of the music business, from live touring to film scoring, composing and producing. Evolution is his hallmark. Glasper’s breakout crossover album Black Radio changed the face of the genre and set a new expectation for what popular music could be. The album won him the Grammy for Best R&B album and established him as the musician of choice for some of the world’s most iconic artists; notably playing keys throughout Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp A Butterfly, winning another Grammy for the elastic track “These Walls”. The ongoing Black Radio series has since become Glasper’s calling card, upholding a place at the heart of a trailblazing community: from long-time sonic brothers Mos Def and Bilal, to legends including Ledisi, Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, Jill Scott, and Erykah Badu. Glasper’s eternal pursuit to further his sound has been consistent in challenging and transforming his creative horizons across the board. Whether producing a remix album with Kaytranda or as a bandleader, Robert consistently defies the limits of the genre. This is evident in a portfolio that ranges from his acoustic jazz trio, which simultaneously defies and elevates the traditional idiom by uniting it effortlessly with electronics from visionary DJ Jahi Sundance, to August Greene, a collaboration with Common + Karriem Riggins, to R+R=Now, a supergroup at the crossroads of hip-hop and Jazz. In the past year, Robert Glasper has released three diverse albums under his exclusive deal with Apple Music. The holiday album In December features artists such as Cynthia Erivo and Andra Day, while Let Go offers a calming, soulful experience that helps listeners find their center. Code Derivation merges jazz and hip-hop, with each track presented in two versions—one in jazz, and the other flipped by a producer. The track “Say Less” was flipped by Glasper’s son, Riley. Code Derivation has been nominated for a 2025 Grammy in the Best Alternative Jazz Album category. In addition to his musical accomplishments, Glasper hosted Black Radio Backstage for Tidal League, where he interviewed A-list guests like Affion Crockett, Thundercat, and Lalah Hathaway, alongside co-host Jahi Sundance. The festival he curates in Napa, The Black Radio Experience, celebrated its third year, and his legendary month-long residency at the Blue Note NYC marked its sixth season, featuring star-studded appearances from Dave Chappelle, Questlove, Marsha Ambrosius, and Andra Day, both on and off stage. Prior to a knockout 2024, in 2023 Glasper released Black Radio III and Black Radio III Supreme Edition on Loma Vista Records, with features ranging from Jennifer Hudson, Killer Mike, and the late Mac Miller. On screen, he created the original score for Run The World Season 2 and The Best Man television series. With boundless innovation and elite technique as his signature, it’s no surprise that Glasper has an avalanche of accolades, awards, and achievements to his name. Glasper is an artist at the heart of a moment - and a movement - to champion Black music, Black people, and the possibility of a better future. The hip-hop-head-nod ballad is a dedication to just that: the beauty and brilliance of a heritage that is as much Kendrick as it is Coltrane, and which seeks to empower and uplift with every offering. In his own words: “Black lives matter and so does black love; no one wants a life without love, but we have generations of people in our community who haven’t had the tools to actually be in healthy relationships. It seems like people are finally ready to open their eyes to systemic racism in this country, and if we’re going to talk about it, we have to also talk about how it affects our relationships — how we communicate, how we see ourselves, how we treat each other. It’s not always good, even though maybe it could be.” - Robert Glasper

1a3bd9d6-1bd8-5246-8b3e-9d6441ba376c: In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. Through mindful movement, standing and seated practices, breath, and attention to the subtle ways we organize ourselves in space, we'll investigate what allows us to feel both grounded and free. This event happens each week at the Alembic. Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves.. Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition. Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. She teaches students of all ages and abilities, with a particular interest in yoga as a practice for living fully and well over time.
9a477061-d8a6-584b-901d-7ec0131ac37d: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.

de50757a-9d6c-5ee0-88dc-32ee1651c8d0: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is honestly coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. A close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, Relatefulness is an exploration of what is honestly coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. We will notice our relational patterns, emotions, body sensations, and other aspects of our experience. We'll name what we notice and share it with the group to help all of us more clearly see each other and our broader social reality. Relatefulness has value as a complement to traditional meditation practices. By placing awareness on ourselves, in connection with each other, in a collective group, we can: Discover new, more enjoyable ways of relating to our experience and to one another. Take our personal growth insights and test drive them in an interpersonal context. Find healing connection by being deeply seen and understood. This practice tends to bring us to the edge of what we're able to hold in our awareness. Because of this, participants are invited to take care of themselves as needed, either by stepping away from the experience if need be or by leading us into a new way of being with each other. f33e60f8-30fd-4f13-9c64-be95e3d2e908: Plays Duke Ellington’s Nutcracker Suite featuring Tiffany Austin It’s a short walk from the SFJAZZ Center to the War Memorial Opera House, which is where the evening-length ballet The Nutcracker made its North America premiere in the winter of 1944. An immediate sensation, the production unleashed an army of Nutcrackers large and small that march across the country come the holidays, turning Tchaikovsky’s spirited score into an enchanting soundtrack for the season. In 1960, at the urging of Billy Strayhorn, the Duke Ellington Orchestra recorded The Nutcracker Suite (Columbia), a brilliant jazz interpretation of Tchaikovsky’s music. While largely forgotten today, the popular album marked a watershed in one of American music’s most consequent and productive partnerships, as Ellington gave Strayhorn equal billing for the first time on the album’s cover. For bassist, composer, and arranger Marcus Shelby, Ellington and Strayhorn’s Nutcracker Suite arrangements offer an ideal vehicle for his talent-laden New Orchestra, an ensemble he modeled after Ellington’s. Reveling in Tchaikovsky’s enduring melodies, Shelby’s band with guest vocalist Tiffany Austin breathes new life into a singular cultural fusion that gracefully marries the great Russian composer with the orchestral language of two nonpareil jazz innovators, and in addition, features original arrangements of holiday music and black spirituals.
cd72eaa6-8a05-569a-ae14-7c2c2c41a389: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. 30fc6f6a-1a34-5974-a6f1-f44637b206da: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

6142e98b-2052-5c40-97d0-41ab937ac3cd: Every Tuesday morning, the Alembic opens for a half-day of silent meditation practice. This is an unguided silent retreat consisting of three 40-minute meditation periods. There will be no teacher-led instruction during the meditation periods. Participants are invited to bring and engage in their own silent meditation practice. Whether you practice mindfulness, Zen, Vipassana, contemplation, prayer, or another silent form of meditation, all are welcome. The retreat begins promptly at 9:30 AM and concludes at 11:50 AM. Please arrive between 9:15 AM and 9:25 AM to remove your shoes, settle in, and find a seat before the first bell. The morning is divided into three periods of silent meditation: 9:30 AM – 10:10 AM 10:20 AM – 11:00 AM 11:10 AM – 11:50 AM A bell will signal the beginning and end of each meditation period. The meditation hall (Sol) is reserved for silent practice during sitting periods. Between sits, participants may quietly stretch, visit the restroom, or spend time in the tearoom. Conversation is permitted during breaks; however, we encourage participants to keep voices low, as some attendees choose to observe silence throughout the entire morning. You are welcome to leave the meditation hall at any time if needed. If you leave during a meditation period, please wait until the next break before re-entering. We ask that all entrances and exits be as quiet and unobtrusive as possible. This is a “Bring Your Own Silent Meditation” retreat. We provide the structure and the space; you provide your own silent practice. Participants may choose to sit in Sol or engage in quiet movement practice in the tearoom during meditation periods. To minimize disruption, please enter Sol only during the transition periods between sits. If you arrive after a meditation period has begun, you are welcome to practice elsewhere in the Alembic until the next bell. The suggested donation is $10. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. We do ask that all attendees register through the Momence app or via the registration link on the Alembic website. Please note that the retreat ends at 11:50 AM, and we ask all participants to depart by 12:00 PM so that our volunteer teacher and staff may close the space in a timely manner. Thank you for helping us maintain a quiet and supportive environment for practice.
811a14ea-4f28-5341-ae90-ed5d98ed2e94: In this deeply experiential yoga practice, we will explore the dynamic interplay between stability and mobility, strength and relaxation, movement and stillness. This event happens each week at the Alembic. Rather than striving for perfect alignment or mastering difficult poses, we'll approach the practice as an exploration. We'll slow down enough to notice, experiment with different possibilities, and discover how the balance between effort and ease can change our experience of movement — and of ourselves.. Teacher Bio: Vickie Russell Bell has been teaching yoga for more than 30 years, bringing together the precision of alignment-based yoga with a deep curiosity about how we inhabit our bodies, regulate our nervous systems, and move through the world. She is an E-RYT 500 and Certified Yoga Therapist (C-IAYT), and has studied with some of the most respected teachers in the Iyengar-influenced yoga tradition. Her teaching is grounded in the belief that yoga is less about mastering poses than developing a more intimate relationship with ourselves. Her classes invite students to slow down, pay attention, and explore the constantly shifting relationships between stability and mobility, strength and softness, effort and ease. 30835b87-3088-48da-8a1f-a1e39b727c02: Celebrating NYE and his NEW album "Simple Man" · Boney James — A Simple Man Three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and a saxophone voice unmistakably his own, Boney James is still finding new ground. On A Simple Man , his milestone 20th studio album, out October 2 via Concord Records, the multi-platinum saxophonist, composer and producer delivers one of his most personal records. James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four GRAMMY nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s, and in 2024 he became the first artist to score 20 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Recent collaborations have also earned him two Top 10 hits at Adult R&B. For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,” he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.” That clarity runs through the new album. GRAMMY-winning vocalist Ledisi joins him on the warm contemporary R&B duet “I Belong To You,” while acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill appears on “Morocco” and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton guests on the Steely Dan-influenced “Storybook.” James also reimagines Ellington’s “In a Sentimental Mood” over a D’Angelo-inspired groove. James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at 19 and spent his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others before stepping forward with his 1992 debut, Trust . More than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow. On A Simple Man, James’s playing is warmer, deeper, and stronger than ever — and, 20 albums in, he is still making progress. And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man : an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.

c09d4e80-ec93-5804-9a81-2929936dcad7: Embodiment Practices is an invitation to practice giving ourselves permission to arrive fully to where we are, and gently explore movement and stillness to care for our bodies and ourselves. This event happens each week at the Alembic. As an element of self attunement, we will practice making intuitive choices through a lens of self love, meaning that we are each making choices that are nourishing and responsive to ourselves as individuals in that moment. Part of this practice includes being very intentional and explicit about what kinds of choices we might consider, and being curious about how it feels to try them. There will be many options provided throughout, with guidance around how to navigate choice making, including if this is new to you or you are navigating a limitation or injury. There will be a corner of the room set aside in case you’d like to opt out of the facilitated structure and take a moment for yourself to rest. Opening Circle: We'll ground and check-in with whatever feels present for each of us. We get to welcome ourselves to come as we are. Warm Up: We'll do a guided, full-bodied warm up, tuning the instruments of our bodies and attention, giving ourselves time to shake it out, stretch, wiggle, and move through whatever feels stuck. Movements will be simple enough to follow along, giving us a chance to get out of our heads and drop into our bodies, regulating our nervous system. Drawing on contemporary dance and yoga, there will be flow, rhythm, and music. Movement Explorations: We'll explore movements that deepen our connection with our bodies and our intuition, focusing on concepts and areas of the body that can help us settle and release. Meditation: Finally, we'll settle into meditation and rest. Finding stillness might be sitting/standing/lying down and might include cozy props, having eyes open or closed, and suggestions to make yourself comfortable, including allowing some body movement within that quiet space. Please bring clothes you feel comfortable to move in. It’s recommended to bring long sleeves, long pants and socks with you, in case we are moving on the floor. Bring a journal if you’d like. About Suzanne (Zan): With three decades of contemporary/modern dance experience and 15 years of teaching, Suzanne Beahrs guides students in exploring movement as a pathway to deeper connection—with ourselves, our surroundings, and each other. Her classes blend technical training, creative expression, and guidance on being intentional with how we are each practicing. Her movement style was described by The New York Times as “grounded, silken.” In addition to contemporary dance, she is currently heavily influenced by house dance, contact improvisation, and mindfulness practices. She is currently on faculty at Shawl-Anderson Dance Center and teaches around the Bay Area, including ODC, the Berkeley Alembic, and Finnish Hall. Zan has previously taught extensively at Gibney, Elon University, ADF studios, and many more. She has shown her choreography in NY, NC, CA, AZ, MA, and MO, and performed in works by Ishika Seth, Mo Miner, and others. Beyond the studio, Suzanne is a facilitator and has worked as a DEI consultant. She also enjoys exploring writing, visual art, nature, music, and belonging. Education: MFA in Dance, NYU Tisch School of the Arts; BA in Geology, UC Berkeley Learn more about Suzanne, upcoming classes/workshops (contemporary, embodiment, improvisation, contact improvisation and private lessons): IG @suzannebeahrs suzannebeahrs.com

0aca5133-9504-57da-901a-d5b2b863da31: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. ca0063d0-0b7b-41cf-bbab-1211b1c3ec0f: Celebrating NYE and his NEW album "Simple Man" · Boney James — A Simple Man Three decades into a career built on deep groove, melodic instinct and a saxophone voice unmistakably his own, Boney James is still finding new ground. On A Simple Man , his milestone 20th studio album, out October 2 via Concord Records, the multi-platinum saxophonist, composer and producer delivers one of his most personal records. James’ catalog has generated more than two billion on-demand streams in the United States. His honors include four GRAMMY nominations, three NAACP Image Award nominations, four RIAA Gold-certified records and a Soul Train Award. Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists of the 2000s, and in 2024 he became the first artist to score 20 No. 1 singles on the Billboard Smooth Jazz chart. Recent collaborations have also earned him two Top 10 hits at Adult R&B. For James, A Simple Man reflects a growing desire to strip away distraction and focus on what matters most. “As I’ve gotten older, I’ve realized I don’t need a lot to make me happy,” he says. “I love making music and playing my saxophone.” That clarity runs through the new album. GRAMMY-winning vocalist Ledisi joins him on the warm contemporary R&B duet “I Belong To You,” while acclaimed trumpeter Marquis Hill appears on “Morocco” and legendary guitarist Larry Carlton guests on the Steely Dan-influenced “Storybook.” James also reimagines Ellington’s “In a Sentimental Mood” over a D’Angelo-inspired groove. James’ R&B foundation runs deep. He turned professional at 19 and spent his formative years touring with Morris Day, The Isley Brothers, Teena Marie and others before stepping forward with his 1992 debut, Trust . More than three decades later, he remains focused not on preserving a legacy, but on continuing to grow. On A Simple Man, James’s playing is warmer, deeper, and stronger than ever — and, 20 albums in, he is still making progress. And that may be the clearest expression of A Simple Man : an artist who, after more than three decades, knows more clearly than ever what matters.

8d604e5a-1337-4f7a-983e-7d183f5c329e: What better way to welcome the new year than with a blast of Cuban funk, courtesy of the man who invented the genre? Over the past decade, Cimafunk has forged a deeply soulful sound combining funk and hip-hop with rhythms from his native Cuba and other Afro-Caribbean traditions. Living in New Orleans since 2022, the dynamic vocalist dubbed his style “Afro-Cuban funk,” but that convenient label only hints at his breadth. Born in the eastern provincial capital of Pinar del Río, Erik Alejandro Iglesias Rodríguez took the first half of his stage moniker from the cimarróns, escaped slaves who lived in self-sustaining communities in colonial Cuba. He often says that his music is about freedom, and he’s fully embraced an unfettered ethos collaborating with musicians from far and wide. Whether he’s working with Cuban legends Chucho Valdés, Gonzalo Rubalcaba, and Omaru Portuando, British-Jamaican dancehall star Stylo G or the Mothership captain George Clinton himself, Cimafunk has found the universal key to unleashing bodies on the dance floor. Joined by his hard working band La Tribu, he’s recorded a series of celebrated albums, including his latest, the 2025 GRAMMY-nominated Pa' Tu Cuerpa. Returning after his showstopping performance at the 42nd San Francisco Jazz Festival in 2025, Cimafunk kicks off 2027 in spectacular style.

7202a2c2-0fd5-5c69-a6ff-0065176f9a1d: Featuring Nate’ THESOULSANGER & Mirraje · Two powerful women. Two distinctive voices. One soulful night of music. NATE’ THESOULSANGER Some artists find their voice. Nate’ THESOULSANGER inherited hers. Born and raised in Oakland, Nate’ comes from a rich musical heritage as a descendant of the Grammy-winning Gospel Hummingbirds . Raised in a legacy of faith, storytelling, and soul, music was never simply something she discovered it was part of her foundation. An award-winning vocalist, international recording artist, songwriter, producer, actress, event host, and co-founder of SoulGlo Productions, LLC , THESOULSANGER has built a career that refuses to be confined to one genre. Her sound moves through soul, gospel, R&B, hip hop, theater, and beyond , bringing authenticity, power, and unmistakable Oakland soul to every performance. Throughout her career, she has shared stages and studios with artists including Patti LaBelle, Kelly Price, Carlos Santana, MC Hammer, LaRussell , and Grammy-winning producer Narada Michael Walden , with whom she has developed a longstanding creative relationship. Her voice is also woven into Bay Area music history. Nate’ created and recorded the memorable hook for Mac Dre’s “Make You Mine,” a song that became part of his enduring musical legacy. Her credits span radio, film, theater, live production, and recording. A Bay Area Rising Star and Best Vocalist award recipient , she has received KMEL airplay, contributed vocals to the Warner Bros. film The Invasion , and established herself as a trusted creative force both onstage and behind the scenes. At Yoshi’s Oakland , Nate’ has become such a familiar presence as a headliner, host, featured vocalist, producer, and collaborator that she earned the affectionate nickname “Ms. Yoshi’s.” Whether singing, producing, acting, hosting, mentoring, or creating opportunities for others, Nate’ brings the same qualities to every room: authenticity, excellence, soul, and connection. Singer. Songwriter. Producer. Actress. Host. Mentor. Community Builder. Oakland soul in every room she enters. Nate’ THESOULSANGER. The THE is intentional. CHRISTIE “MIRRAJE” MALONE Christie “Mirraje” Malone was born to sing. The daughter of blues musician George “Bluestone” Malone , Mirraje began singing at the age of three and writing songs and poetry by age nine. A gifted singer, songwriter, and natural stage performer, music has been woven into her life from the very beginning. Growing up in Los Angeles, Mirraje’s journey has been shaped by love, loss, perseverance, and an unwavering desire to create. After caring for her mother and experiencing her passing, Mirraje stepped away from singing and writing for four years. The memory of her mother—her greatest inspiration, biggest fan, and loudest cheerleader—eventually reignited her passion and gave her the courage to dream and create again. As she embarked upon her solo career, Mirraje recognized the extraordinary musical journey that had already taken shape. She has shared the stage with celebrated artists including Stevie Wonder, Evelyn “Champagne” King, Morris Day, Zapp, Club Nouveau, Cameo, Sugar Hill Gang, and Klymaxx . Mirraje’s musical influences span genres and generations, with Anita Baker holding a special place among her favorites. Her eclectic love of music allows her to find inspiration in the experiences, thoughts, emotions, and sounds that surround her. Rather than allowing her artistry to be defined by a particular genre or category, Mirraje creates from a place of freedom and authenticity. In her own words: “Life is unpredictable and unique. It should never be defined by genres or categories; nor should our music be. I just do what feels good.” SANG SIS! Together, Nate’ THESOULSANGER and Christie “Mirraje” Malone bring two extraordinary musical journeys to one stage for SANG SIS! —a celebration of powerful women, authentic voices, soulful storytelling, and music that refuses to be put in a box. Rooted in different musical legacies but connected by soul, these two women bring experience, grit, passion, and undeniable vocals to Yoshi’s Oakland for a night designed to make you feel something.

1ece4fbf-9068-42ab-97c8-4653c1236d43: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation, $49 with signed book Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum Interweaving memoir and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson’s latest takes readers along on the journeys that have happened before and those that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and his men said goodbye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they would try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott’s second-in-command decided to take an impromptu sled trip. Chronicled by zoological assistant Apsley Cherry-Garrard, this side trip became The Worst Journey in the World, one of the best adventure books ever written. Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard’s book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as preparation for a research trip to Antarctica for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane, and followed in their ill-fated footsteps. Doors at 7:00 PM.
405d44f2-02ce-5fea-8c3f-33f22fb9d33f: One of the world’s preeminent jazz innovators, trombonist and seashellist Steve Turre, has consistently won both the Readers’ and Critics’ polls in JazzTimes, Downbeat, and Jazziz for Best Trombone and for Best Miscellaneous Instrumentalist (shells). Turre was born to Mexican-American parents and grew up in the San Francisco Bay Area, where he absorbed daily doses of mariachi, blues, and jazz. While attending Sacramento State University, he joined the Escovedo Brothers salsa band, which began his career-long involvement with that genre. In 1972, Steve Turre’s career picked up momentum when Ray Charles hired him to go on tour. A year later, Turre’s mentor Woody Shaw brought him into Art Blakey’s Jazz Messengers. After his tenure with Blakey, Turre went on to work with a diverse list of musicians from the jazz, Latin, and pop worlds, including Dizzy Gillespie, McCoy Tyner, J.J. Johnson, Herbie Hancock, Lester Bowie, Tito Puente, Mongo Santamaria, Van Morrison, Pharoah Sanders, Horace Silver, Max Roach, and Rahsaan Roland Kirk. The latter introduced a hum to the seashell as an instrument. Soon after that, while touring in Mexico City with Woody Shaw, Turre’s relatives informed him that his ancestors similarly played the shells. Since then, Turre has incorporated seashells into his diverse musical style. In addition to performing as a member of the Saturday Night Live Band since 1984, Turre leads several different ensembles. Sanctified Shells utilizes the seashell in a larger context, transforming his horn section into a “shell choir”. Turre’s Spring 1999 Verve release, Lotus Flower, showcases his Sextet With Strings. The recording explores many great standards and original compositions arranged by Turre for a unique instrumentation of trombone and shells, violin, cello, piano, bass, and drums. Turre’s quartet and quintet provide a setting based in tradition and stretching the limits conceptually and stylistically. In the Summer of 2000, Telarc released In the Spur of the Moment. This recording features Steve with three different quartets, each with a different and distinct master pianist: Ray Charles, Chucho Valdes, and Stephen Scott. Turre’s self-titled Verve release pioneers a unique artistic vision, drawing upon jazz, Afro-Cuban, and Brazilian sources. This innovative recording also features Cassandra Wilson, Randy Brecker, Graciela, Mongo Santamaria, and J.J. Johnson. Previously, Turre recorded Right There and Rhythm Within, featuring Herbie Hancock, Jon Faddis, Pharoah Sanders, and Sanctified Shells, on Verve’s subsidiary label, Antilles. Steve Turre continually evolves as a musician and arranger. He has a strong command of all musical genres, and when it comes to his distinct brand of jazz, he always keeps one foot in the past and one in the future.

3082bff4-bc58-557a-be12-b631c3cdfe0f: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. 971811a3-3e45-541b-9349-3fe0675d7341: Award-winning guitar virtuoso and blues singer · " One of the most prodigious and gifted electric bluesmen on the planet...a deeply soulful singer and incendiary guitarist [with] a seemingly endless penchant for invention." –AllMusic "Smoking songs and heavy-hitting guitar full of fire and passion...Montoya’s rough-edged voice is filled with feeling. Bluesy, powerful and unpredictable...[It]really gets the blood flowing." –Blues Music Magazine "Montoya is a show-stopper...heartfelt singing and merciless guitar with a wicked icy burn. He is one of the truly gifted blues artists of his generation." –Living Blues “’Just play what you feel, be real about it, and enjoy yourself.’ That’s what Albert Collins taught me,” says the award-winning guitar virtuoso and soul-deep singer Coco Montoya. The self-taught, left-handed Montoya mastered his craft under Collins’ tutelage. Incorporating lessons learned from his mentors, the iconic Collins (for whom he originally drummed), and UK legend John Mayall, Montoya puts his own stamp on every song he performs. Since his first solo album in 1995 (which won him the Blues Music Award for Best New Artist), Montoya’s endlessly inventive guitar work and passionate, hard-hitting vocals have kept him at the top of the blues world. With his new Alligator Records album, Writing On The Wall (his sixth for the label), Montoya delivers what he is already calling one of the best records he’s ever made. For the very first time on Alligator, he decided to bring his road-tested band—noted keyboardist and songwriter Jeff Paris (Keb’ Mo’, Bill Withers), bassist Nathan Brown, and drummer Rena Beavers—into the studio with him. Between the camaraderie of the long-time bandmates and the sheer talent of all involved, the results have left Coco, in his words, “over the moon.” Produced by Grammy Award-winner Tony Braunagel (Bonnie Raitt, Taj Mahal) and co-produced by Jeff Paris, Writing On The Wall is a tour-de-force of memorable, hook-filled songs, sung with passion and fueled by equally memorable, top-shelf musicianship. The 13 tracks include five written or co-written by Montoya. The set opens with a signature, career-defining performance of the soul-baring I Was Wrong , written for Coco by songwriter Dave Steen. From the blistering Save It For The Next Fool to the enjoy now/pay later philosophy of Jeff Paris’ (I’d Rather Feel) Bad About Doin’ It to the riveting reinvention of Lonnie Mack’s Stop , Montoya delivers each song with heart-pounding emotion. Special guest Lee Roy Parnell adds his well-seasoned slide guitar to the smoldering A Chip And A Chair . And Coco’s friend, guitarist Ronnie Baker Brooks (son of late Alligator star Lonnie Brooks), joins in for some good-natured fun on the droll Baby, You’re A Drag and adds his blistering playing to the searing cover of Bobby Bland’s You Got Me. “I am so proud of this one,” Montoya says of Writing On The Wall . “We recorded in Jeff Paris’ studio, and everything just gelled together. And the band inspired me; they all gave extra effort at every turn. Jeff, Nathan and Rena played so great, they ended up making me play even harder. They made me sound better than I am!” Henry “Coco” Montoya was born in Santa Monica, California, on October 2, 1951, and raised in a working-class family. Growing up, Coco immersed himself in his parents’ record collection. He listened to big band jazz, salsa, doo-wop and rock ‘n’ roll. His first love was drums; he acquired a kit at age 11. He got a guitar two years later. “I’m sure the Beatles had something to do with this,” Montoya recalls. “I wanted to make notes as well as beats.” But guitar was his secondary instrument. Montoya turned his love of drumming into his profession, playing in a number of area rock bands while still in his teens and becoming an in-demand drummer. In 1969, Montoya saw Albert King opening a Creedence Clearwater Revival/Iron Butterfly concert at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles. He was transformed. “After King got done playing,” says Montoya, “my life was changed. When he played, the music went right into my soul. It grabbed me so emotionally that I had tears welling up in my eyes. Nothing had ever affected me to this level. He showed me what music and playing the blues were all about. I knew that was what I wanted to do.” The next chapter of Montoya’s story was kick-started by a chance meeting in the mid-1970s with legendary bluesman Albert Collins. Montoya says, “Albert was coming through Los Angeles and needed to borrow my drum set, which I left at the club where he was going to be playing. I went down to see his show that night, and it just tore my head off. The thing that I had seen and felt with Albert King came pouring back on me when I saw Albert Collins.” A short time later, Collins hired Montoya as his band’s drummer. With Albert mentoring Coco on the guitar during the band’s downtime, Coco soon became Collins’ second guitarist. “We’d sit in hotel rooms for hours and play guitar,” remembers Montoya. “He’d play that beautiful rhythm of his and just have me play along. He was always saying, ‘Don’t think about it, just feel it.’ He was like a father to me,” says Coco, who often slept at Collins’ home. When Collins declared Montoya his “son,” it was the highest praise and affection he could offer. In return, Montoya learned everything he could from the legendary Master of the Telecaster. Needing a more regular paycheck, Montoya left Collins’ band after two years and took a job tending bar, jamming on weekends at Los Angeles clubs. One day, legendary British musician John Mayall heard Coco playing Otis Rush’s All Your Love (I Miss Loving) onstage. Soon after, Mayall called on Montoya to join his famous Bluesbreakers. Filling the shoes of previous Bluesbreakers guitarists Eric Clapton, Peter Green and Mick Taylor would not be easy, but Montoya knew he could not pass up the opportunity to play with another legend. For the next ten years he toured the world and recorded with Mayall on seven albums, soaking up the experience of life on the road and in the recording studio. Montoya’s recorded debut as a bandleader came with 1995’s Gotta Mind To Travel (originally on Silvertone Records in England and later issued in the USA on Blind Pig Records). The album became an instant fan favorite. Blues enthusiasts, radio programmers, and critics sent praise from all corners. The album immediately made it clear that Montoya ranked among the best players on the contemporary scene. Two more Blind Pig albums followed, and Coco was well on his way. In 2000, Montoya’s Alligator debut, Suspicion , quickly became the best-selling album of his career, earning regular radio airplay on over 120 stations nationwide. Montoya’s fan base exploded. After two more highly successful and massively popular Alligator releases—2002’s Can’t Look Back and 2007’s Dirty Deal —Montoya signed with Ruf Records, cutting both a live and a studio album. Returning to Alligator with 2017’s Hard Truth and 2019’s Coming In Hot , the guitar master continued to blaze his trail. “Montoya unleashes one career-topping performance after another,” declared the UK’s Blues Matters . Still an indefatigable road warrior, Montoya continues to tour virtually nonstop, bringing audiences to their feet from New York to New Orleans to Chicago to San Francisco. Across the globe, he’s performed in countries including Australia, Belgium, Switzerland, Germany, Norway, England, Brazil, Argentina, Spain, Mexico, Ecuador, Italy, Poland, Russia, the Czech Republic and Canada. Now, with the dynamic Writing On The Wall and a tour calendar busting at the seams, Coco Montoya is as excited as he’s ever been to perform the new songs live with his burning-hot band. Montoya’s well-earned reputation as an eye-popping live performer precedes him. Vintage Guitar states, “Coco keeps getting better and better. He plays with fire and passion rarely seen in this day and age.” Billboard declares, “In a world of blues guitar pretenders, Coco Montoya is the real McCoy. He exudes power and authenticity. Be prepared to get scorched by the real thing.”

299dce88-cfbf-4843-85cf-3a33368e68e4: With his finely etched features and piercing green eyes, trumpeter Chris Botti combines matinee idol looks with the simmering lyricism of an expert balladeer” (The Mercury News). A trumpeter with a sumptuous, enveloping tone, fluent phrasing, and sense of space, Botti became a masterly musician equally at home in the realms of jazz and pop. He honed his craft performing and recording with stars like Frank Sinatra, Buddy Rich, Paul Simon, Joni Mitchell, and Sting, who featured him on his Brand New Day tour and who was one the stellar artists on Botti’s chart-topping 2009 album Live in Boston. Botti’s 2012 CD Impressions won the GRAMMY for Best Pop Instrumental Album, and he made his Blue Note Records debut in 2023 with Vol. 1, his first new recording in over a decade. Stepping back from the lush orchestral arrangements of his recent work, Botti returns to an intimate, small group dynamic on the album, focusing on classic standards like “Old Folks,” “Blue in Green,” “Bewitched, Bothered, and Bewildered,” and “Someday My Prince Will Come,” among others. Produced by 16-time GRAMMY-winner David Foster, Vol. 1 features performances by violinist Joshua Bell, pianist Taylor Eigsti, guitarist Gilad Hekselman, and drummer Vinnie Colaiuta. Botti’s SFJAZZ shows have become a New Years tradition and always sell out in advance. Personnel: Chris Botti (trumpet); Others TBA
