d7f9ebb5-8ba3-5b65-b945-fc2f7e1e5abf: In Midnight's Daughter by Sarita Sarvate, named after a freedom fighter, Aruna must ultimately fight for her own liberation in this deeply moving memoir of resilience, love, and self-discovery. Although the country was free, its daughters were not. “A thoroughly satisfying account of one spirited woman.” — Molly Giles, author of Life Span Winner of the 2025 International Voices in Creative Nonfiction Competition On Republic Day, 1960, young Aruna stands before her middle school classmates delivering a speech in a newly independent India. At home awaits a family full of promise: a fiercely intelligent mother pursuing her BA, a playful younger brother, and a father who encourages his daughter to find her voice, echoing Jawaharlal Nehru’s words spoken at India’s independence: “At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom.” But beneath the surface, the family is quietly unraveling. When Aruna is thirteen, her mother suffers a devastating nervous breakdown, forcing Aruna into the role of caretaker while she continues to excel academically. Pressured by societal expectations, she enters an arranged marriage that soon turns disastrous. Determined to reclaim her future, she escapes to graduate school in Berkeley, endures the stigma of divorce, and eventually falls in love with an Englishman living in New Zealand. Crossing continents and cultures, Sarvate traces one woman’s search for identity, belonging, and freedom. Midnight’s Daughter is both an intimate personal story and a powerful meditation on racism, colonialism, motherhood, and the patriarchal forces surrounding women’s lives—including the hidden roots of her mother’s mental illness. Named after a freedom fighter, Aruna must ultimately fight for her own liberation in this deeply moving memoir of resilience, love, and self-discovery. Midnight’s Daughter is a thoroughly satisfying account of one spirited woman’s resistance to what she calls “the tyranny of patriarchy and the demands of Hindu womanhood”—although, as we follow Sarvate from her unhappy childhood in Nagpur, India, to her trials and tribulations in Berkeley, Hawaii, and New Zealand, we begin to see that perhaps it is not just “Hindu womanhood” that is the problem, but womanhood itself. Sarvate often references Jane Eyre in recounting her life story, and the comparison is appropriate—both are modest, direct, and deserving survivors with one major difference: Jane Eyre never yearned to belt Blue Bayou out in a nightclub and if Sarvate hasn’t fulfilled that delightful ambition yet I’m hoping she soon will. - Molly Giles, author of LIFE SPAN, a memoir in flash Her meticulous eye for detail woven together with graceful prose made me feel like an intruder into the most intimate moments of Sarita's life which she bravely shares to transcend her aloneness. - Sandy Close, Director Emeritus, American Community Media, and winner of the MacArthur “Genius Grant.” Midnight's Daughter traces one woman's remarkable journey across continents and through eras. Sarvate escapes poverty, patriarchy and the long shadow of mental illness, carrying with her a complexity of histories and cultures as she forges her identity. She fears becoming a "fallen woman," a fate that has claimed so many girls from her youth, but instead she becomes a free woman, a Midnight's Daughter -- moving from the old world to the new, finally finding her voice and 'giving her soul utterance,' as Jawaharlal Nehru, the freedom fighter against British colonial rule, invoked. - Elizabeth Stix, author of Things I Want Back from You Sarita Sarvate was raised in India and came to the U.S. to attend graduate school at U.C. Berkeley. Her award-winning opinions have been published in the Los Angeles Times, the San Jose Mercury News, the Baltimore Sun, the San Francisco Examiner, and Salon.com. She has aired commentaries on NPR and its affiliate KQED. For twenty-five years, she wrote the Last Word column for India Currents, a magazine catering to the Indian diaspora. She is a member of the San Francisco Writers Grotto and an alumna of the Hedgebrook Writers Residency and the Voices of our Nation Foundation. Please visit www.saritasarvate.com . 291c3026-b489-5875-aaf4-298b4491e030: In a refugee camp of half a million people, Frank undertakes a quixotic mission to teach traumatized orphans baseball, raising the questions: How do you hold on to fair play, honesty, and respect for common ground in an increasingly cynical, callous, and power-driven world? Can healing happen—for an individual, a community, or a country—in the face of abysmal violence, and if so, how? Could you throw yourself away? Frank Matter asks himself this question as he boards a one-way flight to Syria. He might as well ask: Can you find your life by losing it? In spring 2016, after a run of personal sorrows, Frank, a lapsed Catholic clinging to one last scrap of faith, undertakes a dangerous journey to his family's village of origin outside Damascus on a two-pronged rescue mission. He hopes to scoop up his deaf cousin Dayzi, whom he has loved since they were young, and escape with her to America, but their progress is halted by the terror and upheaval of the Syrian Civil War. In the refugee camp of half a million people where they find themselves, Frank takes on another quixotic mission: to teach a deeply traumatized collection of orphans the game of American baseball. Everything and everyone resists it. Frank's obsession will not only test his resolve and bedrock sense of reality. It will risk his life and the lives of everyone he is trying to help. It will transform them. He and his adoptive family will wonder: How do you hold on to fair play, honesty, and respect for common ground in an increasingly cynical, callous, and power-driven world? Can healing happen--for an individual, a community, a country--in the face of abysmal violence, and if so, how? Gregory Orfalea was born and raised in Los Angeles and is the author or editor of eleven books, including Journey to the Sun: Junipero Serra’s Dream and the Founding of California (Scribner) and the just-released novel Wonder + Shame. He has taught writing and literature at the Claremont Colleges, Westmont College, Santa Barbara City College, and his alma mater, Georgetown University, among others. His collection of memoirs, Angeleno Days, was a finalist for the PEN USA Prize and won the Arab American Book Award. He lives within blocks of sons and granddaughters in Santa Barbara. A trumpeter with a sumptuous, enveloping tone, fluent phrasing, and sense of space, Botti became a masterly musician equally at home in the realms of jazz and pop. Botti’s 2012 CD Impressions won the GRAMMY for Best Pop Instrumental Album, and he made his Blue Note Records debut in 2023 with Vol. 1, his first new recording in over a decade. Stepping back from the lush orchestral arrangements of his recent work, Botti returns to an intimate, small group dynamic on the album, focusing on classic standards like “Old Folks,” “Blue in Green,” “Bewitched, Bothered, and Bewildered,” and “Someday My Prince Will Come,” among others. Produced by 16-time GRAMMY-winner David Foster, Vol. 1 features performances by violinist Joshua Bell, pianist Taylor Eigsti, guitarist Gilad Hekselman, and drummer Vinnie Colaiuta. 6ad89f76-c961-55a9-afaf-7454691a4355: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

b3424f67-0c50-51a5-8d45-5d5d0f070cc4: Veteran China expert and journalist Orville Schell recounts the extraordinary investigation that uncovered China's prison labor network, the personal cost of reporting the truth, and the enduring global implications of forced labor and political intimidation. More than three decades before forced labor, supply chain transparency, and Chinese government influence became front-page international issues, China scholar Orville Schell helped expose one of the Chinese Communist Party's most closely guarded secrets. In Inside China's Secret Prisons: An Undercover Expose and its Lasting Legacy (Columbia University Press; September 1, 2026), Schell delivers the first behind-the-scenes account of the landmark 1991 60 Minutes investigation that revealed China's vast “reform through labor” prison system and documented how prison-made goods were illegally entering the United States disguised as legitimate exports. The investigation took Schell and his colleagues deep inside China's hidden penal colonies, where they worked alongside a former political prisoner and used hidden cameras to document forced labor inside prison factories. In one of the investigation's most startling moments, Chinese prison officials openly attempted to sell prison-made products to CBS journalists posing as American buyers. But the book reveals far more than the mechanics of an extraordinary investigative report. For the first time, Schell explains why he chose not to publish his original account of the investigation for The New Yorker. Concerned that the Chinese government could retaliate against his Chinese-born wife, her family, their friends, and even jeopardize his own ability to continue reporting from China, Schell made the painful decision to remain silent—offering a rare and deeply personal examination of how authoritarian governments can foster self-censorship far beyond their own borders. Today, as allegations of forced labor involving Uyghur Muslims, concerns over global supply chains, and escalating tensions between the United States and China dominate international headlines, Schell's account provides timely historical context for issues that continue to shape global politics, commerce, and human rights. “History has a way of resurfacing,” says Schell. “The questions we confronted more than 30 years ago about forced labor, accountability, economic dependence, and the risks of telling uncomfortable truths have only become more urgent.” More than a work of investigative journalism, Inside China's Secret Prisons is a firsthand account of the ethical dilemmas faced by reporters working under authoritarian regimes, the hidden costs of exposing state-sponsored abuses, and the enduring struggle between truth and political intimidation. “The author’s craft and clarity of structure stem entirely from his passion for truth and his unwavering dedication to pursuing it." -- Ai Weiwei, artist, activist, and author of 1000 Years of Joys and Sorrows: A Memoir “The courage, resourcefulness, and persistence of the main characters in this international political thriller are nothing short of inspiring." -- Minxin Pei, author of The Broken China Dream: How Reform Revived Totalitarianism “Adventure story, love story, psychological thriller, reflection on repression and dissent, and object lesson in how to deal with China―this book has it all, and it's all true." -- Andrew J. Nathan, Class of 1919 Professor of Political Science, Columbia University ORVILLE SCHELL is one of America's foremost experts on China, an award-winning journalist, author, and longtime China analyst. He has written extensively about modern China and has reported on the country for decades, including his groundbreaking investigative work for CBS News's 60 Minutes . Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. Rhae Lynn Barnes - Darkology DARKOLOGY, from Princeton historian Rhae Lynn Barnes, meticulously unravels the complex, subterranean, and all–too–often expunged history of blackface in American society— documenting how it shaped our country’s politics, economics, and culture for nearly two centuries. The product of decades of archival research into networks of white supremacists, local and national, who’ve used blackface to amass and maintain power, DARKOLOGY provokes a necessary reckoning with America’s past. By 1830, blackface, which caricatured ex–slaves for their supposed subservience and happy demeanor, had become a venomous cultural export into all corners of the country. Blackface theater soon segued into everyday amateur shows, with minstrelsy proliferating in Elks Clubs, churches, universities, and schools during Jim Crow, whose name derives from the practice’s founding character. Beloved by presidents including FDR and Gerald Ford, blackface saturated twentieth–century America, permeating U.S. military bases abroad and World War II Japanese American internment camps as an “Americanization” tool. Despite a 1950s backlash led by Black mothers protesting public school performances, 1960s college students from California to Vermont aggressively challenged legal bans and continued holding amateur shows for decades longer— shows whose construction, circulation, and handing down of racist stereotypes intergenerationally continue to impact our society today. With its gripping writing and penetrating archival research, DARKOLOGY is a landmark work of cultural and social history—and an essential tool, as Barnes writes, to negate minstrelsy’s power and weight on our country’s soul. “Essential . . . [Barnes’] immensely readable work covers more than a hundred years of white America’s embrace of this sordid form of entertainment . . . An important and necessarily uncomfortable work on a disturbing legacy.” —Kirkus Reviews starred review “The scope and tenacity of Barnes’ research is impressive, as she reveals blackface as a cultural institution supported by white officials at every level of government . . . Darkology tells the story of a genre that pervaded American culture and politics across decades, taking care along the way to highlight the voices of those who resisted.” —Booklist “In Darkology, Rhae Lynn Barnes shines an unsparing spotlight on blackface. . . . Through fastidious research and the painstaking pursuit of archives and documents hidden from historians for decades, Barnes has written nothing short of an exposé of the structural racism that undergirds the very foundations on which America is built.” —Henry Louis Gates, Jr., Harvard University Rhae Lynn Barnes is Assistant Professor of American Cultural History at Princeton University and the nationally bestselling author of "Darkology: Blackface and the American Way of Entertainment" (2026) (Liveright/W.W. Norton). _____________________________________________________ David M. Henkin - Out of the Ballpark From America's Pastime to a global phenomenon--the life of the spectacular game as it is played and celebrated in communities around the world All over the world, masses of people watch, follow, document, and obsess over baseball. Everything remarkable about the impact of baseball derives from the game's history and cultural status as events that draw people together in these ways. Understanding baseball as a cultural phenomenon is therefore less a matter of mastering the vocabulary of the game or merely recollecting its iconic stadiums, players, and stats. While all those details compel insiders and inspire fans, baseball's peculiar and persistent appeal can only be understood by adopting a wider lens. It requires reckoning with the history of structured competition. The classic backyard game of catch between a father and son draws meaning from its associations with the organized sport and its history. The challenge lies less in finding one perfect spot to look, but rather in identifying the many different places where baseball has accumulated significance. Out of the Ballpark reconsiders the character, meaning, and delights of the game by exploring both baseball's unusual features and the sport's many resonances with other aspects of modern life. To this end, it abandons several assumptions and mythologies that underlie most approaches to histories of baseball: that it is unique among sports and fundamentally different from other kinds of entertainment; that it is specific to the United States; that it has changed fundamentally in recent years; and that the keys to understanding it lie primarily in examining what happens on the field of play. Instead, David M. Henkin moves across time and space to examine baseball's history since the nineteenth century and beyond US borders. He takes readers inside the structures of clubs and leagues, interprets the sacred scripture of rulebooks, and illuminates some of baseball's rites and rituals that are often associated with honor and manhood. He charts baseball's significance along the routes of American and Japanese imperial expansion and the shifting maps of race and ethnicity in the US. Baseball is found at negotiating tables that pit capital against labor and in pivotal moments in the history of mass media. Here, we are shown how baseball might offer a complex and capacious space for thinking about such things as spectatorship, success, community, order, and contingency in the modern world. David M. Henkin is Professor of History at the University of California, Berkeley, where he has taught courses on society and culture in nineteenth-century America for close to three decades. He is the author of City Reading (1998); The Postal Age (2006); The Week (2021); and (with Rebecca McLennan) Becoming America (2022). Rhae Lynn Barnes - photo courtesy of the publicist; David M. 73292c88-8ad9-5ee6-8bea-a66e12aae601: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

73a9c9ca-370d-4b9f-8734-d7e2c38ccdf7: One of the most dynamic forces in contemporary blues · Grace. Power. Drive. Meet the Queen of the Pack Some guitar players play the blues. Ana Popovic sets it on fire. An award-winning guitarist, singer, songwriter, and bandleader, Ana Popovic is a force of nature onstage. Blending smoking electric funk, fiery slide guitar, soulful vocals, jazz-infused instrumentals, and deep blues grooves, she has created a sound that is unmistakably her own. For more than 25 years, Popovic has relentlessly toured the world, continually pushing the boundaries of contemporary blues. Her music never stands still. She bends genres, challenges expectations, and reinvents herself with every record, while remaining deeply connected to the power, emotion, and freedom of the guitar. A ten-time Blues Music Award nominee, Popovic was the only female guitarist selected for the 2014-2018 Experience Hendrix all-star lineup, sharing the stage with legendary artists including Buddy Guy, Eric Johnson, and Kenny Wayne Shepherd. She has appeared on the covers of Vintage Guitar and Guitar Player and has shared headlining stages with B.B. King, Joe Bonamassa, Gary Clark Jr., Robben Ford, Keb' Mo', and many other major artists. Bruce Springsteen summed up her musicianship simply: "One helluva guitar player." Popovic's recordings have earned widespread critical and commercial recognition. Can You Stand the Heat and Unconditional were named Pick of the Week by USA Today and featured by NPR Music. Her album POWER reached #1 on the Billboard Blues Albums chart, marking another major milestone in her career. Albums including Like It On Top, Trilogy, Can You Stand the Heat, Unconditional, and Dance to the Rhythm have all appeared among Billboard's best-selling blues albums. Her international profile has also been reflected in numerous magazine covers, including Vintage Guitar (US), Guitar Player Gear Guide (US), Blues Music Magazine (US), Blues Magazine (France), American Blues Scene (US), and Blues Matters! (UK), among many others. POWER & FANTASTAFUNK POWER is a record about unity, friendship, resilience, and the strength we find in one another. Its striking cover-two hands, one black and one white, holding on to each other-captures the album's central message: connection and collective strength have the power to move the world forward. Recorded during one of the most challenging periods of Ana's life, POWER became a deeply personal expression of survival and a renewed faith in the transformative power of music. That same spirit inspired Popovic's FANTASTAFUNK, an explosive 11-piece big band launched in 2023. Bringing together funk, gospel, soul, and blues, FANTASTAFUNK expands her guitar-driven sound into a full-scale, high-energy live experience designed for major festival stages. DANCE TO THE RHYTHM In 2025, Popovic released DANCE TO THE RHYTHM, a vibrant celebration of perseverance, joy, gratitude, and a renewed love of life. Created with longtime collaborator Buthel, the ten-track album blends funk, soul, blues, and gospel into what Popovic calls her "ever-evolving gumbo of sound." Tracks such as "Dance to the Rhythm" and "Sho Nuff" push the electric guitar into infectious, dance-driven grooves, while songs including "Dwell on the Feeling" and "Sisters and Brothers" explore inclusiveness, resilience, faith, love, and the powerful connection between artist and audience. As Popovic puts it: "POWER was about survival. DANCE is about celebrating life-a second chance." Popovic writes for the stage-and that is where her music truly comes alive. a049042a-8ee0-5d0b-b8ad-02fede6b6cc5: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

d0646472-56a2-55bb-ae73-6d7b9639fc24: One of the world’s finest acoustic guitarists · Andy McKee is one of the world’s finest acoustic guitarists, and it’s evident from the accolades he’s received throughout his career. It’s his youthful energy, attention to song structure and melodic content that elevates him above the rest. After nearly a decade without releasing new studio recordings, McKee returns with his six-track EP, Symbol, out Friday, September 17 on Mythmaker Records in conjunction with Cruzen Street Records. “These are my interpretations of tunes that really inspired me,” says McKee. “I wanted to give listeners a chance to hear what I hear when I listen to this music. I also wanted to branch out a bit and include music that isn’t originally for acoustic guitar.” While Symbol is a collection of inspired renditions, they are important song choices; artists that deeply influence McKee and songs that connect to his musical past. He pulls from the catalogues of greats like Michael Hedges, Preston Reed, Billy McLaughlin, and Prince. There’s “Ragamuffin,” the EP’s lead single, which is a nod to one of McKee’s biggest influences, Michael Hedges. McKee notes that “Michael was not only a revolutionary guitarist on the technical side, his ability to compose for solo guitar was also genius. Most importantly though, he was able to search inside of himself and consistently pull up very human and evocative themes that made him a true artist. I’ll always be grateful for his music.” One track that might catch fans by surprise on Symbol is McKee’s gorgeous rendition of Prince’s “Purple Rain.” In 2012, McKee played alongside Prince in his band on the “Welcome 2 Australia” tour, with the song being one of the setlist highlights. “I had originally come up with the ‘Purple Rain’ arrangement to open the shows with while I was on tour with Prince in Australia,” recalls McKee. “I have played it occasionally since then while touring and figured I should finally get a recording of it down. One thing that I learned from Prince while we were on the road is that we both really admire Joni Mitchell. I used that as a reference when trying to describe what I do. Although some of what I do on the guitar is technically demanding, I don’t ever really want that to overshadow the music.” Another standout from Symbol is McKee’s take on “Chattanooga” by acclaimed guitarist Preston Reed. “In my opinion, ‘Chattanooga’ by Preston Reed is one of the finest fingerstyle guitar pieces ever written,” saysMcKee. “It’s just loaded with texture, harmony, percussion, and melody. I love the key changes and chromaticism between some of the chords. This tune really inspired me a lot.” McKee, like many, was infatuated with the Rocky IV soundtrack, specifically the Vince DiCola compositions “War” and “Training Montage.” For Symbol, McKee and DiCola joined forces to craft “Rocky IV Medley.” “That was about as surreal as it gets for me,” says McKee. “I became a fan of Vince’s work when I was six years old, and I bought the soundtrack to the film on cassette. I used to listen to it all the time on my Sony Walkman, and I really found that my favorite tunes were the instrumental tracks, which were “War” and “Training Montage” from Vince. Those tunes awakened my mind to the possibility of being moved by music with no words. To be able to recreate those tunes with the electric guitar and play with Vince is really something I could never have dreamed of.” Andy McKee entertains both the eye and the ear as he magically transforms the steel string guitar into a full orchestra via his use of altered tunings, tapping, partial capos, percussive hits and a signature two-handed technique. McKee’s crossover success has helped him to achieve millions upon millions of YouTube viewers, underscoring his emergence as one of today’s most unique and influential artists. His song “Drifting” became one of the first YouTube viral videos with almost 60 million views. He has been featured as a cover story in both Acoustic Guitar Magazine in the U.S. and Acoustic Magazine in the UK. He also curates his own annual guitar retreat called Musicarium. McKee’s tour dates have taken him through Europe, Asia, Australia and North America, including tours with legendary acts from Dream Theater to Tommy Emmanuel.

47ae0612-6dfa-4190-a32d-19ce451ed214: We welcome the long-awaited return of a pair of master improvisers and long-term collaborators for a landmark evening of duets drawing on their two ECM Records albums, 2016’s A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke and their 2025 follow-up, Defiant Life. “One of the truly great jazz musicians of our time” (Stereophile), pianist and composer Vijay Iyer stretches the boundaries of jazz but has long reached beyond the music’s vocabulary. He was the recipient of the MacArthur Foundation’s “Genius Grant” in 2013 and his current trio with bassist Linda May Han Oh and drummer Tyshawn Sorey is among the most acclaimed small groups in modern jazz. A lion of the avant-garde since his membership in Chicago’s AACM in the late 1960s, trumpeter and composer Wadada Leo Smith is in the midst of a spectacular late career creative burst. Over the past decade, the 2016 Doris Duke Artist Award-winner released nearly two-dozen albums, most notably 2012’s epic Pulitzer Prize finalist Ten Freedom Summers (Cuneiform), an orchestral four-disc project inspired by the civil rights movement. 2016’s A Cosmic Rhythm With Each Stroke took its title from a line in the diaries of Indian visual artist Nasreen Mohamed, and their follow-up for ECM, 2025’s Defiant Life, is devoted to the necessary resistance to state-sponsored violence, at home and abroad. Personnel: Vijay Iyer (piano, Fender Rhodes); Wadada Leo Smith (trumpet)

bb871799-ec1e-5a67-8065-8d9529f79631: In this luminous debut collection, wilderness guide Hannah Hindley weaves together natural history and personal stories across eighteen lyrical essays. Encounters with aquatic life—from remote desert canyons to Alaska’s glacier country—guide her through heartbreak, hope, and transformation, leaving readers with a renewed sense of wonder. A debut essay collection probing the multifaceted range of experiences, both common and unusual, that define human interaction with our wild and human-made worlds. In this luminous debut collection, wilderness guide Hannah Hindley explores small creatures, big landscapes, and the shimmering connections between aquatic life and the human experience. Across eighteen lyrical essays, Love and Other Fish weaves together meticulously researched natural history with deeply personal stories. Drawing on years of work on boats and coastlines, Hindley uses encounters with fish—from remote desert canyons to Alaska’s glacier country—as guides for navigating the depths of heartbreak, hope, and transformation. Rendered with a tenderness for both the wild planet and the human heart, Love and Other Fish will leave readers with a renewed sense of wonder at the world around them. “In describing Love and Other Fish, I could use words like wonder, heartbreak, astonishment, clarity, rumination, and understanding. But what I really want to say is just read this book. With its beautiful narratives and contemplations, Love and Other Fish explores the strangeness of human experience and the strangeness of looking back. How wonderful and immersive to be guided by such a wise and generous writer.”— Beth Nguyen, author of Owner of a Lonely Heart: A Memoir “Hannah Hindley is one of those rare writers whose generosity, knowledge, and lyricism take you on adventures of the heart and wilds while also making you feel right at home. Love and Other Fish swims among watery lives, including ours, with assurance, vulnerability, and wisdom. These essays are gorgeous.”— Christopher Cokinos, author of Still as Bright: An Illuminating History of the Moon from Antiquity to Tomorrow “These astonishing essays braid grief, science, and love so tenderly that the world itself feels newly textured—each fish, each memory, each bright moment asking us to pay better attention to what keeps us alive. Love and Other Fish moves with a deep tenderness—an attention to the overlooked and the nearly forgotten—and in doing so, builds a world where memory, love, and survival can swim and splash beside each other.”— Aimee Nezhukumatathil, author of World of Wonders: In Praise of Fireflies, Whale Sharks, and Other Astonishments Hannah Hindley is a wilderness guide and writer with words in Bay Nature , The Sun , The Rumpus , and more. She is the recipient of the Barry Lopez Prize in Nonfiction, the Thomas Wood Award in Journalism, the Ellen Meloy Desert Writers Award, the Bill Waller Award for Nonfiction, and the Waterston Desert Writing Prize, among other accolades. Her essays about birds are featured in In the Shadow of the Bridge (Heyday, 2026). Hannah graduated from Harvard with degrees in both English and Biology; her writing links those studies, exploring our human relationship with a changing planet. 69e8d434-c7d5-4eef-b673-9b5e7ee8cca1: A teenage girl uncovers the dark secrets of her Smoky Mountain town while searching for a missing classmate in this gripping coming-of-age mystery perfect for fans of Where the Crawdads Sing . Nestled in the foothills of the Smoky Mountains, Beulah has always seemed steady—rooted in tradition, shaped by generations, and slow to change. But in 1986, the ground has shifted, and no one feels that more than fifteen-year-old Barrett Childress Owens. Between her parents’ unraveling marriage and a school full of kids she can’t connect with, she feels invisible in her own hometown. When Lacy Gunderson, the captivating new girl everyone is curious about, suddenly vanishes, the town’s calm surface fractures. Search parties comb the woods. A police investigation begins. Rumors multiply. Families close ranks. And Barrett begins to sense how much the adults around her choose not to say. As Beulah clings to its usual rituals—including the annual Miss Kudzu pageant, which has shaped local girlhood for decades—Barrett is forced to navigate a community where loss lingers in the air and secrets are carefully kept. Her journey through the uncertainty reshapes her understanding of friendships, family, and the complex place she calls home. A rich coming-of-age story with a pulse of mystery and a budding romance, What Happened in Beulah explores the fault lines of a small town and the courage it takes to face the truths people would rather bury. Christy Scott Cashman is a mother, author, and active member of the literary and arts communities. She serves on the boards of directors of the Associates of the Boston Public Library and the American Film Institute and is the founder of YouthINK, a nonprofit mentorship program for young artists in the United States and Ireland. 2c5e2195-fda1-5bfd-af88-2b232fce62cd: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. b6561565-c93e-4528-ade6-0fe82c9f8c0b: Join us for the Invention of Solitude Fiction Book Club. This month we will be discussing the novel, Taiwan Travelogue by Yang Shuang-Zi. About the book: WINNER OF THE 2024 NATIONAL BOOK AWARD FOR TRANSLATED LITERATURE WINNER OF THE 2026 INTERNATIONAL BOOKER PRIZE A bittersweet story of love between two women, nested in an artful exploration of language, history, and power May 1938. The young novelist Aoyama Chizuko has sailed from her home in Nagasaki, Japan, and arrived in Taiwan. She's been invited there by the Japanese government ruling the island, though she has no interest in their official banquets or imperialist agenda. Instead, Chizuko longs to experience real island life and to taste as much of its authentic cuisine as her famously monstrous appetite can bear. Soon a Taiwanese woman-who is younger even than she is, and who shares the characters of her name-is hired as her interpreter and makes her dreams come true. The charming, erudite, meticulous Chizuru arranges Chizuko's travels all over the Land of the South and also proves to be an exceptional cook. Over scenic train rides and braised pork rice, lively banter and winter melon tea, Chizuko grows infatuated with her companion and intent on drawing her closer. But something causes Chizuru to keep her distance. It's only after a heartbreaking separation that Chizuko begins to grasp what the "something" is. Disguised as a translation of a rediscovered text by a Japanese writer, this novel was a sensation on its first publication in Mandarin Chinese in 2020 and won Taiwan's highest literary honor, the Golden Tripod Award. Taiwan Travelogue unburies lost colonial histories and deftly reveals how power dynamics inflect our most intimate relationships.

a5dd8734-64b8-5d14-a821-3e5d84700132: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

93b65d2c-1975-568f-adf5-15d50d32ce13: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. 02655840-f141-45b8-ae94-da45ae825d75: Trumpeter, composer, and SFJAZZ Executive Artistic Director Terence Blanchard kicks off the new year with this residency showcasing an exclusive program of music. A savvy bandleader, celebrated film composer, brilliant jazz writer, and influential educator, the GRAMMY-winning New Orleans native is a major creative force in the modern jazz scene. A prodigious trumpeter, he cut his teeth as a member of drummer Art Blakey’s iconic ensemble The Jazz Messengers and has risen to become one of the most in-demand collaborators in jazz. Blanchard was appointed SFJAZZ Executive Artistic Director in 2023 and was named an NEA Jazz Master in 2024. Personnel: Eliane Elias (piano, vocals); Others TBA

ac58152c-9287-512f-9a8f-875a72f98fc4: We are thrilled to have Mike Chen back at Books Inc. Palo Alto, for the launch party of his new book The Haunting of Santo Domingo Street, a supernatural horror novel set in San Jose! Mike will be in conversation with fellow Bay Area author Yangsze Choo. This event will feature a conversation between these two writers, a reading from the novel, and an audience Q&A so you can have your burning questions answered. More about the book: In this eerie supernatural horror novel, two cousins must decide the fate of their childhood home—but the building has other plans. When Rosella Li and her estranged cousin, Gabe, inherit the last crumbling Victorian in a downtown San Jose block, developers hope to finish their gentrification push. Rosella is happy to see it go—her father, Ming, always cared more for the building and its tenants than her—but Gabe wants to cling on, mourning both his childhood home and the man who quietly raised him. Despite their squabbling, the choice may not be theirs; 43 Santo Domingo Street won’t be relinquished so easily. Indeed, when the cousins arrive to sign it away, they unearth boxes buried in its walls, revealing the desperate history Ming hid for decades, including what really happened to Rosella’s mother. Then, as bulldozers circle, a malevolence makes itself known. Soon, the lies that spanned family and cultures finally surface and, with them, spirits hellbent on one thing: No one leaves Santo Domingo Street. New York Times –bestselling author Mike Chen’s The Haunting of Santo Domingo Street is a chilling exploration of the consequences of erasing the past that will have readers grappling with the cost of not only progress . . . but also forgetting. “Poignant and timely yet terrifying, The Haunting of Santo Domingo Street is that rare haunted house story that reaches beyond brick and mortar, beyond heart and soul, to explore the echoes of trauma baked into the immigrant experience and the ways adults continue to be trapped by the pain of childhood.” —Delilah S. Dawson, New York Times –bestselling author of The Violence and Bloom “The most terrifying type of haunting is one a family inflicts on itself. Mike Chen’s ghost story is crafted with buried records and a melody a daughter has been singing her entire life. A tender but devastating story about the specters we inherit. Beautiful, luminous, and deeply heartbreaking.” —Cynthia Pelayo, Bram Stoker Award–winning author of Something Followed Us Home “An extraordinary tale of a haunted family in a haunted building and their struggles to make peace with their past while making space for themselves in a country that wasn’t always welcoming. This isn’t just another ghost story; it’s a story of immigrants who’ve seen their neighborhood stripped for parts by gentrification, and before the last building comes down for good, its grieving owners must decide what to carry away—and what to leave behind.” —Cherie Priest, award-winning author of The Drowning House “Delivers all the uncanniness of a classic haunted house story while layering family tension, generational trauma, and emotional insight. Mike Chen shines as he unpacks fraught relationships and unspools a ghostly mystery.” —Rowenna Miller, author of The Fairy Bargains of Prospect Hill Mike Chen is the New York Times– bestselling author of the genre-defying novels Here and Now and Then , Light Years from Home , and A Quantum Love Story , among others. He has also published stories set in the worlds of Star Wars, Marvel, Star Trek, and Critical Role, and contributed to the award-winning middle-grade anthology You Are Here: Connecting Flights . His original work has been nominated for a Goodreads Choice Award, a Compton Crook Award, the British Science Fantasy Association Award for Best Novel, and a CALIBA Golden Poppy Award. Chen has been featured on NPR and in USA Today , the Washington Post , the San Francisco Chronicle , and Scientific American . He has also written about geek culture for websites such as Nerdist, the Mary Sue, and StarTrek.com , and in a previous life, he covered the NHL. He lives in the San Francisco Bay Area with his wife, daughter, and many rescue animals. Yangsze Choo is the New York Times bestselling author of The Ghost Bride (now a Netflix Original series) and The Night Tiger , a Reese’s Book Club Pick, and a Big Jubilee Read selection for Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee. She lives in California with her family and loves to eat and read (often at the same time). The Fox Wife and all previous novels would not have been possible without large quantities of dark chocolate.

af4a5429-56ca-5fb6-8828-200563e295af: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours prior to the event start.
2fcb8a6e-b10c-48fa-b9e5-f6d8890a6c9a: Sound Palette is an interdisciplinary performance initiative that emerged from two students’ artistic and academic exploration at Stanford. Harpist-composer Renée Qin and violinist Ania Filochowska create an evening where imagination becomes the catalyst for a multimedia experience co-created in real time with the audience. Through interactive works, including a custom water instrument that responds to touch, flashlights that influence sound and visuals, and spoken words that transform into real-time soundscapes and imagery, participants become creative collaborators. The program features original compositions by Qin, placing acoustic instruments as human witnesses that remind us technology can amplify our stories rather than replace them.

dc2cad41-1604-56d6-a3ac-ada5e7e95903: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

1a5bc248-3040-4d04-a1f2-2a3c4b01109d: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

583c3081-cd4d-5932-ba1d-3b016c3e21e1: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

5c63ef12-e509-4a6e-be47-81c2a3b76a6a: In January of 2024, local artist and author Dylan Miles was diagnosed with stage four appendix cancer. Though his prognosis was grim, Miles refused to give up and with the help of the Appendix Cancer Research Foundation he was able to receive a treatment called Cytoreduction Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC) which saved his life. Throughout the two difficult years from diagnosis through recovery Miles says that he made it through due to "community, movement, and art." Miles' 2026 memoir, My Not Chosen Adventure: A Medical Mystery and Love Story , is not just about his journey surviving cancer but also includes "rainbow squirrels and protective dragons." The book comes from Miles' "passion for open conversation about… hard stuff. And… a passion for joy and love and life." Miles will bring his unique, passionate perspective to the Main Library on Thursday, February 11th in conversation with our OPL librarian about the book and his journey. Following the conversation will be an audience Q&A and book signing. Please register to receive updates and reminders. Registration assists with planning; however, it does not guarantee a seat. Additionally, masks are encouraged and will be provided. Get accessibility information .

a662f8e5-8fed-55e1-93e7-bc81657e26c7: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. 5a96de14-f6a4-4652-9e8c-0f78f21f479c: It’s true that Berkeley-reared Charlie Hunter has long been a familiar presence on Bay Area stages. Even though he moved east decades ago and now resides in Greensboro, North Carolina, Hunter has maintained deep ties to his hometown. But the inveterately inventive 7-string guitar wizard has never presented anything quite like his trio with fellow guitar explorer Ella Feingold. Based in Western Massachusetts, she’s a pioneer of inverted tuning, which facilitates unexpected harmonic structures and voicings inaccessible in standard tuning. Inspired by the dauntingly prolific songwriter, jazz musician, and conceptual artist Chris Weisman, this approach shapes her signature sound—blending lush chord inversions, walking basslines, and expressive melodic phrasing, which makes Feingold a capaciously creative foil for Hunter. He’s hardly the only one seeking her out. She’s also been working with Meshell Ndegeocello, Bootsy Collins, and Erykah Badu (with whom she’s performed many times in the Bay Area). But it’s with Hunter that she’s defining her own musical identity. He’s carved out a major new role for himself over the past decade as a producer, and last year he released their debut album Different Strokes for Different Folks on his SideHustle label. Rooted in funk, jazz, soul and ambient textures, it’s a raw, spontaneous conversation between friends who find limitless new space to investigate deep in the pocket. Personnel: Charlie Hunter (guitar); Ella Feingold (guitar); TBA drums

bad8b19a-a98c-5e14-a62e-f947d2647497: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Deconstructing Yourself strives to encourage, inform, and inspire your meditation practice towards ongoing awakening. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours prior to the event start.
