1029f204-1d36-4131-bfba-b3d9b9403006: With a professional career spanning nearly seven decades, Mavis Staples is the greatest living gospel and soul singer — a five-time GRAMMY winner, a 2016 Kennedy Center honoree, a 1999 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, a Blues and Gospel Hall of Fame inductee, and recipient of the 2005 GRAMMY Lifetime Achievement Award whose soaring voice turned classic spirituals into joyous declarations of freedom. Born in Chicago, Staples made her professional debut at age 10 with her legendary family band, The Staple Singers, singing on timeless songs that became chart topping hits and indelible anthems of the Civil Rights Movement. Her unforgettable performances on a string of classics including “Uncloudy Day,” “Some Truth To Tell,” “Freedom Highway,” “Respect Yourself,” “Why Am I Treated So Bad,” “I’ll Take You There,” and “Let’s Do It Again” have all become intrinsic parts of the American cultural fabric. Staples has recorded 18 albums as a solo artist and led a career that includes a staggering number of highlights, from performing at John F. Kennedy’s inauguration and marching with Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. to collaborating with Bob Dylan, Prince, The Band, Wilco’s Jeff Tweedy, and countless others. Her newest ANTI Records release, 2025’s Sad and Beautiful World, is her fourteenth album and won GRAMMYs for Best American Roots Performance and Best Americana Performance, and includes material by the likes of Leonard Cohen, Curtis Mayfield, Gillian Welch, and Tom Waits. Staples received the SFJAZZ Lifetime Achievement Award at SFJAZZ Gala 2020. Personnel: Mavis Staples (vocals); Others TBA
6df18f9b-8f63-4e0d-871e-bdc6c49bf916: Ages 3.5 - 5 ABOUT WEBOP AT SFJAZZ We are thrilled to partner with our sister organization—Jazz at Lincoln Center—in launching the West Coast version of the acclaimed early childhood music education program, WeBop! The perfect preamble to our Family Matinee program and designed for youngsters between the ages 2-5 and their caregivers, WeBop at SFJAZZ is designed to introduce young children to jazz music and performance in a safe, welcoming and interactive setting. Classes are 45 minutes long and provide plenty of opportunities to learn, explore, and play. ABOUT THIS CLASS Musical activities for the Gumbo Group utilize dramatic play as a core learning element and provide opportunities for discovery and exploration through jazz. The multisensory nature of music—hearing, moving, touching, vocalizing—creates many entry points for children in this age group to be engaged and develop. They will learn to identify and repeat short musical patterns, explore important musical concepts—such as dynamics and tempo—through singing, listening, playing, and improvising with jazz tunes and stories.

9605d83a-a087-5dd2-8d29-d22df9a5a00c: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

0118993f-f15d-515a-9cb2-12f8e9b68ffa: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

Across eleven songs, @ balance darkness and wonder with striking confidence. The album moves effortlessly between haunting folk textures, progressive flourishes, indie-pop hooks, and moments of cinematic beauty. Highlights include the expansive title track “Autosmile,” the nostalgic earworm “I Know You Are (But What Am I Thinking),” and the intricately arranged “Punish My Mind,” each exploring themes of change, self-reflection, loss, and acceptance through lyrics that remain deliberately open-ended and deeply relatable. Equal parts mysterious, virtuosic, and playful, Autosmile showcases @ at their most fully realized—an adventurous partnership capable of looking backward and forward at once. It is an album of contrasts: beauty and pain, humor and gravity, intimacy and ambition. In the face of uncertainty, @ offer curiosity, connection, and the possibility of transformation. 24b53cee-5886-5b90-b4be-f4c700962d8e: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

c25749b9-76c5-503a-b4aa-303b57ccb10a: Deconstructing Yourself is a weekly drop-in guided meditation (approximately one hour) plus Q & A with Berkeley Alembic founding teacher Michael Taft. Deconstructing Yourself is all about sharing the life-changing force that is meditation. We extend beyond any particular religion or technique in order to welcome any and all who are interested. Meditations are archived on YouTube here: https://www.youtube.com/michaeltaft108 Please arrive 10 minutes early. We do not allow any late entries for this event. Alembic founding teacher Michael W. Taft is a maverick meditation teacher, bestselling author, and podcaster. As a mindfulness coach, he specializes in secular, science-based mindfulness training in retreats, groups, corporate settings, and one-on-one sessions. Michael is the author of several books, including the bestselling The Mindful Geek, Nondualism: A Brief History of a Timeless Concept, and Ego (which he co-authored), as well as the editor of such books as Hardwiring Happiness by Rick Hanson and The Science of Enlightenment by Shinzen Young. He has often taught meditation at Google, worked on curriculum development for SIYLI, and is currently core faculty at Wisdom Labs, in San Francisco. Michael is also a featured teacher on the Simple Habit app, and an official advisor to the Therapeutic Neuroscience Lab. He was previously editor-in-chief of Being Human, and was the long-time editorial director of Sounds True. From Zen temples in Japan to yogi caves in India, Michael has been meditating for over thirty five years and has extensive experience in both Buddhist Vipassana and Hindu Tantric practice. Michael is a senior facilitator in Shinzen Young’s Unified Mindfulness system, and is a teacher of meditation groups around the Bay Area. He currently lives in Oakland, California, and is founding editor of the iconoclastic mindfulness meditation blog and podcast Deconstructing Yourself. NO ONE TURNED AWAY FOR LACK OF FUNDS. 029d3fc2-3461-4daa-8e25-0a924a811944: 70th Birthday Celebration A six-time GRAMMY winner, Pultizer Prize finalist, and 2009 Guggenheim Fellow, pianist and composer Billy Childs is an iconic artist whose innovative work bridges the jazz tradition and contemporary chamber music. Instead, their compositions thrive on tension and release, balancing virtuosic complexity with infectious melodies and digitally inspired textures. Against the Fall of Night represents the clearest realization of Sungazer’s artistic philosophy to date. Across the album, shimmering synthesizers collide with explosive drumming, while intricate rhythmic modulations transform each track into an unpredictable sonic journey. By combining internet-age electronic aesthetics with improvisational sophistication, the band has carved out a singular identity that continues reshaping expectations for contemporary instrumental music. b7c756a0-2283-4faa-a978-c4a3fe83f0de: For his second night of the season, trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire performs with his long-term working quartet including pianist Sam Harris, bassist Harish Raghavan, and drummer Justin Brown — the group with which he made his first SFJAZZ appearance as a leader in 2011. To the jazz world, Akinmusire’s ascension from young Oakland-born trumpeter at Berkeley High School to one of the most important voices in jazz seemed shockingly brief. In truth, his trajectory has been a linear progression, starting in earnest with a touring opportunity from influential saxophonist and composer Steve Coleman while still in high school, and built on a foundation of study at the Manhattan School of Music and the Thelonious Monk Institute of Jazz at USC with Herbie Hancock, Wayne Shorter, and Terence Blanchard. After decamping to New York, Akinmusire built his résumé as a sideman with the likes of Vijay Iyer and Aaron Parks, and in 2007, won both the prestigious Carmine Caruso International Jazz Trumpet Solo Competition and the star-making Thelonious Monk International Trumpet Competition. Since then, the trumpeter has been a whirlwind of activity but has always returned to this quartet as home base, heard most recently on 2020’s GRAMMY-nominated On the Tender Spot of Every Calloused Moment. Personnel: Ambrose Akinmusire (trumpet); Sam Harris (piano); Harish Raghavan (bass); Justin Brown (drums)

1efc2001-db2c-48c7-ad50-8c015486e0c7: The GRAMMY-winning Jewish klezmer superstars celebrate 40 years of music with this performance of material from their new album, We Were Made For These Times — a powerful new body of work rooted in protest, hope, and resilience. Formed in New York’s East Village in 1986, the Klezmatics led the resurgence of the nearly forgotten klezmer tradition and contemporized it with an irreverent dose of punk rock attitude, and since their inception, have been one of most visible faces of today’s Yiddish culture. Enduring a number of personnel changes over the past two decades, the band has revolved around original members Lorin Sklamberg on lead vocals and accordion, trumpeter/keyboardist Frank London and bassist Paul Morrissett. They have collaborated with violin virtuoso Itzhak Perlman, Pulitzer Prize winner Tony Kushner and Israeli vocalist Chava Alberstein, and have released a dozen diverse albums, including the GRAMMY-winning Wonder Wheel, their first session that set previously unused Woody Guthrie lyrics to their own original material. The band would expand their integration of Guthrie’s words to new compositions on their Happy Joyous Hanukkah and Happier Joyous Hanukkah projects that have been an SFJAZZ holiday tradition for many years. Released on International Workers’ Day in 2026, We Were Made For These Times brings together Jewish, Black gospel, Latin American, Crimean Tatar, and avant-jazz voices, creating a shared musical language of solidarity for the world we are living in now. Personnel: Lorin Sklamberg (lead vocals, accordion, guitar, piano); Matt Derriau (kaval, clarinet, saxophone); Lisa Gutkin (violin, vocals); Frank London (trumpet, keyboards); Paul Morrissett (bass, tsimbl); Richie Barshay (percussion)
71852a01-dc19-5f75-9e29-d7e873214842: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

(1992). A successful bandleader for over 35 years, Green has released a string of fine records played on scores of dates with the likes of Etta Jones, Ralph Moore, and Milt Jackson. In 1993, the late great Oscar Peterson picked Green to receive Toronto’s Glenn Gould International Protégé Prize in Music and later recorded the dazzling Oscar & Benny album with him. More than a bass superstar, Christian McBride has become a commanding force in American culture as an eight-time GRAMMY Award-winning bandleader and recording artist. “One of the most prominent contemporary jazz drummers” (All Music Guide), Carl Allen was a protégé of the legendary Art Blakey and has amassed a staggering resume as a bandleader, sideman, and educator. f5ee7406-837c-4715-9b12-c689f218cb88: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

7fe6f62c-9dcb-586a-825e-dc7909790b73: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

70269a8a-baca-4487-857c-5419a71abd6e: The electrifying young vocalist brings her signature blend of jazz, traditional Latin folk, and modern pop to SFJAZZ. Weaned on the percussive sound of son jarocho while growing up in Veracruz, Lucía Gutierrez Rebolloso started performing in her family’s ensemble before enrolling in grade school. She’s carried her Mexican roots with her, but these days the Harlem-based vocalist, who records and performs under the single moniker Lucía, is one of the most sought-after young artists in jazz. Her 2022 victory at the prestigious Sarah Vaughan International Jazz Vocal Competition has fueled her rise. The first Mexican artist to win the event, she’s following in the ascending footsteps of previous winners Samara Joy (2019) and Jazzmeia Horn (2013). 2e3ffcb3-7c8c-5685-8b28-425e11263400: By midlife and beyond, the societal messages for women and non-binary people are clear: disappear or accept whatever life has wrought in their personal and creative lives. Two authors who span generations, Kate Farrell (Silent Generation) and Jordan Rosenfeld (Gen X), reject this notion completely. This workshop offers revised attitudes and innovative approaches to our writing and lives in midlife and beyond. Come prepared to discuss, write, and reframe how we think about creativity, feminine archetypes, and aging. Drawing on mythology, literary examples, personal stories, psychological research, and an exploration of the enduring power of feminine creativity (widely defined), Kate and Jordan crack open old ideas and lead participants in exercises to awaken our essential forces through challenging midlife transitions. You don’t have to be a writer, but come prepared to respond to thoughtful, playful prompts that ignite the power of your life's next chapter. Meet Your Instructors Jordan Rosenfeld is author of Writing Through the Pause: Mining Midlife for Powerful W riting , seven other books on the craft and process of writing including Make a Scene, How to Write a Page Turner , and The Sound of Story: Developing Voice and Tone in Writing , and three novels, with a fourth, Seeking Solace , publishing in ’28. Learn more at Jordanrosenfeld.net and jordanwritelife.substack.com. Kate Farrell is the author of Fairy Tale Heroine: Live and Write Her Journey, Story Power: Secrets to Creating, Crafting, and Telling Memorable Stories , and she founded Woven, an ongoing workshop platform using the framework of the heroine's journey for creative projects. Read more at woventales.net and katefarrell.net .

9b71ad94-6e21-4067-b531-26689a35d299: w/ BHP Jazz Big Band A versatile young vocalist and bandleader whose taste for classic jazz spans the 20s through the 40s, Stella Heath presents a special evening devoted to the life and music of the great Billie Holiday, accompanied by the BHP Big Band. Born in Novato and raised in Petaluma, Heath began singing at eight and was inspired by the Billie Holiday records in her mother’s collection. She spent the last two years of high school at Michigan’s prestigious Interlochen Arts Academy before acting studies in New York and a career as a working Shakespearean actor that took her from Florida to Beijing and all points in between. Upon returning to the Bay Area, Heath dove headlong into music, assembling a series of groups that would honor areas of early jazz that she wanted to explore and bring to audiences, from the Roma jazz of Django Reinhardt and the traditional jazz of the 1920s to the swing of the 30s and 40s and the Great American Songbook. For this night, Heath celebrates the legacy of Lady Day — particularly her collaborations with pianist Teddy Wilson in the 1930s — through music, storytelling, and visuals that immerse the listeners in the era, placing the songs in historical context that gives the timeless music a still deeper meaning. Heath released her album dedicated to Holiday, For Billie, in 2026. Personnel: Stella Heath (vocals); Others TBA

6a744e40-c7e4-4220-b844-d4f2854e6b01: A 2026 NEA Jazz Master, vocalist and composer Carmen Lundy is a bona fide giant in the music who first made her mark more than four decades ago and has led an incredibly influential career. Championed by jazz giants like Geri Allen, Billy Childs, Bobby Watson and Walter Bishop Jr., Lundy is a renaissance woman whose creativity knows no bounds. A brilliant songwriter with several contemporary standards to her credit (“These Things You Are to Me”), she’s an actress, painter, bandleader, arranger and composer with an extensive book of finely wrought original songs. On stage, she’s a riveting performer, utterly at ease and open to wherever the music needs to go. Already well-established on the New York scene in 1985 when Dr. Herb Wong’s Black Hawk label released her first album Good Morning Kiss, she’s recorded a stellar body of work since then for JVC, Arabesque and Justin Time (which reissued Good Morning Kiss in 2002). Lundy has been running her own label Afrasia since 2005’s Jazz and the New Songbook: Live at the Madrid, and her two most recent albums, 2019’s Modern Ancestors and 2022’s Fade to Black, were each nominated for a GRAMMY. b3c7788e-bcae-5f8a-93d7-896e75310215: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

72c0312a-065e-4ae0-81c3-b55ac42f649d: A restless explorer who has collaborated with master musicians of Mali, interpreted the cabaret of Kurt Weill, and embraced the hard bop of Horace Silver, 2017 NEA Jazz Master Dee Dee Bridgewater brings a powerful new program she calls We Exist!, accompanied by a stellar rhythm section including pianist Alexis Lombre, bassist Liany Mateo, and drummer Shirazette Tinnin. Since she first gained recognition in the early 1970s with the great Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra, Bridgewater has thrived wherever she’s landed, and this show stands as a revelatory statement of purpose. Built as a “rallying cry” that connects past and present struggles, the program reimagines songs of protest such as Nina Simone’s “Mississippi Goddam” and Roberta Flack’s “Trying Times,” tracing the ongoing fight for justice and equality. Taking a cue from drummer and activist Max Roach’s landmark 1961 protest album We Insist!: Freedom Now Suite, the project confronts issues of racial oppression and civil rights while also championing female empowerment in a historically male-dominated jazz world. Bridgewater reinforces this message through an all-female ensemble, transforming the band itself into a living symbol of representation and change. It is a celebration of resilience, a platform for women in jazz, and a reminder—delivered with power and elegance—that music can still be a force for cultural and social transformation. Personnel: Dee Dee Bridgewater (vocals); Alexis Lombre (piano); Liany Mateo (bass); Shirazette Tinnin (drums)
15ab3189-25ce-5686-9899-176674667b2c: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

07951b30-0b01-4123-b707-790045bb21cf: A restless explorer who has collaborated with master musicians of Mali, interpreted the cabaret of Kurt Weill, and embraced the hard bop of Horace Silver, 2017 NEA Jazz Master Dee Dee Bridgewater brings a powerful new program she calls We Exist!, accompanied by a stellar rhythm section including pianist Alexis Lombre, bassist Liany Mateo, and drummer Shirazette Tinnin. Since she first gained recognition in the early 1970s with the great Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra, Bridgewater has thrived wherever she’s landed, and this show stands as a revelatory statement of purpose. Built as a “rallying cry” that connects past and present struggles, the program reimagines songs of protest such as Nina Simone’s “Mississippi Goddam” and Roberta Flack’s “Trying Times,” tracing the ongoing fight for justice and equality. Taking a cue from drummer and activist Max Roach’s landmark 1961 protest album We Insist!: Freedom Now Suite, the project confronts issues of racial oppression and civil rights while also championing female empowerment in a historically male-dominated jazz world. Bridgewater reinforces this message through an all-female ensemble, transforming the band itself into a living symbol of representation and change. It is a celebration of resilience, a platform for women in jazz, and a reminder—delivered with power and elegance—that music can still be a force for cultural and social transformation. 06395a01-8dbc-5744-862c-13bed39b5720: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

e62838be-1a76-4a98-b3d0-bdd4e604d87a: “One of the strongest pianists of his generation” (DownBeat), SFJAZZ Collective pianist Edward Simon brings his latest and most expansive project to the stage. When Dogs Howl is an ambitious multidisciplinary project that blends jazz composition, Afro-Venezuelan percussion, dance, storytelling, and immersive video design into a unified performance experience. Created in collaboration with SFJAZZ and commissioned by the Creative Work Fund, the work centers on the journeys of Venezuelan refugees and migrants who travel thousands of miles across Latin America in search of safety, opportunity, and belonging. Simon combines a jazz big band with traditional South American instruments and percussion, creating a sound world that merges contemporary improvisation with Venezuelan rhythmic traditions. Rather than presenting migration as abstract politics, the project emphasizes lived emotional experiences: displacement, resilience, memory, and reinvention. Its unique strength lies in how music, projected visuals, and movement interact to create a cinematic narrative atmosphere. When Dogs Howl reflects Simon’s long-standing commitment to socially engaged jazz and cross-cultural collaboration and further elevates his status as a visionary artist whose creativity continually pushes beyond borders, genres, and restrictions. d4436786-b7b4-49a9-9082-0cb4cb8c4c96: The March installment of Terence Blanchard’s UpSwing series presents the Paris-based singer and songwriter Gabi Hartmann and the brother and sister duo of flutist Elena and keyboardist Samora Pinderhughes, highlighting the rising generation of jazz torchbearers. Gaby Hartmann is an acclaimed vocalist who elegantly blends pop, jazz, soul, and world music, who takes audiences on “an enticing musical voyage that echoes the bossa nova sounds of Brazil, the Afropop of Miriam Makeba and the cool jazz of Norah Jones” (Montreal Gazette). In 2025, Hartmann unveiled La Femme aux yeux de sel (The Woman with Eyes of Salt), an album steeped in intimacy. Flutist Elena rose through the SFJAZZ High School All-Stars program to become one of the most in-demand musicians in jazz, working with Ambrose Akinmusire, Herbie Hancock, Chief Adjuah, Childish Gambino, Esperanza Spalding, and Milton Nascimento. The award-winning pianist Samora Pinderhughes has ingeniously combined jazz, neo soul, and hip-gop, working with Common, Robert Glasper, Lalah Hathaway, and Sara Bareilles. His 2022 album Grief was listed among the best albums of the year by The New York Times and Bandcamp. The pair recorded their first album together, Catch 22, in 2005 when they were 9 and 13 years old.

c905d252-a87a-4237-899b-34f3238875d4: “One of the most studied (and copied) saxophonists on the planet” (DownBeat), SFJAZZ Collective musical director Chris Potter is undoubtedly one of jazz’s leading lights and a highly engaged student of history. His newest album project, Alive With Ghosts Today, is a stirring set of compositions that explores the power and poignancy of abolitionist John Brown’s life and his 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry that preceded the American Civil War. Joining him on the Edition Records album, and for this performance, is a decidedly off-kilter septet that Potter describes as “a slightly unruly village band” including master guitarist Bill Frisell and a lineup featuring violin, clarinet, trombone, bass, and drums. Drawing inspiration from gospel, blues, African music, and the wide vistas of Aaron Copland, Alive With Ghosts Today captures the spirit of the era during a period of deep fracture in the country, when the battle for slavery and freedom reached a boiling point that still resonates deeply within the collective American psyche. An omnivorous artist who has fronted multiple ensembles and collaborated with a staggering list of music's greatest names, Chris Potter again expands upon his remarkable output with Alive With Ghosts Today — a project he approaches with heart and soul. Of the project, Potter says, “It’s a story that holds the complexity and tragedy of America in one moment. It felt important to engage with it now.” Personnel: Chris Potter (tenor and soprano saxophone); Bill Frisell (guitar); Others TBA

444fd0d9-4b70-5dea-8c0d-3363552dc76a: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

b09eacb4-dec8-4268-83ad-c69075cd7779: “A griot for a new generation of West Africans” (BBC Radio), London-born kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh is a pioneer of the 21-string African lute. Her return marks her debut on the Miner stage with two nights of spellbinding musicianship. Jobarteh is the first female kora master to have emerged from an established family of West African griots, bucking a long-held hereditary tradition that restricted instruction on the instrument to males only. Starting as a prodigy, Jobarteh began studies with her brother, kora great Tunde Jegede, at age four and gave her first public performance on the instrument at London’s Jazz Café at five. She deeply immersed herself in western classical music studies at London’s Royal College of Music, touring the world with her brother’s acclaimed ACM Ensemble as a teen and sharing the stage with Toumani Diabaté, Oumou Sangaré, and the BBC Symphony Orchestra. She composed the score to the 2010 documentary The Motherland, and has done extensive work for film, lending her soaring soprano to the soundtracks of Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom, The First Grader, and The History Channel’s 2016 miniseries Roots. Her beguiling debut solo recording, Fasiya, showcased her skills as vocalist and multi-instrumentalist, and her follow-up for African Guild Records, Badinyaa Kumoo, was voted Best Album of 2022 by Songlines. Personnel: Sam Gendel (alto saxophone, guitar, electronics); Sam Wilkes (bass, guitar, electronics)

6f170421-2749-4f83-9879-4987c09db88d: October Theme: “Broadway and Show Tunes” There’s nothing that brings people together better than singing our favorite songs. It recalls summer nights around the campfire: someone strumming the guitar and all singing a mix of folk music, familiar songs we heard on the radio, and occasional new songs that someone shares. Nobody has to worry about whether you know the songs or can sing like a pro. This is our chance to share the joy of singing simply for the fun of it. Cary Sheldon is a singer, songwriter, and beloved Berkeley voice teacher with 30 years worth of grateful students. She has been playing and teaching in the Bay Area for the last 40 years. Her love for R & B music led her to be part of Zazu Pitts Memorial Orchestra in the 1980’s. Other affiliations include The Henry Kaiser Band, The Henriettas (a recreation of DeZurick sisters, a popular country music duo from the 1940’s), who appeared on Prairie Home Companion, and most recently her band DanceChant, a joyful community-inspired R&B band that encourages audience participation. She continues to be inspired by her love of singing in community. “Singing together with others is one of the greatest joys in my life.” Now in her 60’s, she returns to influences from her early life. Her grade school music teachers included John Langstaff, creator of the Christmas Revels, and the repertoire was based on the American folk tradition, including old English ballads, spirituals, freedom songs, and the popular folk and protest songs of the 1960’s. She hopes to inspire others to explore the depth of this material and rediscover the joy of community singing. Soprano Candace Johnson has led AMN’s Juneteenth Choral Celebration since its inception in 2020. The AMN community knows her through her commitment to the power of the Negro Spirituals tradition, but Candace has a deep connection to theater and to the music of the Broadway stage. A voice instructor at UC Berkeley for 17 years, in 2022 Candace also became the director of the University Gospel Choir. A lyric coloratura soprano, she crosses musical boundaries performing classical, jazz, musical theater, pop and gospel. She has sung on many stages, including Carnegie Hall and The Manhattan Center. Also a playwright and actress, Candace premiered her first one-woman show, Vox in a Box , in UC Berkeley’s Hertz Hall in 2018, which led to her becoming a resident solo artist at The Marsh theater (Berkeley/San Francisco). Candace has written and performed 5 full-length one-woman musicals. Her most recent show, Scat-ter Brain: The Music of ADHD , was commissioned by The Marsh in 2024 for its inaugural IFOYE festival of new works by women-identifying playwrights. Following an extended run, Scat-ter Brain was nominated by Broadway World SF for Best Solo Show of 2025. Please read our Health, Safety and COVID-19 Information Our commitment to our patrons

e4fcdeea-f399-5f90-a3d5-7eb19a7d3051: A group meditation/authentic relating practice that explores what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to each other Welcome to a twice-monthly drop-in Relatefulness practice with Josh Rosenberg and Daniel Ricciardelli. Relatefulness is an exploration of what is coming up in the present moment as we relate to the others in the group. It is a close friend of relational practices like Circling™, Authentic Relating, and T-Group, with slightly more emphasis on group interaction and flexibility in how to express what is arising in the present moment. This is a mixed-levels event. Beginners are welcome and will be supported with tools to aid their exploration. Advanced practitioners will be challenged to find the next edge of their practice. We cap attendance for the event at 15 people. If you want to be sure to be able to join, purchase your ticket in advance! What We’ll Explore Through paired, small group, and full group processes, we will practice: Noticing and naming the content of our experience, including: our emotions, body sensations, and present moment reactions to others in the group. Noticing and naming the context of our experience, including: our assumptions, the norms of the group, and projections onto one another and society. Revealing our experience to one another to help all of us see each other and our broader social reality more clearly. Leading the group in the direction we want to go. This is a practice where all participants are invited to notice their desires for the group and to practice directing the group by embodying the kinds of expression they want to see more of. Why Come? You may be looking to: Cultivate more authentic, nourishing relationships, where you can be yourself and stay connected. Take your insights about personal growth and explore them in an interpersonal context. Set clear, compassionate boundaries instead of repeating painful patterns This practice helps to develop skills that support all of the above. Also, it's fun! What Not to Expect This is not a therapy session or group healing experience, although healing can occur. It’s a group exploration of what is arising in the present moment. This naturally tends to bring out more truth and love in the group, but there is not a particular goal or endpoint we are trying to reach. Here’s what NOT to expect: A space free of conflict or triggers. When people are open about what's coming up in their experience, things can get edgy sometimes! We don’t view being triggered as inherently negative, but rather a natural part of the human experience that can be rich to explore. We aim for a space where safety grows from honesty and genuine care, not from avoiding interpersonal conflict. To support this, we will establish some boundaries up front, such as asking for explicit consent before making physical contact with others. No enforced hierarchy of emotions. Beauty, awkwardness, boredom, anger, and joy are all welcome. Each experience has worth, and none automatically justify themselves as more important. Expression without attunement. We value honest expression, and we also stay attentive to its impact on others. This is a space for mindful connection, not expression at any cost. Facilitators may pause or redirect moments that move away from relational presence. Other logistics and notes Participants enter the space at 6:30 and we close the doors for the event at 6:35. Please arrive on time! We hope to see you at a future event! Feel free to reach out to jhrosenberg [at] gmail [dot] com or dbricciardelli [at] gmail [dot] com if you have questions about whether this event is a fit for you. More about the facilitators Josh Rosenberg (he/him) is a certified facilitator through the Relateful Company training program. He has hosted and facilitated weekly relatefulness sessions for small groups for several years while continuing to grow his practice through retreats and regularly engaging other facilitators. Josh loves exploring what's honestly coming up in the present moment in a group of people, and the novelty and relief it tends to bring. When he's not leading relatefulness sessions or at work, you may find him loving the heck out of music, movies, and comedy, participating in Michael Taft's meditation courses, or passionately following the New York Jets football team despite its many flaws. In his day job, Josh is CEO at the Forecasting Research Institute, a nonprofit aiming to advance the science of forecasting and increase its policy-relevance. Daniel Ricciardelli (he/him) has hundreds of hours in relational awareness practices of various forms, and is a certified Relatefulness practitioner through the Relateful Company. He draws from a decade of experience guiding men’s circles, performance dance teams, applied AI research, and meditation. Some recent inspirations of his are Ego Development Theory, madhyamaka philosophy, and Brazilian zouk. He is known for his steady, compassionate presence and calibrated relational risk-taking. He works full-time at the intersection of mental health and AI as a machine learning researcher.

d0b96137-497c-48c2-afb6-f329b28ab63a: In recent years, the most vital, inclusive, and innovative jazz scene on earth has shifted east across the Atlantic to London, and the figure that stands atop this revolution is Shabaka (formerly known as Shabaka Hutchings). The former leader of the heralded conglomerations Sons of Kemet, Shabaka and the Ancestors, and The Comet is Coming, Shabaka returns to SFJAZZ with music from his 2026 release Of the Earth — an innovative and adventurous solo recording that marks both his return to the saxophone and his immersion into electronic beats and loops that has opened new worlds for exploration. A multi-faceted instrumentalist and composer whose influence has spread far beyond the U.K., the Birmingham-raised Hutchings spent the formative years of his youth in Barbados, an island rife with reminders of Britain’s colonial history, where the budding artist first picked up the saxophone and where the seeds of his creative aesthetic in the roots of the African diaspora were planted. Bristling with raw energy and deep spiritual power, Of the Earth was inspired by the solo producer-auteur approach of the late D’Angelo and points to Shabaka’s vision for his future relationship with the instrument, allowing him to fully embrace new sonic realms and chart new expressive paths, each marked by resonances from the ancient past while feeling resolutely of the moment. Personnel: Shabaka (tenor saxophone, flute, electronics)

778ffb7d-42fa-53e9-bd62-f87dcd3e41ed: Creative expression is a way to integrate phenomenon and visions experienced in altered states of consciousness, whether they be meditative or entheogenic in nature. From the very first forms of mark-making to the caves of Lascaux to the works of Pablo Amaringo and Alex Grey, humanity has sought to understand our internal landscapes through visual expression. Alligator Lizards in the Air: Healing and Integration through Creative Expression, is a once a month chance to bring these experiences to life through two dimensional mark making. Art mediums from paint to colored pencils, crayons to markers, will be available for everyone to use along with paper and canvas. Krisztina Lazar will be your visionary guide in creativity and will help you realize your experience before your eyes. No art background needed for this class. All you need is an open mind and a willingness to explore. No one turned away for lack of funds. If this applies to you, please email hello@berkeleyalembic.org at least 48 hours before the event start. Krisztina Lazar is a visionary artist primarily working in oil paint, watercolor and drawing. She is a Mische Technique lineage holder, a mixture of oil and egg tempera painting invented during the Dutch Renaissance and revolutionized by modern master, Ernst Fuchs. This technique creates an opalescent under painting that the colors are then glazed over, rendering each painting out of light rather than shadow, bringing the images to life with fractal clarity. Utilizing this transformative style that she learned from visionary pioneer, Brigid Marlin, her current body of work explores painting a hybrid of Mische and Alla Prima to render hyperealistic sacred art. With these two techniques combined, Krisztina creates images of Pop Shamanism, portals and visions that speak to today’s cultural climate of the occult, magic, fantasy, psychedelics, meditation, pop, nostalgia, and the environment movement. Originally from Cleveland, OH, she completed her BFA at Carnegie Mellon University in 2004 and her MFA graduate degree in 2011 at the San Francisco Art Institute New Genres department. Her paintings have been exhibited in group and solo shows throughout the United States and Europe, most notably at the H.R. Geiger museum in Gruyere, Switzerland. She teaches her unique styles of painting to many students in group and private settings. Her work has been featured in multiple articles, galleries and book publications. She currently lives and works in Northern California.

fd9e9f8c-8ea9-45fe-a846-0103a47edf73: Aga Khan Master Musicians is a collective spanning traditions from the Mediterranean to Asia. The lineup: Wu Man is a world-leading player on the pipa (Chinese lute), Syrian-born Basel Rajoub has developed an entirely new repertoire for the saxophone, Feras Charestan is a master of the qanun (Middle-Eastern zither), Yurdal Tokcan is an authority on oud (Turkish lute), and Uzbek Abbos Kosimov is a virtuoso on the doira (Uzbek frame drum). They are joined by two eminent French musicians: accordionist, singer, and composer Vincent Peirani—whose work spans jazz, contemporary music, and improvisation—and Vincent Ségal, a renowned cellist and bassist. Together they reveal a collection of jointly-created works inspired by ancient trade routes and enduring cross-cultural connections.

c9877b22-77d5-55cc-91be-052e8663f683: 5Rhythms® dance is a profound medicine, offering a dynamic movement map into the vast, unexplored wilderness between our head and feet. Each rhythm - Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical, and Stillness, is a gateway, a wisdom teacher guiding us toward greater presence, healing, and transformation. This event occurs every two weeks at the Alembic. In a Sweat Your Prayers®, we support your individual practice with the rhythms and your movement journey by dancing wave after wave with light guidance. People often leave feeling cleansed, grounded, more alive, and more connected to themselves and their deeper knowing. 5Rhythms® is for every body. Many have discovered that not having prior dance training is actually liberating! Bring your body temple and a willingness to be surprised by what's waiting to move in and through you. The dance will end around 12:15pm, followed by a closing circle until around 12:30-ish. We encourage spacious arrivals and unhurried departures. So plan your time generously: a little time to land, a little time to linger, and a little less rushing back into the busy world. This dance can be your mini-retreat for the week! Teacher Bio: Qibei is a 5Rhythms® teacher, mindfulness teacher, holistic healer, and Associate Marriage and Family Therapist, though no title could fully capture the many worlds she moves between. Her work bridges the clinical and the mystical, the tender and the fierce, the grounded intelligence of the body and the mystery of Spirit moving through human life. For over 20 years, alongside 5Rhythms®, her path has been richly shaped by Continuum Movement, Open Floor, somatic contemplative practice, and relational communication. Over time, these disciplines began weaving together into the way she listens, guides, and teaches. For Qibei, dance is medicine, prayer, and creative laboratory, a place where we can move beyond numbness, habitual defenses, and rigid identities we’ve learned to carry, and reconnect with our raw aliveness and deeper knowing. She believes embodied presence is what brings depth, vitality, connection, and magic into our lives. In her movement spaces, Qibei creates a trauma-sensitive and inclusive field for all bodies, inviting authentic expression and the dynamic interplay between body, heart, psyche, and spirit. Her music and facilitation are often described as exquisite, nourishing, and deeply transporting, guiding movers into inner landscapes they didn’t know they could reach. Qibei also facilitates women's circle and retreats. Learn more about her work at www.Qibei.be.

a32e2c19-e17f-470e-902b-ce1fdba27e91: w/ Melissa Aldana, Linda May Han Oh, & Jeff “Tain” Watts “The titan among us,” (DownBeat), GRAMMY Award-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano is one of the era’s definitive improvisers and bandleaders and brings a remarkable group of the most accomplished instrumentalists in jazz to SFJAZZ for these two nights. John Coltrane famously described his musical journey to fellow legend Wayne Shorter as “starting a sentence in the middle and then going to the beginning and the end of it at the same time…both directions at once." To help commemorate one of this season’s themes, celebrating the centennial of John Coltrane, Lovano presides over a staggering band of all-stars including saxophonist Melissa Aldana, bassist Linda May Han Oh, and drummer Jeff “Tain” Watts for a project he calls “Both Directions at Once.” Winner of the 2013 Thelonious Monk International Saxophone Competition, GRAMMY nominee Melissa Aldana was named to DownBeat’s “25 For the Future” list in 2016 and has released eight albums including 2026’s Filin. A veteran of work with Pay Metheny, Vijay Iyer, and Dave Douglas, Linda May Han Oh has released five albums and was voted Bassist of the Year by JazzTimes, Hothouse, and the Jazz Journalists Association. Among the most influential drummers in jazz history, Jeff “Tain” Watts is a powerhouse artist best known for his long-term work with Branford and Wynton Marsalis, Kenny Garrett, and his own incendiary releases. Personnel: Joe Lovano tenor & soprano saxophone; Melissa Aldana (tenor saxophone); Linda May Han Oh (bass); Jeff "Tain" Watts (drums); TBA piano

7adeea6a-e9f1-4151-9258-1e62155b3096: w/ Julian Lage, Asante Santi Debriano, and Will Calhoun An artist The Boston Globe accurately describes as “jazz royalty,” GRAMMY-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano showcases his latest ensemble for the second two nights of his 2026-27 Season residency — a masterful assemblage of virtuosos including guitar great Julian Lage, esteemed bassist Asante Santi Debriano, and Living Colour drummer Will Calhoun — performing music from Lovano’s new ECM Records release Paramount Quartet. Cutting his professional teeth with the bands of Woody Herman and Mel Lewis, Lovano is the most acclaimed saxophonist and composer in modern jazz, leading over 40 albums and forging long-term partnerships with John Scofield and Paul Motian and collaborating with artists ranging from Jim Hall and McCoy Tyner to Abbey Lincoln and Elvin Jones. The spark of the Paramount Quartet dates to a meeting with Debriano and Calhoun at a fundraiser for Puerto Rico hurricane relief in 2023 and adding Lage to the mix was a natural step, as the two had been talking about doing a project together for over two decades. Consisting of all original compositions and a loving version of Wayne Shorter’s “Lady Day,” the album is possessed of a singular magic. As Lovano himself puts it, “There's a lot of magic that just kind of unfolds as we play. And the more we play, the more magical it becomes." Personnel: Joe Lovano (tenor & soprano saxophone); Julian Lage (guitar); Asante Santi Debriano (bass); Will Calhoun (drums)

Performing initially in small venues, the group developed a distinctive approach that pairs formal presentation with playful musical exploration. aafe7f5e-a9a8-4629-a74c-d87a347f3886: w/ Julian Lage, Asante Santi Debriano, and Will Calhoun An artist The Boston Globe accurately describes as “jazz royalty,” GRAMMY-winning saxophonist Joe Lovano showcases his latest ensemble for the second two nights of his 2026-27 Season residency — a masterful assemblage of virtuosos including guitar great Julian Lage, esteemed bassist Asante Santi Debriano, and Living Colour drummer Will Calhoun — performing music from Lovano’s new ECM Records release Paramount Quartet. Cutting his professional teeth with the bands of Woody Herman and Mel Lewis, Lovano is the most acclaimed saxophonist and composer in modern jazz, leading over 40 albums and forging long-term partnerships with John Scofield and Paul Motian and collaborating with artists ranging from Jim Hall and McCoy Tyner to Abbey Lincoln and Elvin Jones. The spark of the Paramount Quartet dates to a meeting with Debriano and Calhoun at a fundraiser for Puerto Rico hurricane relief in 2023 and adding Lage to the mix was a natural step, as the two had been talking about doing a project together for over two decades. Consisting of all original compositions and a loving version of Wayne Shorter’s “Lady Day,” the album is possessed of a singular magic. As Lovano himself puts it, “There's a lot of magic that just kind of unfolds as we play. And the more we play, the more magical it becomes." Personnel: Joe Lovano (tenor & soprano saxophone); Julian Lage (guitar); Asante Santi Debriano (bass); Will Calhoun (drums)
